check: Section 1 completed and signed by the employee on/before the first day of employment for pay.
requirement: Employee completes and signs Section 1 (Employee Information and Attestation) at the time of hire = actual commencement of employment for wages. May be done after offer acceptance, never before. <3-business-day engagements: by day 1.
trigger: New employee (hired after Nov 6, 1986) begins employment for wages.
threshold: By end of business on day 1 (first day worked for pay); not before offer acceptance.
deadline: First day of employment (hire date). No grace.
severityPenalty: Substantive if Section 1 is not timely attested on the hire date under the current ICE I-9 Inspection fact sheet. Civil penalty $288–$2,861/individual (2025, in force through CY2026).
citation: Regulatory hook **8 CFR 274a.2(b)(1)(i)(A)** ("Completes section 1 … at the time of hire and signs the attestation") + **8 CFR 274a.1** (definition of "hire" = "the actual commencement of employment … for wages or other remuneration"). The "first day of employment / after offer / not before offer" gloss is **USCIS M-274 §3.0 / Form I-9 Instructions**, not the CFR. Penalty **8 CFR 274a.10(b)(2)** / **8 USC 1324a(e)(5)**. *(Original cited 274a.2(b)(1)(i)(A); 274a.2(b)(1)(ii); penalty cites — the (b)(1)(ii) and the "<3 business days" clauses were dropped as they govern Section 2, not Section 1.)*
dataNeeded: employeeId; hireDate (first day of employment for pay); section1CompletedDate; section1SignedFlag; section1SignDate; offerAcceptedDate.
implementationNote: Deterministic: flag if section1SignDate null OR > hireDate. Flag section1SignDate < offerAcceptanceDate when captured. Date-only comparison. Rehires within 3 yrs may reuse a prior I-9 via 274a.2(c) — suppress for rehires electing update-and-reverify. Borderline late/defective Section 1 (technical vs substantive) → NEEDS-COUNSEL.

check: Employee checked exactly one of the four citizenship/immigration-status attestation boxes in Section 1.
requirement: Employee attests to exactly one of: (1) U.S. citizen; (2) noncitizen national; (3) LPR (with A-number/USCIS number); (4) noncitizen authorized to work (with work-auth expiry if applicable + A-number/USCIS number, I-94 number, or foreign passport number).
trigger: Any Form I-9 Section 1.
threshold: Exactly one of four boxes; zero or multiple = defect.
deadline: At Section 1 completion (day 1).
severityPenalty: Substantive under the current ICE I-9 Inspection fact sheet; no technical cure. $288–$2,861/form.
citation: The four-box "check exactly one" rule lives on the **Form I-9 (ed. 01/20/25)** + **USCIS Form I-9 Instructions (01/20/25)** + **M-274 §3.0** — NOT in the reg. Regulatory duty to complete Section 1 + sign: **8 CFR 274a.2(b)(1)(i)(A)**. Substantive/non-curable classification: **ICE Form I-9 Inspection fact sheet updated 2026-03-16**. Penalty **8 CFR 274a.10(b)(2)**. *(Original implied (b)(1)(i)(A) enumerated the four boxes; it does not.)*
dataNeeded: section1StatusAttested enum (citizen|national|lpr|alien_authorized|none); boxesCheckedCount; for LPR: aNumber; for alien_authorized: workAuthExpiry + one of (aNumber|i94|foreignPassport).
implementationNote: Deterministic: flag statusAttested==none OR boxesChecked != 1. Conditional sub-checks: LPR ⇒ aNumber required; alien_authorized ⇒ (workAuthExpiry present unless N/A) AND ≥1 identifier. Flag (don't auto-fail) when an identifier field is ambiguous/mis-keyed.

check: Section 1 attestation signed AND dated by the employee.
requirement: Employee signs and dates the Section 1 attestation under penalty of perjury. Preparer/translator who assisted completes Supplement A.
trigger: Any Form I-9 Section 1.
threshold: Employee signature present AND date present.
deadline: Day 1 of employment ("at the time of hire").
severityPenalty: Missing **signature** or **date** = substantive under the current ICE I-9 Inspection fact sheet; no technical cure. $288–$2,861.
citation: **8 CFR 274a.2(b)(1)(i)(A)** (completes Section 1 "at the time of hire" and signs the attestation; preparer/translator assistance clause is in this same subparagraph) + **8 CFR 274a.2(a)(3)** (attestation "under penalty of perjury"). Deadline = "at the time of hire" per **8 CFR 274a.1(g)**, operationally end of first day per M-274. The DATE-field requirement derives from the **Form I-9 instructions / M-274**, not the reg. **DROP 8 CFR 274a.2(b)(2)** (that is the retention rule) and **DROP the Virtue Memo as authority for the signature mandate** (it governs the technical-vs-substantive classification only). Preparer/Translator = **Supplement A** (current Form I-9, 08/01/2023).
dataNeeded: section1SignaturePresent (bool); section1SignDate.
implementationNote: Deterministic: missing signature OR missing Section 1 date → substantive flag. Keep signature and date as separate field defects for remediation/evidence, but do not mark the missing-date defect technical/curable under the current ICE fact sheet.

check: Employer used a Form I-9 edition that was current/accepted when any part of the form was initially completed.
requirement: Failure to use a version of Form I-9 that is current at the time any part of the form is initially completed is a technical/procedural failure under the ICE I-9 Inspection fact sheet. If ICE serves a Notice of Technical or Procedural Failures, the employer receives at least 10 business days to correct; uncorrected technical failures become substantive.
trigger: Any Form I-9 initial completion or correction/reverification event where the form edition can be read.
threshold: `formEditionDate` must be in the USCIS accepted-editions table on the initial completion date. If no edition date can be extracted, return `insufficient_evidence`, not compliant.
deadline: At initial Form I-9 completion; cure clock only starts if ICE issues a technical/procedural-failure notice.
severityPenalty: Technical/procedural at notice stage; uncorrected after the ICE cure period becomes substantive and penalty-bearing.
citation: ICE Form I-9 Inspection fact sheet updated 2026-03-16 (technical failures list); current form/edition source = USCIS Form I-9 page + M-274; cure period = 8 USC 1324a(b)(6).
dataNeeded: formEditionDate; initialCompletionDate; acceptedI9EditionTable with effective/expiration dates; correctionDate if later cured.
implementationNote: Deterministic table lookup: acceptedI9EditionTable.includes(formEditionDate, initialCompletionDate). Treat wrong/obsolete edition as technical/procedural until the ICE cure window expires. Do not confuse this with stale document-list values; the DOC_CATALOG handles document acceptability by form edition.

check: Preparer/translator certification (Supplement A) completed when someone assisted the employee with Section 1.
requirement: Each assisting preparer/translator completes a separate Preparer and/or Translator Certification block in Supplement A, signs and dates it. Employee must still personally sign Section 1.
trigger: A preparer/translator helped complete Section 1.
threshold: Supplement A present and signed for each assisting preparer/translator.
deadline: Same time as Section 1 (day 1).
severityPenalty: Section-1 attestation defect; typically technical/procedural if mechanics-only, can be substantive if it undermines the attestation. Within $288–$2,861 paperwork range. NEEDS-COUNSEL on substantiveness in a given fact pattern.
citation: 8 CFR 274a.2(b)(1)(i)(A); M-274 Supplement A guidance. *(Verified verbatim against M-274 and the reg — confirmed.)*
dataNeeded: preparerUsed (bool, often not captured); supplementAPresent (bool); supplementASignature + date.
implementationNote: Hard to evaluate mechanically — "was a preparer used" is rarely structured. If preparerUsed==true and Supplement A missing → flag. If preparerUsed unknown → surface as a data-gap note, NOT a violation. NEEDS-COUNSEL on whether a missing Supplement A is substantive.

check: Section 2 completed within 3 business days of the first day of employment.
requirement: Within 3 business days of hire, employer (or authorized rep) physically examines documents and completes Section 2. <3-business-day engagements: Section 2 at time of hire (day 1).
trigger: New employee begins employment for pay.
threshold: 3 business days; first day of employment = day 0, due by end of 3rd business day after. Weekends + federal holidays excluded.
deadline: End of the 3rd business day after the first day of employment.
severityPenalty: Substantive if missing/untimely. $288–$2,861/form, five-factor.
citation: 8 CFR 274a.2(b)(1)(ii); short-engagement exception 8 CFR 274a.2(b)(1)(iii); penalty 8 CFR 274a.10(b)(2). *(All three verified verbatim — confirmed; "hire" defined at 274a.1(c) = first day for pay.)*
dataNeeded: hire/start date; section2CompletionDate (employer sign date); businessDayCalendar (federal holidays); employmentDurationDays.
implementationNote: Deterministic with a business-day calendar. Flag businessDaysBetween(hireDate, section2Date) > 3, or section2Date null. Use the current form's "first day of employment" field to drive the clock, not the form-completion date. Re-hires use rehire date. Exactly-3 borderline cases → flag for review (ICE resolves slightly in employer's favor).

check: Employer physically (or via authorized remote alternative) examined original documents that reasonably appear genuine and relate to the person.
requirement: Examine original document(s) (or copies + live video under the DHS remote alternative for qualified E-Verify employers); ensure they reasonably appear genuine and relate to the individual. Employee — not employer — chooses List A vs List B+C.
trigger: Section 2 completion.
threshold: One List A doc, OR one List B (identity) + one List C (employment auth). Reasonable-appearance standard.
deadline: Within 3 business days of hire.
severityPenalty: Substantive if no acceptable docs / improper docs. Knowingly accepting fraudulent docs → knowing-hire ($716–$28,619 tiers) + criminal exposure. Genuineness/relate-to judgment → NEEDS-COUNSEL.
citation: 8 CFR 274a.2(b)(1)(ii)(A); 8 CFR 274a.2(b)(1)(v); remote alt 88 FR 47990 (publ. **July 25, 2023**; eff. Aug 1, 2023) / M-274 §4.5. Optional precision: cite **274a.2(b)(1)(ix)** (remote-alternative authority) and **274a.2(a)(2) / INA 274B (8 USC 1324b)** (employee-choice / anti-over-documentation). *(Confirmed — (b)(1)(v) carries the List A XOR List B+C structure verbatim.)*
dataNeeded: listA docs OR (listB + listC); per doc: title, issuing authority, number, expiration; remoteAlternativeUsed (bool); copiesRetained (bool, required if remote).
implementationNote: Mechanical: validate the recorded combination is structurally valid (exactly one List A, or exactly one B + one C; never B alone, never B+A). "Reasonably appears genuine / relates" = human judgment → NEEDS-COUNSEL. Auto-check no over-documentation pattern (A + B + C all recorded) — see overdocumentation rule.

check: Section 2 records document title, issuing authority, document number, expiration date per document, plus the employee's first day of employment.
requirement: Record for each document: title, issuing authority, number, expiration (if any); record first day of employment; sign and date the employer attestation with business name/address.
trigger: Section 2 completion.
threshold: All required fields populated; employer signature + date + business name/address.
deadline: Within 3 business days of hire.
severityPenalty: Substantive under the current ICE I-9 Inspection fact sheet when document title, issuing authority, document number, and/or expiration date is missing. The retained-copy carveout no longer controls severity. $288–$2,861.
citation: **8 CFR 274a.2(b)(1)(ii)** (within 3 business days; physically examine; complete Section 2 + sign) AND **8 CFR 274a.2(b)(1)(v)** ("The identification number and expiration date … of all documents must be noted … on the Form I-9"). **Document title and issuing authority fields derive from the Form I-9 itself / M-274**, not the CFR text. Penalty **8 CFR 274a.10(b)(2)**. *(Original cited (b)(1)(ii)(A)-(B) — there is no (b)(1)(ii)(C)/(D); the recording mandate is (b)(1)(v).)*
dataNeeded: per doc: title, issuingAuthority, number, expiration (nullable for non-expiring docs); section2EmployerSignature + date; businessName; businessAddress; firstDayOfEmployment; copiesRetainedEvidenceFlag (evidence only, not severity-changing).
implementationNote: Deterministic field-presence; missing title/issuing authority/number/required expiration is substantive regardless of retained copies under the current ICE fact sheet. Null expiry is legitimate for non-expiring docs (unrestricted SSN card, U.S. birth certificate) — maintain a lookup; don't flag those.

check: Employer signed and dated the Section 2 attestation.
requirement: Employer/authorized rep signs and dates Section 2, certifying under penalty of perjury that it examined the documents and they appear genuine and relate to the employee.
trigger: Section 2 completion.
threshold: Employer signature present AND date present.
deadline: Within 3 business days of hire.
severityPenalty: Missing employer **signature** or **date** = substantive under the current ICE I-9 Inspection fact sheet. Do not backdate corrections; enter current date + initials/annotation. $288–$2,861.
citation: 8 CFR 274a.2(b)(1)(ii); ICE Form I-9 Inspection fact sheet updated 2026-03-16; penalty 8 CFR 274a.10(b)(2). *(Prior Virtue/Interim-Guideline treatment of missing dates as technical is stale.)*
dataNeeded: section2EmployerSignaturePresent (bool); section2EmployerSignDate.
implementationNote: Deterministic: missing signature OR missing Section 2 certification date → substantive. Keep signature and date as separate field defects for remediation/evidence.

check: Reverification (Supplement B) completed on/before the date the employee's temporary work authorization expires.
requirement: When recorded employment authorization (or the document evidencing it) has an expiration date, reverify continued authorization in Supplement B no later than the expiry, examining a List A or List C doc the employee chooses.
trigger: Employee recorded with time-limited employment authorization / expiring work-auth document.
threshold: Reverification recorded on/before the work-authorization expiration date.
deadline: By the expiry date of the employment authorization.
severityPenalty: Substantive — continuing to employ after lapse without timely reverification → knowing-continued-employment ($716–$28,619 tiers) + paperwork ($288–$2,861).
citation: **8 CFR 274a.2(b)(1)(vii)**; paperwork penalty **8 CFR 274a.10(b)(2)**; knowing-continued-employment penalty **8 CFR 274a.10(b)(1)** (use **(b)(1)(i)** for first-offense tier — (b)(1)(ii) is the *second*-offense tier, $5,724–$14,308). *(Original cited (b)(1)(ii) generically.)*
dataNeeded: workAuthExpiry; reverificationDate (Supplement B); reverifiedDocType; current employment status.
implementationNote: Deterministic: if workAuthExpiry not null AND active AND (reverificationDate null OR > workAuthExpiry) → flag. **CRITICAL guard:** do NOT fire while an EAD auto-extension is active — if an I-766 was presented with an I-797C auto-extension, the deadline is the END of the auto-extended period (274a.2(b)(1)(vii)/274a.13(d)), not the card face date; otherwise false positive. Suppress for non-reverifiable docs (US passport, US passport card, Form I-551/green card, List B). Auto-extension eligibility ambiguity → NEEDS-COUNSEL.

check: Employer did NOT improperly reverify documents/persons on the no-reverify list.
requirement: Never reverify on expiry of: U.S. passport, U.S. passport card, Form I-551 (green card); never reverify List B (identity-only) docs; never reverify U.S. citizens/noncitizen nationals/LPRs. Demanding such reverification can be unlawful document abuse.
trigger: Any employee whose recorded doc/status is in the no-reverify set, esp. where software auto-schedules off a printed expiry.
threshold: No reverification demanded based on expiry of US passport/passport card/Form I-551, a List B doc, or for a US citizen/national/LPR.
deadline: n/a (prohibition).
severityPenalty: Improper reverification / requesting more-or-different docs = unfair documentary practice 8 USC 1324b(a)(6): **$236–$2,364/individual** (2025), **intent to discriminate required**.
citation: 8 CFR 274a.2(b)(1)(vii); M-274 §6.0 (Supplement B) & §7.1 (LPRs); 8 USC 1324b(a)(6); 28 CFR 44.200. *(All five confirmed; the no-reverify LIST is M-274 policy, correctly attributed; reg cite supplies only the reverification trigger.)*
dataNeeded: recorded Section-2 doc type; Section-1 status attested; reverification events + the doc type that triggered them.
implementationNote: Maintain NO_REVERIFY = {US passport, US passport card, Form I-551, any List B doc, status ∈ {US citizen, noncitizen national, LPR}}. Flag (a) any reverification keyed to a NO_REVERIFY expiry as over-reverification/document-abuse risk, and (b) ensure the timing rule suppresses these. Highest-value guard — reverification software frequently mis-fires on green-card expiry. Note: temporary I-551/I-94 ADIT stamp DOES require reverification (it's the *permanent* green card that does not). 1324b liability requires intent → NEEDS-COUNSEL.

check: Rehire handled correctly via Supplement B when rehiring within 3 years of original I-9 execution.
requirement: If rehired within 3 years of the date the original I-9 was executed, employer may either complete a new I-9 or complete Supplement B (recording rehire date and reverifying if prior authorization expired).
trigger: Rehire of a former employee.
threshold: Within 3 years of original I-9 → Supplement B permitted; beyond 3 years → new I-9 required.
deadline: By the rehire date (and within Section 2 / reverification timing if a new auth check is needed).
severityPenalty: Failure to re-establish authorization on rehire = substantive verification failure ($288–$2,861; potential knowing-employment exposure).
citation: **8 CFR 274a.2(c)(1)** (rehire within 3 years of initial I-9 execution; reverify expired authorization per (b)(1)(vii)); **USCIS M-274 §6.0 / §6.2**. **DROP the "(b)(1)(viii)-(ix)" pinpoint** — (b)(1)(viii) = continuing employment (leave/layoff/promotion); (b)(1)(ix) = alternative document-examination procedures; neither addresses rehire. *(Original cited (b)(1)(viii)-(ix) + (c)(1); only (c)(1) was correct.)*
dataNeeded: originalI9Date (= the Section-2 execution date); rehireDate; priorWorkAuthExpiry; whether new I-9 or Supplement B used on rehire.
implementationNote: Deterministic: rehireDate − originalI9Date ≤ 3 yrs → Supplement B acceptable (verify completed); else require a new I-9 (flag if only Supplement B used). Chain to reverification: priorWorkAuthExpiry < rehireDate ⇒ reverification/new authorization required. Anchor on the original I-9 execution date, NOT the rehire date.

check: Only currently-acceptable List A/B/C documents accepted in the correct combination.
requirement: Identity + employment authorization established only by docs on the current Lists of Acceptable Documents: List A = both; List B = identity only; List C = employment auth only. List A stands alone; otherwise one List B AND one List C. Don't ask for more from someone presenting an acceptable List A doc.
trigger: Any Section 2 / reverification document recording.
threshold: {one List A} XOR {one List B + one List C}; on current list; unexpired (except no-expiry docs).
deadline: At Section 2 / reverification.
severityPenalty: Listing improper documents = substantive ($288–$2,861). Over-documentation → 1324b document abuse ($236–$2,364).
citation: 8 CFR 274a.2(b)(1)(v); INA 274A(b)(1)(B)-(D) (8 USC 1324a(b)); M-274 §13.0–13.3. *(Confirmed verbatim; current web edition is §13.0–13.3 — older PDF edition numbers this 12.0–12.3.)*
dataNeeded: canonical DOC_CATALOG tagged List A/B/C with hasExpiry + acceptability window; per-form recorded doc types + numbers + expiries; reverification docs (List A or C only).
implementationNote: Deterministic with a maintained, versioned reference table keyed to the form edition in use on the completion date. Validate combination cardinality + list membership; flag expired docs (where hasExpiry) recorded as valid at completion. Reverification must use List A or List C only.

check: Receipt for a lost/stolen/damaged document handled within the receipt rule and replaced within 90 days.
requirement: Accept a receipt for the replacement application; employee presents the actual replacement within 90 days of hire (or, for reverification, within 90 days of the work-auth expiry). Receipt rule unavailable for <3-business-day engagements. Distinct arrival-document and refugee receipts have their own windows.
trigger: Employee presents a receipt instead of an actual List A/B/C document.
threshold: Replacement presented within 90 days of hire (or reverification trigger). Receipt rule unavailable for <3-day hires.
deadline: 90 days from hire (or reverification date).
severityPenalty: Overdue replacement, or receipt where not permitted, = substantive verification defect ($288–$2,861).
citation: **8 CFR 274a.2(b)(1)(vi)(A)** (lost/stolen/damaged receipt + 90-day replacement); short-term <3-day exception **8 CFR 274a.2(b)(1)(iii)** (also restated in (b)(1)(vi)); **distinct arrival-document and refugee receipts at 8 CFR 274a.2(b)(1)(vi)(B) and (b)(1)(vi)(C)** — NOT (b)(1)(iii); **M-274 §4.4**. *(Original sourced the arrival/refugee receipts implicitly to (b)(1)(iii); those live in (vi)(B)/(vi)(C).)*
dataNeeded: receiptUsed (bool); receiptType; hireDate (or reverification date); replacementDocPresentedDate; employmentDurationDays.
implementationNote: Deterministic: receiptUsed + replacementDocPresentedDate null + (today − hireDate) > 90 → overdue; employmentDurationDays < 3 + receiptUsed → flag (not allowed). The arrival/refugee receipts are NOT uniformly 90 days (temporary I-551 stamp runs to stamp expiry or 1 yr if undated; refugee I-94 = 90 days) → NEEDS-COUNSEL where receiptType is the refugee/arrival variant.

check: Form I-9 retained for the later of 3 years from hire OR 1 year from termination.
requirement: Retain each I-9 until the LATER of (a) 3 years after hire, or (b) 1 year after termination.
trigger: Any current/former employee with an I-9.
threshold: Retain until max(hireDate + 3y, terminationDate + 1y). Active employees: indefinitely.
deadline: Earliest destruction date = max(hire+3y, term+1y).
severityPenalty: Failure to retain/produce = substantive (presentation failure) — $288–$2,861/missing form.
citation: 8 CFR 274a.2(b)(2)(i)(A); 8 USC 1324a(b)(3); penalty 8 CFR 274a.10(b)(2). *(Confirmed verbatim — (A) is the employer max() rule; (B) is the recruiter/referrer case.)*
dataNeeded: hireDate; terminationDate (nullable); i9OnFile (bool); destructionDate if purged.
implementationNote: Deterministic: requiredRetentionUntil = max(hire+3y, (term ? term+1y : +∞)). Flag i9OnFile==false where requiredRetentionUntil ≥ today, or a form destroyed before requiredRetentionUntil. The 1-year-post-termination prong starts only on a real termination — leaves of absence are not terminations.

check: I-9s stored in a compliant medium and producible within 3 business days of an inspection request.
requirement: Retain on paper (original signatures), microfilm/microfiche (reader-printer at exam site), or electronically (access controls, backup/recovery, training, secure-permanent-record audit trail on create/complete/update/modify/alter/correct). Produce within 3 business days of an inspection request.
trigger: Ongoing storage; an inspection / NOI.
threshold: Production within 3 business days; electronic systems meet the security/audit-trail standard.
deadline: 3 business days after NOI / inspection request.
severityPenalty: Inability to produce = failure to present ($288–$2,861/form). Deficient electronic storage undermines admissibility.
citation: **8 CFR 274a.2(b)(2)(i)-(ii)** (retention period + 3-business-days inspection notice / production-at-location) — *not* (b)(3), which is "Copying of documentation"; **8 CFR 274a.2(e)-(g)** (electronic retention standards: (e) controls/indexing, (f) documentation/audit trails, (g) security incl. (g)(1)(iv) secure-permanent-record-on-create/complete/update/modify/alter/correct); **M-274 §10.0–10.1** ("present within 3 business days of the date requested"). *(Original cited (b)(3); the "produce within 3 business days of request" obligation is M-274/ICE practice — the CFR's literal "3 business days" is the notice-before-inspection clock in (b)(2)(ii).)*
dataNeeded: storageMedium (paper|microfilm|electronic); for electronic: accessControls, backup, auditTrail, tamperEvident (bools); inspectionProducibility / time-to-produce.
implementationNote: Partly programmatic (assert electronic system HAS audit trail + access controls + backup as config booleans; flag any false), partly operational (3-business-day production = system-level control attestation). Whether a vendor's audit trail meets 8 CFR 274a.2(e) → NEEDS-COUNSEL.

check: Corrections by line-through + initial + date; no white-out, no backdating; written explanation; correct party corrects each section.
requirement: Draw a single line through the error, enter correct info, initial and date. Never erase/white-out. Never backdate (enter current date + initial). Attach a dated written explanation (signature recommended). Employee corrects Section 1; employer corrects Section 2.
trigger: Any correction to an existing I-9 (e.g., self-audit).
threshold: Line-through + initials + correction date; no white-out; no backdated entries; explanation attached.
deadline: n/a (governs how, not when).
severityPenalty: Improper corrections (backdating, white-out, wrong-party) can convert a curable defect into substantive and support fraud allegations. Concealment-looking alteration → NEEDS-COUNSEL.
citation: **M-274 §9.0 (Correcting Errors or Missing Information on Form I-9)** — the governing source; optionally **Form I-9 Instructions**. **DROP "8 CFR 274a.2(b)(2) (integrity of the record)"** — (b)(2) is the retention rule; no paragraph of 274a.2 prescribes manual line-through/initial/date corrections (that procedure exists only in M-274 §9.0). *(One overstatement softened: the written explanation need not be "signed, dated" per M-274 — signing is best practice.)*
dataNeeded: correctionEvents: field changed, who corrected, correctionDate vs originalDate, method (line-through|whiteout|overwrite), explanationAttached (bool).
implementationNote: Hard from structured data alone (white-out is visual). Where correction metadata exists: flag correctionDate < originalEventDate (backdating), Section-1-by-employer or Section-2-by-employee (wrong party), or method==whiteout. Digital systems with audit trails → fully deterministic; scanned paper → human/visual review (NEEDS-COUNSEL).

check: Remote (alternative-procedure) exam used only by qualified E-Verify employers, with the box checked and copies retained.
requirement: Examine documents remotely only if enrolled in E-Verify in good standing (and, for the employee, created an E-Verify case except for reverification): examine front-and-back copies, conduct a LIVE video interaction, CHECK the alternative-procedure box in Section 2/Supplement B, and RETAIN clear/legible front-and-back copies.
trigger: Section 2 (or Supplement B) completed without physical in-person exam.
threshold: E-Verify enrolled + good standing + case created (non-reverification) + live video + box checked + copies retained.
deadline: Same 3-business-day Section 2 clock.
severityPenalty: Remote exam by a non-qualified E-Verify participant, or missing any element, invalidates the exam — substantive ($288–$2,861).
citation: **DHS final rule "Optional Alternatives to the Physical Document Examination," 88 FR 47990 (publ. July 25, 2023; eff. Aug 1, 2023)** — added **8 CFR 274a.2(b)(1)(ix)**; companion authorization notice **"Optional Alternative 1," 88 FR 47749 (July 25, 2023)** (sets out the five operative conditions); **M-274 §4.5**; 3-day clock **8 CFR 274a.2(b)(1)(ii)**. *(Original mis-pinned the FR cite to the Aug 1 effective date and omitted the 47749 companion notice that imposes the five elements.)*
dataNeeded: remoteAlternativeUsed (bool); employerEnrolledInEVerify + goodStanding; eVerifyCaseCreated (except reverification); altProcedureBoxChecked; copiesRetainedFrontBack; liveVideoConducted (attested).
implementationNote: Deterministic gating: remoteAlternativeUsed==true ⇒ require enrolled && goodStanding && (caseCreated || isReverification) && boxChecked && copiesRetainedFrontBack — flag any false. liveVideoConducted is an unverifiable attestation (flag only if captured false). Non-E-Verify employers cannot use this procedure at all — hard fail.

check: Employer did not request more/different documents than required, or specify which documents the employee must present.
requirement: Must not request more/different docs, specify which acceptable doc(s) to present, or reject genuine-appearing docs — when done with intent to discriminate by citizenship status or national origin ("document abuse" / unfair documentary practices).
trigger: Document request/collection during verification; patterns like always requiring a green card from foreign-looking employees, or A+B+C all collected.
threshold: No over/under-documentation; employee free choice; no document-type targeting by citizenship/national origin. **Intent to discriminate required.**
deadline: n/a (charge filed with DOJ-IER within 180 days — see charge_window).
severityPenalty: 8 USC 1324b(a)(6): **$236–$2,364/individual** (2025). Enforced by DOJ-IER, not ICE. Intent element required.
citation: 8 USC 1324b(a)(1) & (a)(6); 28 CFR 44.200(a)(3); penalty 8 USC 1324b(g)(2)(B)(iv)(IV) as adjusted in 28 CFR 85.5. *(Confirmed verbatim; 28 CFR 85.5 Table 1 maps (iv)(IV) to unfair documentary practices, distinct from (iv)(I)-(III).)*
dataNeeded: per form: documents-per-list count (over-collection = List A + B/C both present); doc type vs national-origin/citizenship status (risk signal only); rejection events.
implementationNote: Partly deterministic as a RISK SIGNAL, not a legal finding: flag forms with a List A doc AND List B/C both recorded (textbook over-doc), or a single doc type disproportionately required from a protected subgroup. Liability requires intent → always emit NEEDS-COUNSEL; surface the pattern for IER/human review, never auto-adjudicate 1324b.

check: No citizenship-status or national-origin discrimination in hiring, firing, or recruitment/referral for a fee.
requirement: Unlawful to intentionally discriminate against protected individuals by citizenship/immigration status, or any individual by national origin, in hiring/discharge/recruitment-or-referral-for-a-fee. National-origin coverage under 1324b: employers with 4–14 employees (Title VII covers 15+; citizenship-status prong has no upper cap and binds all 4+). "US-citizen-only" policies generally unlawful absent a law/contract requirement.
trigger: Hiring/firing/recruitment decisions; citizenship-status preferences.
threshold: No intentional citizenship-status/national-origin discrimination; "US-citizen-only" unlawful unless required by law/regulation/EO/government contract (INA 274B(a)(2)(C)).
deadline: Charge filed with DOJ-IER within 180 days of the act.
severityPenalty: Per individual (2025): first $590–$4,730; second $4,730–$11,823; third+ $7,093–$23,647; plus back pay + hiring/reinstatement (28 CFR 85.5 adjusted figures).
citation: 8 USC 1324b(a)(1),(a)(2),(a)(3); 28 CFR 44.200; penalties 8 USC 1324b(g)(2)(B)(iv)(I)-(III) as adjusted in 28 CFR 85.5. Sharpen: 180-day deadline = **1324b(d)(3)**; the "4–14" band is a synthesis of **(a)(2)(A)** (floor: excludes "three or fewer," so 4+) and **(a)(2)(B)** (ceiling: national-origin deferred to Title VII, so 15+) — not verbatim statutory text. *(Confirmed.)*
dataNeeded: employee count (for the 4–14 national-origin line); job-posting citizenship requirements; legal/contractual basis for any citizenship requirement; adverse-action records by protected status.
implementationNote: Almost entirely NEEDS-COUNSEL — intent and pattern-or-practice are legal determinations. Mechanical sub-checks only: flag postings/policies with "US citizens only" / "no visa sponsorship / green-card holders only" absent a recorded legal-authority basis; confirm headcount to determine 1324b (4–14) vs Title VII (15+) jurisdiction.

check: Awareness that 1324b charges must be filed with DOJ-IER within 180 days of the act.
requirement: A charge of an unfair immigration-related employment practice must be filed with DOJ-IER within 180 days of the alleged occurrence.
trigger: An alleged discriminatory or document-abuse act.
threshold: 180 days from the act.
deadline: 180 days after the act.
severityPenalty: Procedural/jurisdictional — late charge generally time-barred.
citation: 8 USC 1324b(d)(3); 28 CFR 44.300(b). *(Confirmed verbatim; the USC/CFR text says "Special Counsel" — renamed IER in 2016 without amending the text, so "DOJ-IER" reflects current practice.)*
dataNeeded: date of alleged act; date charge filed (if known).
implementationNote: Deterministic if a charge date exists: chargeDate − actDate > 180 → likely time-barred. Primarily an exposure-scoping helper; equitable-tolling exceptions make a hard bar a NEEDS-COUNSEL call.

check: E-Verify case created by the third business day after the employee starts work for pay.
requirement: Create a case for each new hire no later than the 3rd business day after start of work for pay. Case cannot be created until the I-9 is complete; may not pre-screen before offer acceptance. Late cases require a documented delay reason.
trigger: New hire at an E-Verify employer (or FAR-E-Verify federal contractor).
threshold: By the 3rd business day after first day of work for pay. Earliest: after I-9 completion and offer acceptance.
deadline: 3rd business day after start of work for pay.
severityPenalty: MOU compliance (Art. II.A); persistent lateness can terminate E-Verify enrollment and is evidence in an ICE inspection. For FAR contractors, contract-compliance issue.
citation: E-Verify User Manual §2.2 "Create a Case"; prohibited-practices/pre-screening list + Glossary "Prescreening"; **FAR 52.222-54 (48 CFR 52.222-54), prescribed at FAR 22.1803** for federal contractors; E-Verify MOU Art. II.A (secondary). **REMOVE "6 CFR Part 5"** (that is DHS FOIA/Privacy Act disclosure, unrelated). *(For contractors, FAR phrases timing as "within 3 business days after date of hire," with a 30-day enroll + 90-day phase-in window.)*
dataNeeded: first day of work for pay; eVerifyCaseCreationDate; i9CompletionDate; businessDayCalendar; delayReason (if late); federalContractorFlag.
implementationNote: Deterministic: businessDaysBetween(startDate, caseCreationDate) > 3 → late (check delayReason present). Flag caseCreationDate < i9CompletionDate (out of order) and pre-hire case creation (prohibited pre-screening). "3 or more days late requires a reason" ⇒ lateCase==true should always carry a delayReason.

check: On a TNC (mismatch), employer notified the employee promptly and completed required referral steps within 10 federal government working days.
requirement: Notify the employee ASAP, give and privately review the Further Action Notice (FAN), let the employee decide, confirm the decision, and refer if contested — all within 10 federal government working days of mismatch issuance. If no decision by day 10, close the case.
trigger: E-Verify returns a TNC/mismatch (SSA or DHS).
threshold: Employer action (notify + confirm decision + refer if contested) within 10 federal government working days of TNC issuance.
deadline: 10 federal government working days after TNC issuance.
severityPenalty: MOU compliance; mishandling supports bad-faith findings and 1324b exposure; can lead to E-Verify termination / contractor non-compliance.
citation: E-Verify MOU Art. II §A; E-Verify User Manual §3.3 (incl. 3.3.1 Notify / 3.3.2 Confirm Decision / 3.3.3 Refer); USCIS guidance "REMINDER: Employer Action Required on Tentative Nonconfirmations (Mismatches) within 10 Federal Government Working Days." *(Confirmed.)*
dataNeeded: tncIssueDate; employeeNotifiedDate; fanGivenDate; employeeDecisionDate; referralDate; federalWorkingDayCalendar.
implementationNote: Deterministic with a FEDERAL working-day calendar (excludes weekends AND federal holidays — distinct from the I-9 "business day" calendar): flag if notify/confirm/refer not completed within 10 federal working days of tncIssueDate, or fanGivenDate null.

check: Referred employee given the 8-federal-working-day window to contact SSA/DHS, reflected in the Referral Date Confirmation.
requirement: On a contested+referred TNC, the employee must contact DHS or visit an SSA field office within 8 federal government working days; employer must print and give the Referral Date Confirmation (read/translate if LEP) and attach a copy to the I-9.
trigger: Employee elects to contest a TNC and the case is referred.
threshold: Employee has 8 federal government working days from referral; employer must provide the Referral Date Confirmation.
deadline: 8 federal government working days for the employee (employer duty: provide the confirmation at referral).
severityPenalty: MOU obligation; mishandling = E-Verify violation + 1324b risk.
citation: **E-Verify User Manual §3.3.3 "Refer Employee To DHS or SSA"** (with §3.3.2 "Confirm Employee Decision" as cross-ref); E-Verify MOU Art. II. **The supplied §3.3.2 URL/slug is stale/dead** (manual renamed "tnc" → "mismatch"). *(Original cited §3.3.2; the 8-day window + RDC employer-duty language is in §3.3.3.)*
dataNeeded: referralDate; referralDateConfirmationProvided (bool); federalWorkingDayCalendar.
implementationNote: Mostly a presence/timing check employer-side: flag if a referral occurred but referralDateConfirmationProvided==false. The 8-day clock is the employee's; the evaluator confirms the employer issued the confirmation and did not close/terminate prematurely. Do not conflate with the separate 10-day employer action window or the 10-day DHS/SSA update window.

check: Employer took NO adverse action against an employee contesting a TNC (case pending / referred / in continuance).
requirement: While a TNC case is pending (referred or in continuance), may not terminate, suspend, delay/withhold training, reduce hours, lower/withhold pay, or take any other adverse action because of the mismatch, until a Final Nonconfirmation. Employee continues working while resolving.
trigger: An E-Verify case is in TNC/referred/continuance status.
threshold: Zero adverse actions attributable to the mismatch until Final Nonconfirmation (or close with authorization).
deadline: n/a (prohibition spanning pendency).
severityPenalty: Adverse action while pending = MOU violation + strong 1324b risk ($236–$23,647 ranges) + back-pay. After FNC, may terminate with no MOU liability.
citation: E-Verify MOU Art. II §A (paras 12-13, no-adverse-action / close-without-liability); E-Verify User Manual §3.3; 8 USC 1324b (anti-discrimination overlay: (a)(1) citizenship/national-origin + (a)(5) anti-retaliation). *(Confirmed near-verbatim.)*
dataNeeded: caseStatus timeline (TNC|referred|continuance|FNC|closed); adverse-action events (termination/suspension/hour-reduction/pay-change) with dates; reason codes.
implementationNote: Deterministic correlation: flag any adverse-action event dated while caseStatus ∈ {TNC, referred, continuance} and before a Final Nonconfirmation. "Because of the mismatch" causation = judgment (an unrelated documented for-cause termination is permissible) → emit the timing flag + NEEDS-COUNSEL on causation. One of the highest-liability E-Verify checks.

check: Photo-matching step performed and, on a photo-mismatch contest, a copy of the employee's document submitted to DHS.
requirement: For photo-matching documents (U.S. passport/passport card, Form I-551, Form I-766), compare the E-Verify-displayed photo to the document photo and indicate match. On a contested DHS photo-mismatch TNC, attach/submit a copy of the document to DHS.
trigger: Employee presents a passport/passport card, Form I-551, or Form I-766 (List A) and a case is created.
threshold: Photo comparison recorded; on photo-mismatch contest, document copy uploaded to DHS.
deadline: Case created by the 3rd business day after start of work for pay; employer notify+refer within 10 federal working days of mismatch; employee acts within 8 federal working days after referral. *(Original "10 federal working days to act" conflated the employer's 10-day window with the employee's separate 8-day window.)*
severityPenalty: MOU/process obligation; failure to perform photo matching or submit the copy on a photo TNC can invalidate the case and support bad-faith findings.
citation: E-Verify User Manual §2.2.2 (E-Verify Photo Matching) and §3.3 (TNC handling); E-Verify MOU Art. II. *(Confirmed; the four photo-matching documents and document-submission-on-mismatch verified verbatim.)*
dataNeeded: section2DocType; photoMatchResult (match|no-match|recorded); on photo-TNC contest: documentCopySubmittedToDHS (bool); copyRetained (bool).
implementationNote: Deterministic gating: section2DocType ∈ {US passport, US passport card, Form I-551, Form I-766} ⇒ photoMatchResult must be recorded (flag if missing). DHS photo-mismatch TNC contested ⇒ require documentCopySubmittedToDHS==true. Chain to copy-retention (photo matching requires a retained document copy).

check: Classify each defect as substantive vs technical/procedural and apply the ≥10-business-day cure period correctly.
requirement: During an ICE I-9 inspection, technical/procedural failures are noted on a Notice of Technical or Procedural Failures with AT LEAST 10 business days to correct; uncorrected → substantive. Substantive + uncorrected-technical violations are penalized.
trigger: Any detected I-9 defect during a self-audit or ICE inspection.
threshold: Substantive = no cure. Technical/procedural = ≥10 business days to cure; uncorrected → substantive. Cure period runs from ICE's notice.
deadline: ≥10 business days from the Notice of Technical or Procedural Failures.
severityPenalty: Each substantive (or uncorrected technical) → $288–$2,861 (2025). Knowing-hire separate ($716–$28,619).
citation: Cure provision = **INA 274A(b)(6) = 8 USC 1324a(b)(6)** ("not less than 10 business days") — **NOT 8 CFR 274a.2(b)(3)** (the cure period is statutory and does not appear in 274a.2). Penalty **8 CFR 274a.10(b)(2)** (correct). **The 1997 Virtue Memorandum no longer controls the classification** — superseded by the **ICE Form I-9 Inspection fact sheet updated 2026-03-16**. Current substantive examples include missing Section 1 date/signature/status, missing Section 2 document title/issuing authority/number/expiration, missing alternative-procedure checkbox where applicable, and missing Section 2 signature/date.
dataNeeded: per defect: defect type; section; prepared/presented flags; timeliness facts; cure status + cure date vs ICE notice date; retained-copy evidence may be captured for record completeness but must not lower severity.
implementationNote: Implement a CLASSIFICATION TABLE mapping defect type → {substantive|technical} from the current ICE fact sheet, not the Virtue Memo. Do not encode a retained-copy severity branch for missing Section 2 document data. Deterministic for enumerated items; NEEDS-COUNSEL for anything off-table or where OCAHO case law is evolving. Cure logic: technical uncorrected after ≥10 business days from notice → reclassify substantive. This rule converts per-field flags into penalty-bearing findings.

check: Paperwork penalty derived from the five statutory factors and the correct per-form base range.
requirement: Per-individual penalty set within the range using FIVE factors: (1) business size, (2) good faith, (3) seriousness, (4) whether the individual was an unauthorized alien, (5) prior-violation history. ICE's baseline-percentage matrix scales within the min/max; OCAHO may adjust.
trigger: Any assessed substantive or uncorrected-technical paperwork violation.
threshold: Per individual/form: $288–$2,861 (2025, in force through CY2026). Knowing-hire separate: 1st $716–$5,724; 2nd $5,724–$14,308; 3rd+ $8,586–$28,619. Indemnity-bond: $2,861.
deadline: n/a.
severityPenalty: Defines per-violation dollar exposure; figures re-adjust annually under 28 CFR 85.5.
citation: 8 CFR 274a.10(b)(2) (paperwork + five factors) and (b)(1)(ii)(A)-(C) (knowing-hire tiers); inflation-adjusted amounts 28 CFR 85.5; 8 USC 1324a(e)(5),(e)(4). *(Confirmed — five factors verbatim and in order; dollar figures match current 28 CFR 85.5, effective July 3, 2025 per 90 FR 29447. Note the CFR body text in 274a.10 still shows stale base ranges; the 28 CFR 85.5 amounts control.)*
dataNeeded: employer size; good-faith indicators; per-violation seriousness tag; unauthorized-alien status; prior-violation history; violationDate + assessmentDate.
implementationNote: Two-part: (a) deterministic range selection — pick min/max from a versioned 28 CFR 85.5 table keyed to violationDate and assessmentDate (do NOT hard-code 288/2861); (b) five-factor scaling is partly discretionary — encode ICE's baseline matrix as a transparent estimate but flag final number = ICE/OCAHO discretion → NEEDS-COUNSEL. Keep knowing-hire vs paperwork as distinct schedules.

check: Actual wage paid ≥ greater of (actual wage for similarly-employed workers) and (prevailing wage on the LCA).
requirement: Pay the "required wage" = greater of (i) the actual wage to all individuals with similar experience/qualifications for the specific employment, or (ii) the prevailing wage for the occupation in the area of intended employment. Cash in hand, free and clear, when due.
trigger: Any pay period for any H-1B worker on a certified LCA.
threshold: max(actual_wage, prevailing_wage). A posted wage RANGE satisfies only if the bottom of the range ≥ prevailing wage. Hourly↔annual via 2,080 hrs/yr.
deadline: Each pay period (at least monthly).
severityPenalty: Back wages (655.810(a)) = required − paid. CMP up to $2,364 (substantial) / $9,624 (willful). Debarment 1–3 yrs.
citation: 20 CFR 655.731(a); 655.731(a)(1) (actual); 655.731(a)(2) (prevailing); 655.731(c)(1) (cash in hand / free and clear). *(Confirmed verbatim; payment-frequency basis is (c)(7); range rule (a)(2)(ii); 2,080-hr conversion (c)(2)(ii).)*
dataNeeded: Per worker: LCA prevailing_wage (amount+unit+level); employer actual_wage for the role; gross wages paid per period; pay frequency; FT/PT; hours; cohort wage rates.
implementationNote: Deterministic once actual_wage and prevailing_wage known: required = max(...); flag if paid < required. PT ⇒ compare hourly (convert via 2,080). Wage range compliant only if floor ≥ prevailing. Deriving the "actual wage" from the peer cohort → NEEDS-COUNSEL; the arithmetic comparison is mechanical.

check: Prevailing wage from an acceptable source, correct skill level, within its validity window at filing.
requirement: PW determined as of filing from an acceptable source: arms-length CBA; OFLC NPWC PWD (arithmetic mean of OES/OEWS at level I–IV); independent authoritative survey; or another legitimate source. An OFLC PWD is valid ≥90 days and ≤1 year from determination.
trigger: At LCA filing, and whenever the wage basis is documented/refreshed.
threshold: PWD validity ≥90 and ≤365 days. Survey recency: data collected within 24 months preceding publication; latest published edition (published within 24 months before filing). Academic/research employers: level reflects only such institutions.
deadline: Determined as of filing; OFLC PWD must be valid on the filing date.
severityPenalty: A defective PW flows into a wage violation (back wages + CMP up to $2,364, or $9,624 willful). Misrepresenting the PW basis = substantial/willful-misrepresentation.
citation: **20 CFR 655.731(a)(2)** (PW determined "as of the time of filing"; greater-of); **655.731(a)(2)(i)** (CBA); **655.731(a)(2)(ii) / (a)(2)(ii)(A)** (OFLC NPC/OES, arithmetic mean of BLS OES); **655.731(a)(2)(ii)(A)** (validity "not less than 90 days or more than 1 year") and **(a)(2)(ii)(A)(1)** (file LCA within the PWD validity period); **655.731(a)(2)(ii)(B)/(C)** (independent authoritative / other legitimate source); **655.731(a)(2)(vii)** (academic/nonprofit-research carve-out); **655.731(b)(3) / (b)(3)(iii)(B)-(C)** (documentation incl. 24-month recency). **For the wage LEVEL I–IV tiering, cite 20 CFR 656.40(b)(2) + DOL OFLC PW guidance, NOT 655.731** ("level I-IV" does not appear in 655.731). *(Thresholds verbatim-correct; pinpoints corrected.)*
dataNeeded: PW source type; PWD tracking number + issue + expiration (if OFLC); OES area + SOC + level; survey publication date + data-collection window; CBA citation; employer entity-type flag (academic/research).
implementationNote: Validity-window and recency checks = deterministic date math (90≤days≤365; survey≤24mo). SELECTION of the correct OES level (I–IV) → NEEDS-COUNSEL; the validity/recency arithmetic is mechanical.

check: Worker in employer-caused non-productive status still paid the full required wage; non-payment only where the (c)(7)(ii) exception applies.
requirement: Non-productive status due to an EMPLOYER decision (lack of work, lack of permit/license, any reason except (c)(7)(ii)) ⇒ pay salaried the full pro-rata amount, or hourly for a full-time week (40 hrs, or the employer's demonstrated full-time number), at the required wage. Need NOT pay for non-productive time due to conditions UNRELATED to employment that EITHER (a) take the worker away at their voluntary request/convenience, OR (b) render them unable to work — subject to benefit plans and FMLA/ADA.
trigger: Any period a worker who has entered into employment performs no work (bench time, project gap, pending license).
threshold: Salaried: full pro-rata salary at required wage. Hourly: a full-time week (40 hrs, or the employer's demonstrated full-time number) at required wage; PT LCAs pay ≥ the I-129 hours. The (c)(7)(ii) exception applies when the period is due to conditions UNRELATED to employment that EITHER (a) are at the worker's voluntary request/convenience OR (b) render the worker unable to work — **these are alternative limbs joined by OR, not a single "voluntary + unable-to-work" test**; and not to the extent payable under the employer's benefit plan or FMLA/ADA. *(Original threshold wrongly required "(a) unrelated AND (b) voluntary rendering unable to work.")*
deadline: Continuous — every pay period of the non-productive period.
severityPenalty: Back wages for unpaid bench time ("benching"). CMP up to $2,364, or $9,624 willful. Debarment 1–3 yrs.
citation: 20 CFR 655.731(c)(7)(i) (pay required); 655.731(c)(7)(ii) (exception). *(Confirmed verbatim; only the compressed threshold wording was wrong.)*
dataNeeded: Per worker/period: productive/non-productive flag; reason code (employer-caused vs worker-voluntary-non-employment); FT/PT + full-time-hours definition; wage paid; approved-leave/FMLA/ADA flag; benefit-plan PTO usage.
implementationNote: Mechanical if the reason is coded employer-caused (pay mandatory; any shortfall = violation). Classifying a gap as employer-caused vs the (c)(7)(ii) exception → NEEDS-COUNSEL. Pair with the wage-start-clock rule: bench liability begins only once the worker has "entered into employment." No required-wage payment after a bona fide termination.

check: Required-wage liability begins no later than 30 days after admission, or 60 days after becoming eligible to work (if already present).
requirement: Obligation attaches when the worker "enters into employment" (first available for work / under employer control); in no case later than 30 days after admission pursuant to the petition, or — if already in the U.S. at approval — 60 days after becoming eligible to work.
trigger: Onboarding of a new H-1B worker (consular admission or in-country COS/transfer).
threshold: 30 days after admission; OR 60 days after becoming eligible (already in U.S.).
deadline: Wage flowing by day 30 (admission) / day 60 (in-country) at the latest, even without assigned work.
severityPenalty: Back wages / benching exposure for the gap. CMP up to $2,364 (or $9,624 willful).
citation: **20 CFR 655.731(c)(6)(i)-(ii)** (paragraph (c)(6) has only (i) and (ii) — **drop the "(iii)"**), with the nonproductive-status cross-reference at **655.731(c)(7)**. *(Original cited (c)(6)(i)-(iii); there is no (c)(6)(iii).)*
dataNeeded: Per worker: consular admission date (I-94) OR in-country eligibility date; entry pathway; first available-for-work date; first pay date.
implementationNote: Deterministic: required_start = admission_date+30 (new admission) or eligibility_date+60 (in-country); flag if first_pay_date > required_start. "Eligible to work" = date of need on the petition or DHS adjustment date, whichever later.

check: H-1B workers offered the same benefits package on the same criteria as similarly-employed U.S. workers; benefits actually received.
requirement: Benefits and eligibility offered on the SAME BASIS and SAME CRITERIA as U.S. workers; no stricter rules; not denied as "temporary." Good-faith offers resulting in actual receipt. Limited home-country options for ≤90-day short-term and >90-day extended multinational assignments.
trigger: Enrollment windows; any benefit offered to the U.S. workforce in the same occupation.
threshold: Same package + same criteria. Multinational home-country cut-off: 90 consecutive calendar days. Identicality not required where the worker voluntarily elects different options from the same package.
deadline: Throughout the longer of LCA validity or H-1B employment.
severityPenalty: Withheld benefits recoverable as back wages. CMP up to $2,364 (or $9,624 willful).
citation: **20 CFR 655.731(c)(3)(i)-(iii)** (requirement + threshold) and **documentation at 655.731(c)(3)** (and cross-referenced (b)(3) recordkeeping). **DROP the (b)(1) documentation pin** — (b)(1) is general payroll/wage-statement documentation, not the benefits-documentation duty. *(Confirmed substance; 90-consecutive-calendar-day cut-off verbatim in both (c)(3)(iii)(B) short-term and (C) extended.)*
dataNeeded: Benefit plan eligibility rules; enrollment records H-1B vs U.S.-worker cohort same occupation; waiting-period/vesting; for multinationals: assignment length + home-country enrollment + reciprocal-treatment evidence.
implementationNote: Partially mechanical (compare eligibility flags/waiting periods vs the U.S.-worker plan; flag stricter terms). "Same basis" and multinational home-country equivalence → NEEDS-COUNSEL.

check: No deduction reduces the wage below the required wage unless in one of three authorized categories; employer business expenses (incl. ACWIA fee) never passed to the worker.
requirement: A deduction may reduce cash wage below required wage ONLY if (1) required by law (tax, FICA); (2) CBA-authorized, or reasonable-and-customary in the occupation/area (not a recoupment of employer business expense); or (3) a voluntary, written-authorized deduction principally for the worker's benefit, not a business-expense recoupment, ≤ fair market value, within CCPA garnishment limits. May not recoup the ACWIA fee or other employer business expenses; early-cessation penalties prohibited.
trigger: Any payroll deduction, wage offset, or cost-shift to the worker.
threshold: Post-deduction cash wage ≥ required wage unless category (1)/(2)/(3). ACWIA fee ($500/$1,000 by employer size) and the $500 fraud fee non-recoupable in full.
deadline: Each pay period.
severityPenalty: Back wages restore the deducted amount. ACWIA-fee or early-termination-penalty charge = distinct violation: CMP up to $2,364 (+ reimbursement); willful up to $9,624.
citation: **20 CFR 655.731(c)(9)(i)-(iii)** (three authorized categories; business-expense bar at (c)(9)(iii)(C)); **655.731(c)(10)(i)** (early-cessation PENALTY prohibition; penalty-vs-liquidated-damages under State law); **655.731(c)(10)(ii)** (worker may not pay any part of the $500/$1,000 additional filing fee). **NOT (c)(11)** — (c)(11) is the separate "unauthorized deduction = non-payment of wages" rule. The $500 fraud-prevention fee = INA 214(c)(12)/8 USC 1184(c)(12), recoupment barred via (c)(9)(iii)(C)/(c)(10)(i). *(Dollar precision: 655.731(c)(10)(ii) names only $500/$1,000, keyed to filing before vs on/after Dec 18, 2000 — it does not contain $1,500, and the "$500 fraud fee" is not in 655.731.)*
dataNeeded: Per worker/period: itemized deductions with category code; written authorization on file (Y/N); whether the item is an employer business expense; FMV basis; any training-fee/visa-cost/attorney-fee/breach-penalty charged to the worker; net wage vs required wage.
implementationNote: Mechanical for the floor test (net ≥ required_wage) and hard-prohibited items (flag any ACWIA/fraud-fee or early-termination-penalty charge to the worker). Whether a category-2/3 deduction is genuinely "for the worker's benefit" → NEEDS-COUNSEL.

check: H-1B workers afforded working conditions (hours, shifts, vacation, seniority-based preferences) on the same basis as similarly-employed U.S. workers.
requirement: Attestation 2: employment of H-1B workers will not adversely affect the working conditions of similarly-employed workers; afford the same basis/criteria (hours, shifts, vacation, fringe such as seniority-based training/schedule preferences).
trigger: Setting/changing schedules, shifts, vacation, or seniority-based perks for the occupation.
threshold: Same basis/criteria as similarly-employed U.S. workers (no quantitative threshold).
deadline: Throughout the longer of LCA validity or H-1B employment.
severityPenalty: Substantial violation if it rises to misrepresentation / attestation failure; CMP up to $2,364, or $9,624 willful.
citation: 20 CFR 655.732(a) (attestation/scope); 655.732(b) (documentation). *(Confirmed verbatim — §655.732 is the second LCA requirement; statutory hook INA 212(n)(1)(A)(ii).)*
dataNeeded: Scheduling/shift/vacation policy; seniority/training-program access rules; H-1B vs U.S.-worker comparison same occupation; complaints alleging adverse effect.
implementationNote: Largely qualitative/attestation-style. Whether conditions "adversely affect" → NEEDS-COUNSEL. Implement as a presence-of-policy + parity-of-treatment checklist, not a numeric evaluator.

check: No strike/lockout in the occupation at the place of employment as of filing; if one arises post-certification, notify ETA within 3 days and stop placing H-1B workers there.
requirement: Attestation 3: as of filing, no strike/lockout in the occupational classification in the area of intended employment. If one occurs after submission, notify ETA within 3 days (mail/fax/private carrier) and do not place/assign/lease/contract out an H-1B worker to any place of employment with such a strike/lockout until ETA determines it ended. ETA may certify to DHS under 8 CFR 214.2(h)(17).
trigger: LCA filing (point-in-time attestation); any strike/lockout/work-stoppage in the occupation at the worksite during the LCA's life.
threshold: 3 days to notify ETA. Scope = the named occupational classification at the place of employment (post-cert no-placement); attestation as-of-filing scope = area of intended employment.
deadline: Notice to ETA within 3 days; cessation of placement immediate.
severityPenalty: CMP up to $2,364 (substantial), up to $9,624 willful. Obligations survive LCA withdrawal (655.750(b)). Petitions for the struck location invalidated.
citation: 20 CFR 655.733(a); 655.733(a)(1) (3-day ETA notice); 655.733(a)(2) (ETA certification to DHS, 8 CFR 214.2(h)(17)). *(Confirmed verbatim, incl. the mail/fax/private-carrier channels and the "place, assign, lease, or otherwise contract out" verbs. One scope-sharpen: the as-of-filing attestation is keyed to "area of intended employment," not "place of employment.")*
dataNeeded: Per worksite/occupation: active labor-dispute/strike/lockout flag + start date; ETA notice sent date; H-1B placements at the affected worksite; occupational classification.
implementationNote: Mechanical once an event is recorded: enforce notify-ETA-within-3-days + block new placements. Whether a given event is a qualifying "strike or lockout in the course of a labor dispute in the occupational classification" → NEEDS-COUNSEL; the 3-day clock is deterministic.

check: Notice to the bargaining rep, OR posted in 2 conspicuous locations for 10 days / delivered electronically, on or within 30 days before filing, with required content and dated proof.
requirement: Attestation 4: notify the bargaining rep (if any) on or within 30 days before filing; OR, if none, post hard-copy notice in ≥2 conspicuous locations at each place of employment for a total of 10 days, OR provide electronic notification to affected employees for 10 days. Content: H-1B sought; number; occupational classification; wage rate; period; location(s); LCA available for public inspection; complaints may be filed with U.S. DOL.
trigger: Every LCA filing; every new place of employment added.
threshold: 2 physical posting locations per worksite; 10 days posted/available; window = on or within 30 days BEFORE filing.
deadline: Posting on/within 30 days before filing; hard-copy stays up 10 days; electronic available 10 days.
severityPenalty: Notice violation; CMP up to $2,364, up to $9,624 willful.
citation: **20 CFR 655.734(a)(1)(i)** (bargaining-rep notice + content + WHD statement, 30-days-before); **655.734(a)(1)(ii)** chapeau (no-rep notice content + "available for public inspection" + WHD statement); **655.734(a)(1)(ii)(A)** and **(a)(1)(ii)(A)(3)** (≥2 conspicuous locations, posted on/within 30 days before, 10 days); **655.734(a)(1)(ii)(B)** (electronic notice, 10 days, single direct e-mail suffices); **655.734(b)** (documentation); **655.734(c)/§655.760** (retention). **DROP the cite to "655.734(a)(1)(iii)" for content** — no such paragraph exists (content is carried in (a)(1)(i) and the (a)(1)(ii) chapeau). *(Original cited a non-existent (a)(1)(iii).)*
dataNeeded: Per LCA: bargaining-rep exists? + notice date; OR posting locations (count + addresses) + start date + take-down date (≥10 days); OR electronic-notice method + window; content fields present; filing date.
implementationNote: Highly mechanical: verify posting_start within [filing−30, filing], duration ≥10 days, location_count ≥2 (hard-copy), and each required content field present. Bargaining-rep path = either/or branch keyed off a single flag. Good candidate for a fully deterministic evaluator with a content-completeness sub-check.

check: Each H-1B worker received a copy of the ETA-certified LCA no later than their first day of work.
requirement: Provide the H-1B worker a copy of the certified LCA (ETA-9035/9035E) no later than the date the worker reports to work (cover pages ETA-9035CP on request).
trigger: Onboarding / first reporting date of each H-1B worker.
threshold: By the first workday.
deadline: On/before the worker's first day of work.
severityPenalty: Notice violation; CMP up to $2,364 (substantial), up to $9,624 willful.
citation: 20 CFR 655.734(a)(3). *(Confirmed verbatim; "(a)(3)" is exactly the worker-copy requirement.)*
dataNeeded: Per worker: certified-LCA-delivered date; worker first-report-to-work date; acknowledgment of receipt (if captured).
implementationNote: Fully deterministic: flag if delivery_date > first_workday or null. For a worksite-change scenario the trigger is the actual report-to-work date at that place of employment, which may be a later placement date.

check: LCA used only within its certified validity period; H-1B petition not relying on an expired/withdrawn LCA.
requirement: Certified LCA valid for the DOL-stated period, ≤3 years for H-1B (E-3 ≤2; **H-1B1 initial ≤3 — same as H-1B**; H-1B1 extension ≤2). Validity cannot begin before certification. May be filed no earlier than 6 months before the start date.
trigger: LCA filing; petition filing/extension relying on the LCA.
threshold: Max validity 3 years (H-1B). Earliest filing: 6 months before start.
deadline: Employment within [certified start, certified end]; filing ≥ start−6 months.
severityPenalty: Out-of-period LCA undermines the petition and can support misrepresentation; CMP up to $2,364 (or willful $9,624).
citation: 20 CFR 655.750(a) (validity, 3-yr max); 20 CFR 655.730(b) (no earlier than 6 months before start). *(Both confirmed verbatim. CORRECTION: the "H-1B1 initial ≤2 yrs" sub-claim is WRONG — 655.750(a) groups initial H-1B1 WITH H-1B at 3 years; only the H-1B1 EXTENSION is capped at 2.)*
dataNeeded: Per LCA: certified start, certified end, filing date, intended start; mapped H-1B petition validity dates.
implementationNote: Deterministic: (end−start) ≤ 3yr; filing_date ≥ start−6mo; flag employment dates outside [start,end]. Pure date math.

check: Every worksite where the worker performs work is within the area of intended employment on a certified LCA (or covered by short-term-placement / Simeio amendment).
requirement: The place of employment must be within the "area of intended employment" — within normal commuting distance of the LCA address; any place in the same MSA/PMSA is deemed within commuting distance. Brief developmental activities and short peripatetic visits are not "places of employment" (peripatetic ≤5 consecutive workdays/visit; based-elsewhere occasional ≤10 consecutive workdays).
trigger: Any worksite assignment, client placement, or relocation.
threshold: Within normal commuting distance / same MSA. Non-worksite carve-outs: peripatetic ≤5; based-elsewhere occasional ≤10 consecutive workdays.
deadline: Continuous.
severityPenalty: Working outside an LCA-covered area without a new LCA / short-term coverage = LCA specificity/wage violation; CMP up to $2,364 + back-wage exposure if the new area's PW is higher; triggers Simeio amended petition.
citation: 20 CFR 655.715 (definitions); 655.731(a)(2) (PW tied to area of intended employment). *(Confirmed verbatim.)*
dataNeeded: Per worker: current worksite address(es) + MSA; LCA worksite address(es) + MSA; commuting/MSA mapping; consecutive-workday counts at off-LCA locations.
implementationNote: Mechanical with an MSA/commuting geocode: flag worksite_MSA not in {LCA_MSAs} and not short-term-covered. "Normal commuting distance" outside a shared MSA → NEEDS-COUNSEL. Peripatetic-day counting deterministic against the 5/10-day thresholds.

check: Off-LCA placements stay within the 30-workday (or qualifying 60-workday) safe harbor; wage + lodging + travel conditions met.
requirement: Place at a non-LCA worksite without a new LCA only if: (a) meets 655.730–734 for the listed area; (b) no strike/lockout at the new site; (c) per day, pays required wage (higher of home-worksite PW or actual wage) PLUS actual lodging (workdays and non-workdays) PLUS actual travel/meals/incidentals. ≤30 workdays/year (default); extendable to 60 only if the worker keeps an office/work station at the permanent worksite, spends substantial time there, and keeps a U.S. residence in the permanent-worksite area. At the cap: file a new LCA for the area or terminate the placement.
trigger: Placing an H-1B worker at a worksite outside any certified LCA's area.
threshold: 30 workdays/1-year period (default); 60 only if the 3 ties-to-permanent-worksite conditions are met. A "workday" = any day the worker performs any work in the short-term area.
deadline: Stop or file a new LCA on hitting 30 (or qualifying 60) workdays in the rolling year; per-day wage+lodging+travel throughout.
severityPenalty: Exceeding the cap (or missing lodging/travel) → LCA specificity + wage violation; back wages (incl. unreimbursed lodging/travel) + CMP up to $2,364 (or $9,624 willful).
citation: **20 CFR 655.735(b)(3)(i)-(iii)** (wage + lodging + travel — refine from bare (b)); **655.735(c) / (c)(1)-(3)** (30/60 workday caps + 60-day conditions); **655.735(d)** (workday definition); **655.735(f)** (action at the cap). *(Wage/lodging/travel duties are at (b)(3)(i)-(iii), not bare (b).)*
dataNeeded: Per worker/short-term area: workday count in the rolling 1-year window; flags for the three 60-day conditions; per-day lodging paid; per-day travel/meals/incidentals; required wage paid; strike/lockout flag at new site.
implementationNote: Workday counting against 30/60 in a rolling year = deterministic; lodging/travel-payment presence = deterministic. Whether the 60-day extension qualifies → NEEDS-COUNSEL. Treat 30 as the hard auto-flag ceiling unless the conditions are affirmatively evidenced.

check: An amended/new H-1B petition (with corresponding certified LCA) filed BEFORE the worker starts work at a new worksite requiring a new LCA.
requirement: Per Matter of Simeio Solutions and 8 CFR 214.2(h)(2)(i)(E), a change of worksite to an area requiring a new/corresponding LCA is a MATERIAL CHANGE; file an amended/new I-129 with the new certified LCA BEFORE the worker begins at the new location. Same-MSA/commuting-distance moves don't require an amendment (LCA posting still required); short-term placements (655.735) and non-worksite locations also don't, by themselves.
trigger: Relocation to a worksite in a different MSA / area of intended employment than the approved petition's LCA.
threshold: Material change = move to an area requiring a new LCA; amended petition due BEFORE work begins. Same-MSA move = no amendment.
deadline: File the amended/new petition before the worker starts at the new worksite (work may begin upon filing).
severityPenalty: DHS: petition non-compliant / worker out of status (revocation, extension denials). DOL: LCA/wage violation (CMP up to $2,364; back wages if higher PW).
citation: Matter of Simeio Solutions, LLC, 26 I&N Dec. 542 (AAO 2015); 8 CFR 214.2(h)(2)(i)(E); 20 CFR 655.734 (new-site posting still required). *(Confirmed — citation, volume, page, tribunal, year all correct; the worksite-specific "material change" holding is the AAO's interpretation, not bare reg text.)*
dataNeeded: Per worker: approved-petition LCA worksite + MSA; new worksite + MSA; new LCA filing + certification date; amended I-129 filing date; worker start-date at new site; same-MSA determination.
implementationNote: Mechanical trigger: new_worksite_MSA != petition_MSA (and not within commuting distance / not short-term-735) ⇒ require amended_I129_filed_before new_site_start_date + a certified new LCA. Same-area / commuting-distance determination → NEEDS-COUNSEL; otherwise deterministic.

check: An LCA is withdrawn only when no H-1B worker is employed under it and no investigation is pending; wage/working-condition obligations continue until a superseding LCA or bona fide termination.
requirement: Withdraw a certified LCA before expiry only if (i) no H-1B/H-1B1/E-3 worker is employed under it and (ii) the Administrator has not commenced an investigation. Required-wage and working-condition obligations continue at any time H-1B workers are employed under the LCA, unless superseded by a subsequently certified LCA. Strike/lockout obligations remain regardless of withdrawal (and regardless of whether workers are employed).
trigger: Employer attempts to withdraw an LCA, or stops using it while workers remain employed.
threshold: Withdrawal blocked while any covered worker is employed under it or an investigation is open. Withdrawal request must be in writing and sent to ETA OFLC. **The regulation specifies NO effective date for withdrawal** — *(original wrongly asserted "withdrawal is effective on the date ETA receives it"; 655.750(b)(2) sets no effective date.)*
deadline: Obligations run continuously until a valid withdrawal (no workers employed) OR a bona fide termination.
severityPenalty: Purporting to withdraw while a worker is employed does not cut off wage liability — continued back-wage exposure (CMP up to $2,364/$9,624). Doctrinal hook for benching-after-project-end liability.
citation: 20 CFR 655.750(b). Sharpen sub-cites: wage/working-condition continuation = **655.750(b)(3)**; strike-lockout/notice survival = **655.750(b)(4)**. *(Confirmed except the fabricated effective-date detail.)*
dataNeeded: Per LCA: withdrawal request date + ETA-receipt date; whether any covered worker still employed; open-investigation flag; superseding LCA exists?; bona-fide-termination status per worker.
implementationNote: Mechanical gate: block "withdrawn" if employed_workers > 0 or investigation_open; mark wage obligations continuing until withdrawal_valid OR bona_fide_termination per worker. (b)(4) strike/lockout survival is unconditional on employment; (b)(3) wage/working-condition survival is conditioned on workers being employed — keep distinct. Couples with the bona-fide-termination rule.

check: To cut off wage/benching liability: (1) expressly terminated the worker, (2) notified USCIS to revoke the petition, and (3) paid the reasonable cost of return transportation to the worker's last foreign residence.
requirement: Wage liability (incl. non-productive time) does not end until a BONA FIDE termination. Per DOL ARB (Amtel): (1) expressly terminate; (2) notify USCIS so the petition can be revoked; (3) provide return transportation abroad for an involuntary dismissal before the end of authorized admission. Until all three, the employer remains liable.
trigger: Termination or layoff of an H-1B worker.
threshold: All three elements (return-transportation only for employer-initiated/involuntary terminations, to the last foreign residence). Worker has a separate 60-day grace period under 8 CFR 214.1(l)(2).
deadline: Wage clock stops only on the date the LAST of the three is completed; until then back wages accrue.
severityPenalty: Failure → continued back-wage/benching liability for the full required wage through the LCA period. CMP up to $2,364 (or $9,624 willful). Single highest back-wage-exposure rule.
citation: Core test **20 CFR 655.731(c)(7)(ii) AS CONSTRUED BY DOL ARB in Amtel Group of Fla., Inc. v. Yongmahapakorn, ARB No. 04-087 (Sept. 29, 2006)**; supporting **8 CFR 214.2(h)(4)(iii)(E)** (return transportation; not on voluntary resignation) and **8 CFR 214.2(h)(11)** (notify USCIS / revocation). **REMOVE the USCIS "Options for Nonimmigrant Workers Following Termination" archive page** as authority for the employer test — it is worker-side grace-period guidance (archived 2025). *(Two caveats: the reg says only "liable for the reasonable costs" — no "actually provide/pay vs offer" verb; and ARB precedent (Vinayagam/21Tech) EXCUSES the return-transportation element where the worker does not depart / obtains a new H-1B employer. Treat element 3 as the general rule, not absolute → NEEDS-COUNSEL on any disputed/voluntary separation.)*
dataNeeded: Per terminated worker: express-termination date + evidence; USCIS withdrawal/revocation-request date + confirmation; return-transportation paid/provided date + amount (involuntary); voluntary/involuntary flag; last day worked / last paid date; authorized-stay end date.
implementationNote: Mechanical scoring of the 3-element checklist: bona_fide_date = max(termination_date, uscis_notice_date, return_transport_date[if involuntary]); wage liability accrues until that date. Voluntariness and USCIS-notice sufficiency → NEEDS-COUNSEL. Treat missing elements as open liability, not compliant.

check: Employer correctly determines H-1B-dependency (7/12/15% tests), which switches on the extra non-displacement + recruitment attestations.
requirement: H-1B-DEPENDENT if: ≤25 FTE & >7 H-1B; or 26–50 FTE & >12 H-1B; or ≥51 FTE & H-1B ≥15% of FTEs. A willful violator (within prior 5 years) is treated like a dependent employer. FT = 40 hrs/week (floor 35). Status switches on the 655.738 (non-displacement) and 655.739 (recruitment) attestations, unless the LCA is exempt-only.
trigger: Each LCA filing; recompute on material workforce/H-1B change.
threshold: ≤25 FTE & >7; 26–50 & >12; ≥51 & ≥15%. FT = 40 (floor 35). Willful-violator look-back = 5 years.
deadline: As of each LCA filing (and petition filing).
severityPenalty: Mis-marking to evade 655.738/.739 = substantial/willful misrepresentation: CMP up to $2,364, or up to $9,624 (willful), and up to $67,367 + debarment if willful + U.S.-worker displacement.
citation: **20 CFR 655.736(a)(1)(i)-(iii)** (three-part test); **655.736(c)(2)** (snap-shot); **655.736(g)** (consequences/attestations, cross-ref 655.738/.739); **655.736(a)(2)(iii)(A)** (FTE / full-time = 40 hrs, floor 35); **655.736(f)** (willful-violator, 5-yr look-back). **The definitions of "H-1B-dependent employer," "willful violator," and "full-time employee" are in 655.736, NOT 655.715**; "exempt H-1B nonimmigrant" is at 655.736(g)/655.737. *(Original cited definitions at 655.715, which is the general definitions section and does not define these terms.)*
dataNeeded: FTE U.S. employee count (with hours; floor 35); H-1B worker count (FT + PT); prior willful-violation finding within 5 yrs (Y/N); exempt-only-LCA flag.
implementationNote: Headcount/ratio test = deterministic arithmetic (3 brackets + 15% ratio). FTE computation from mixed FT/PT and the snap-shot methodology → NEEDS-COUNSEL near a bracket boundary (7, 12, or 15% line). Status drives whether the next two rules apply.

check: If a dependent/willful-violator employer relies on the exempt carve-out, every worker on the LCA is genuinely exempt ($60,000+ or master's-or-higher in a related specialty).
requirement: A dependent/willful-violator employer is relieved of the 655.738/.739 attestations for an LCA used exclusively for exempt workers. Exempt if (1) wages (incl. assured cash bonuses, NOT benefits) ≥$60,000/yr, or (2) a master's-or-higher degree (or equivalent) in a specialty related to the employment. $60,000 is a full-year cash figure actually received, free and clear, not pro-rated for PT, not met with benefits.
trigger: A dependent/willful-violator employer marks an LCA exempt-only to avoid the extra attestations.
threshold: $60,000/yr cash (full-time-rate, actual receipt) OR master's-or-higher in a related specialty.
deadline: Assessed at LCA/petition filing; the $60,000 must actually be received.
severityPenalty: Wrongly claiming exemption = substantial violation; if it masks a willful failure + displacement, up to $67,367/violation + 3-yr debarment.
citation: 20 CFR 655.737(b) (definition: $60,000 / master's, at (b)(1)/(b)(2)); 655.737(c) (measurement rules: benefits excluded, assured-bonus only, cash free and clear, full $60k received, no PT proration). *(Confirmed verbatim; DOL Fact Sheet #62Q corroborates.)*
dataNeeded: Per worker on the LCA: annual cash wage (excl. benefits) + actual receipt; assured-bonus components; degree level + field + relatedness; FT/PT.
implementationNote: $60,000 prong = mechanical (annual cash ≥ 60000, not pro-rated, benefits excluded). "Master's in a RELATED specialty" and bonus-assurance → NEEDS-COUNSEL. Exemption fails if ANY worker on the LCA is non-exempt.

check: (Dependent/willful-violator, non-exempt LCA) No U.S. worker in an essentially-equivalent job displaced within 90 days before to 90 days after petition filing — including a secondary-employer inquiry.
requirement: Non-exempt LCA: attest no displacement of a U.S. worker in an essentially equivalent job in the area within 90 days before and 90 days after petition filing (DIRECT). For placement with a secondary employer, must have inquired and have no knowledge that the secondary employer displaced/intends to displace a similarly-employed U.S. worker within 90/90 of placement (SECONDARY).
