"Lay off" excludes discharge for cause, voluntary departure/retirement, expiration of a grant/contract (with conditions, not a temporary-contract evasion), and refusal of a bona fide similar offer at equal/greater pay.
trigger: Filing a non-exempt H-1B petition by a dependent/willful-violator employer; placement at a secondary/third-party worksite.
threshold: 90 days before AND 90 days after petition filing (direct) / placement (secondary). "Essentially equivalent" = comparable duties/qualifications in the same area (commuting distance / same MSA).
deadline: Prohibition spans the 180-day window; the secondary inquiry must precede placement.
severityPenalty: Top-tier: CMP up to $9,624 (willful), up to $67,367/violation + ≥3-year debarment where willful failure + displacement.
citation: 20 CFR 655.738(c) (direct, 90/90); 655.738(d) (secondary, inquiry + 90/90); 655.738(b) (definitions: lay off; essentially equivalent job; same-area/MSA test); 655.738(e) (documentation). *(Confirmed verbatim, incl. all four lay-off exclusions and the commuting-distance/MSA test.)*
dataNeeded: Dependency/willful-violator + exempt-only flags; petition filing date; U.S.-worker separations same occupation/area within ±90 days (+ reason codes); secondary-placement flag + date + documented inquiry; essentially-equivalent-job mapping.
implementationNote: 90/90 window = deterministic date math against a separations log. Whether a separated worker held an "essentially equivalent job" and whether a separation is a "lay off" vs an excluded category → NEEDS-COUNSEL per candidate separation. Only fires for non-exempt LCAs of dependent/willful-violator employers.

check: (Dependent/willful-violator, non-exempt LCA) Good-faith industry-standard recruitment of U.S. workers at ≥ required wage; job offered to any equally/better-qualified U.S. applicant; documented in the PAF.
requirement: Non-exempt LCA: take good-faith steps to recruit U.S. workers using industry-wide standard procedures (internal + external + some active recruitment, not lowest-common-denominator), at compensation ≥ required wage, and offer the job to any equally/better-qualified U.S. applicant. Retain documentation; PAF summary.
trigger: Filing a non-exempt H-1B petition/LCA by a dependent/willful-violator employer.
threshold: Recruitment comp ≥ required wage; offer mandatory to any equally/better-qualified U.S. applicant. No fixed ad count; must meet industry norms.
deadline: Recruitment before filing; documentation retained per 655.760; PAF recruitment summary.
severityPenalty: Substantial recruitment failure = $2,364-tier; willful up to $9,624; failure to offer to a qualified U.S. applicant actionable. Debarment 1–2 yrs.
citation: 20 CFR 655.739(e) (industry-wide standards: (e)(1) internal+external, (e)(2) some active); 655.739(f)-(g) (legitimate, non-skewing criteria); 655.739(i)(4) (PAF summary); 655.739(j) (must offer to qualified U.S. applicant, 8 USC 1182(n)(1)(G)(i)(II), DOJ-enforced). *(All paragraph cites confirmed verbatim.)*
dataNeeded: Dependency/exempt flags; recruitment method list with dates/places; compensation offered vs required wage; applicant log + disposition; record of any equally/better-qualified U.S. applicant and whether offered; PAF recruitment summary present.
implementationNote: Presence checks mechanical (comp ≥ required_wage; PAF summary present; applicant log exists). "Industry-wide standards" and "equally/better qualified" (mandatory offer) → NEEDS-COUNSEL. Gate on dependent/willful-violator + non-exempt.

check: A complete PAF assembled within 1 working day of filing, kept at the principal place of business or place of employment.
requirement: Within one working day of filing, make available for public examination a PAF containing: (1) certified LCA + ETA-9035CP (signed printout if electronic); (2) wage-rate documentation; (3) full clear explanation of the actual-wage system; (4) prevailing-wage documentation (source + methodology); (5) union/employee notice documentation; (6) benefits summary; and for H-1B-dependent/willful-violator employers, (9) exempt-worker list and (10) recruitment methods/time-frame summary (plus (7) corporate-change sworn statement and (8) single-employer entity list where applicable).
trigger: Every LCA filing.
threshold: Assembled within 1 WORKING DAY of filing; the enumerated documents (conditional items by status).
deadline: Within one working day after filing.
severityPenalty: $2,364-tier item (impedes DOL oversight).
citation: **20 CFR 655.760(a)** — the introductory text of (a) (1-working-day + location) and items **(a)(1)-(a)(6)** for the six core documents, plus **(a)(9)** (exempt-worker list) and **(a)(10)** (recruitment summary) for dependent/willful-violator employers (and (a)(7) corporate-restructuring, (a)(8) single-employer list). **NOT "(a)(1)-(7)"** — paragraph (a) runs through (a)(10); (a)(7) is the corporate-restructuring sworn statement, not the recruitment summary. *(Original pinpoint range was wrong.)*
dataNeeded: Per LCA: presence/date of each PAF component; PAF assembly date vs filing date; PAF storage location; H-1B-dependent/willful flag (drives (a)(9)/(a)(10)); corporate-change/single-employer flag.
implementationNote: Deterministic completeness + timeliness: flag missing components and assembly_date > filing_date + 1 working day. Dependent/willful components conditionally required. Adequacy of the "full, clear explanation" of the actual-wage system → NEEDS-COUNSEL only if challenged.

check: PAF documents retained 1 year past the period of employment (or LCA expiry/withdrawal); payroll records retained 3 years from creation.
requirement: PAF retained 1 year beyond the last date any H-1B worker is employed under the LCA, or 1 year from expiry/withdrawal if none employed. Payroll/wage records (655.731(b)) retained 3 years from creation. Extended while an enforcement proceeding is pending (payroll).
trigger: End of employment under the LCA / expiry/withdrawal (PAF clock); creation of each payroll record (payroll clock).
threshold: PAF: 1 year beyond end of employment (or expiry/withdrawal). Payroll: 3 years from creation.
deadline: PAF = employment_end + 1yr; payroll = creation + 3yr (later if enforcement pending).
severityPenalty: $2,364-tier item; forfeits documentary defense in an audit.
citation: 20 CFR 655.760(c); cross-ref 655.731(b). *(Confirmed verbatim — both thresholds and the enforcement-extension; note the extension textually attaches to payroll records.)*
dataNeeded: Per LCA: last date a worker was employed / expiry-or-withdrawal date; per payroll record: creation date; open-enforcement flag.
implementationNote: Deterministic retain-until: PAF_retain_until = employment_end + 1yr (or expiry/withdrawal + 1yr); payroll_retain_until = creation + 3yr; extend if investigation_open. Flag records eligible for premature destruction.

check: Map any violation to back wages + the correct CMP tier ($2,364 / $9,624 / $67,367, 2025) + debarment (1/2/3 yrs).
requirement: On a violation, WHD assesses back wages/fringe owed; CMPs tiered (substantial/other-than-willful; willful/misrepresentation/whistleblower; willful + displacement in the 90/90 window). Debarment ≥1/≥2/≥3 years.
trigger: Any sustained violation of an LCA attestation/obligation.
threshold: Back wages: full make-whole. CMP per violation: $2,364 (tier1) / $9,624 (tier2) / $67,367 (tier3) [2025]. Debarment ≥1/≥2/≥3 years.
deadline: Back wages for the full underpayment period; WHD complaint generally within 12 months of the violation (655.806).
severityPenalty: This IS the penalty schedule. Tier turns on willfulness + displacement; back wages mandatory regardless.
citation: **20 CFR 655.810(a)** (back wages); **655.810(b)(1)/(b)(2)/(b)(3)** (CMP tiers); **655.810(d)(1)-(3)** (debarment); INA 212(n)(2) / 8 USC 1182(n)(2) (base $1,000/$5,000/$35,000); complaint limitations **655.806(a)(5)** (12 months). **§655.810 is in SUBPART I, not Subpart H** — use `.../subpart-I/section-655.810`. Current figures are the amounts codified in current **20 CFR 655.810** and confirmed by the DOL WHD Civil Money Penalty table; DOL made **no 2026 inflation adjustment** (91 FR 31358, May 27, 2026), so the 2025 amounts remain in force for 2026. **29 CFR 580 is procedural only, and 29 CFR 578 is FLSA-specific; neither is the H-1B LCA amount source.** *(Original cited 29 CFR 578 and the Subpart-H URL.)*
dataNeeded: Per violation: type; willful flag; displacement-within-90/90 flag; workers affected; underpayment amount + period; good-faith/history factors.
implementationNote: Tier SELECTION mechanical given two booleans (willful?, displacement?): displacement+willful → $67,367/3yr; willful → $9,624/2yr; else → $2,364/1yr. Back-wage amount = arithmetic. WILLFULNESS and the precise back-wage period (esp. the bona-fide-termination cut-off) → NEEDS-COUNSEL. Versioned figures table; refresh annually.

check: PAF contains a copy of the certified LCA (ETA-9035E/9035) + cover pages (ETA-9035CP); if e-filed, a printout signed by the employer.
requirement: Verbatim 20 CFR 655.760(a)(1). Foundational PAF document; required for EVERY certified LCA.
trigger: An LCA has been certified by DOL OFLC.
threshold: Exactly one signed, certified ETA-9035/9035E + ETA-9035CP per LCA. E-filings require a wet/e-signed printout.
deadline: Available for public examination within 1 working day of filing (655.760(a)); retain per 655.760(c).
severityPenalty: Tier 1, 20 CFR 655.810(b)(1)(vi) (~$2,364/violation; conditional "impedes" trigger). Substantive PAF defect.
citation: 20 CFR 655.760(a)(1); penalty 20 CFR 655.810(b)(1)(vi); INA 212(n)(2) / 8 USC 1182(n)(2). *(Confirmed verbatim word-for-word.)*
dataNeeded: lcaId/caseNumber; certifiedLcaDocumentPresent (bool); lcaSignedPrintoutPresent (bool, if e-filed); filingMethod (paper|electronic); eta9035cpCoverPagesPresent (bool); lcaCertificationDate; employerSignaturePresent (bool).
implementationNote: Mechanical presence check. Flag a missing signature on an e-filed printout as a distinct defect. Edge: amended/superseding LCAs each need their own certified copy.

check: PAF contains documentation stating the wage rate to be paid.
requirement: Verbatim 20 CFR 655.760(a)(2). Required for every LCA. Substantively the paid wage must be ≥ greater of actual or prevailing wage (655.731(a)); this item is the statement of the rate.
trigger: An LCA has been certified.
threshold: A stated wage rate (salary or hourly). For PAF-completeness, presence of the wage-rate documentation.
deadline: In PAF within 1 working day of filing (655.760(a)); retain per 655.760(c).
severityPenalty: Tier 1, 655.810(b)(1)(vi). NOTE: an actual UNDERPAYMENT is a separate, more serious wage violation under 655.731 / 655.810(b).
citation: 20 CFR 655.760(a)(2); related 20 CFR 655.731(a); penalty 20 CFR 655.810(b)(1)(vi). *(Confirmed verbatim. Deadline-attribution fix: the 1-working-day timing is in 655.760(a), not (c) — cite (c) only for retention.)*
dataNeeded: wageRateDocPresent (bool); offeredWageAmount; wageUnit (year|hour|month); positionTitle; workerName/id. (Cross-rule: actualWage, prevailingWage.)
implementationNote: Mechanical presence check. Do NOT conflate with wage-sufficiency — keep PAF-presence and wage-floor separate. Wage-sufficiency disputes → NEEDS-COUNSEL; bare presence is mechanical.

check: PAF contains a full, clear explanation of the system used to set the "actual wage" (incl. periodic increases).
requirement: Verbatim 20 CFR 655.760(a)(3) (memo summarizing the system or a copy of the pay scale; payroll records not required but available on enforcement). Required for every LCA. Actual-wage system defined at 655.731(a)(1)/(c)(2).
trigger: An LCA has been certified.
threshold: A written explanation/memo OR pay scale documenting how the actual wage is determined, including periodic increases.
deadline: In PAF within 1 working day of filing; retain per 655.760(c).
severityPenalty: Tier 1, 655.810(b)(1)(vi). Substantive PAF defect.
citation: 20 CFR 655.760(a)(3); actual-wage system 20 CFR 655.731(a)(1) & 655.731(c)(2); penalty 20 CFR 655.810(b)(1)(vi). *(Confirmed verbatim incl. example + parenthetical.)*
dataNeeded: actualWageMemoPresent (bool); actualWageMemoDate; lcaFilingDate; describesPeriodicIncreases (bool); occupation/SOC.
implementationNote: Presence check mechanical; keep the staleness check (memo should not predate the actual-wage determination for the filing — compare actualWageMemoDate vs lcaFilingDate). Whether the memo is "full, clear" vs conclusory → NEEDS-COUNSEL.

check: PAF contains documentation used to establish the prevailing wage (general source + methodology is what must be public; underlying individual data is NOT public but goes to DOL on enforcement).
requirement: Verbatim 20 CFR 655.760(a)(4). Required for every LCA. PW rules at 655.731(a)(2)/(b).
trigger: An LCA has been certified.
threshold: Documentation identifying the PW source (OES/OFLC PWD, independent authoritative survey) AND methodology/level. Source+methodology description suffices for public exam.
deadline: In PAF within 1 working day of filing; retain per 655.760(c).
severityPenalty: Tier 1, 655.810(b)(1)(vi). Substantive PAF defect.
citation: 20 CFR 655.760(a)(4); PW 20 CFR 655.731(a)(2) & 655.731(b); penalty 20 CFR 655.810(b)(1)(vi). *(Confirmed verbatim incl. parenthetical.)*
dataNeeded: prevailingWageDocPresent (bool); pwSource (OES|NPWC-PWD|independentSurvey|CBA|other); pwLevel (I-IV, if OES); pwSOC; pwAmount; pwValidityDates; methodologyDescriptionPresent (bool).
implementationNote: Presence check mechanical. HONESTY BOUNDARY: do NOT require the underlying individual wage data in the PAF (reg expressly excludes it) — requiring it = false positive. Whether an independent survey meets 655.731(b)(3) → NEEDS-COUNSEL; OES/NPWC-PWD source presence is mechanical.

check: PAF contains the document(s) satisfying the union/employee notification of 655.734.
requirement: Verbatim 20 CFR 655.760(a)(5). Required for every LCA. Notice is EITHER to the bargaining rep OR (if none) by posting in two conspicuous locations / electronic notification, on or within 30 days before filing, kept posted 10 days.
trigger: An LCA has been certified; form of notice depends on bargaining-rep existence.
threshold: Unionized: dated copy of notice to the rep. Non-union: copy of the posting showing two locations and posting dates (10-day duration; posted within [filing−30, filing]) OR proof of electronic notification.
deadline: Notice per 655.734 timing; PAF copy available within 1 working day of filing; retain per 655.760(c).
severityPenalty: Tier 1 (and a substantial §655.734 notification failure is independently sanctionable under 655.810(b)(1)(ii)). Most commonly cited LCA violations.
citation: 20 CFR 655.760(a)(5); notice requirement 20 CFR 655.734; penalty 20 CFR 655.810(b)(1)(vi). *(Confirmed verbatim incl. "of this part." Note: the legacy "notice_to_employees" key is NOT a separate (a)(5) item — collapse them.)*
dataNeeded: noticeDocPresent (bool); noticeType (unionNotice|physicalPosting|electronic); postingStartDate; postingEndDate; postingLocationsCount (int); lcaFilingDate; hasBargainingRepresentative (bool); worksiteAddress.
implementationNote: Two-branch: (a) presence of a notice document; (b) if physical posting, validate postingStartDate within [filing−30, filing], duration ≥10 days, locationsCount ≥2. Implement the date/location validation, not just presence. Whether a novel electronic method satisfies 655.734(b) → NEEDS-COUNSEL.

check: PAF contains a summary of benefits offered to U.S. workers in the same occupational classifications, with a differentiation statement and a home-country-benefits statement where applicable.
requirement: Verbatim 20 CFR 655.760(a)(6) (proprietary cost/stock-option details may be omitted; home-country-benefits statement where applicable, see 655.731(c)(3)). Required for every LCA.
trigger: An LCA has been certified.
threshold: A benefits summary for the occupational classification + a differentiation statement if benefits vary + (if applicable) a home-country statement.
deadline: In PAF within 1 working day of filing; retain per 655.760(c).
severityPenalty: Tier 1, 655.810(b)(1)(vi). (A failure to OFFER equivalent benefits is a separate substantive wage/benefit violation.)
citation: 20 CFR 655.760(a)(6); benefits-parity 20 CFR 655.731(c)(3); penalty 20 CFR 655.810(b)(1)(vi). *(Confirmed verbatim incl. the "(see § 655.731(c)(3))" parenthetical.)*
dataNeeded: benefitsSummaryPresent (bool); differentiationStatementPresent (bool, only if benefits differ); homeCountryBenefitsStatementPresent (bool, if applicable); occupation/SOC; benefitsDifferAcrossEmployees (bool).
implementationNote: Presence check mechanical for the summary; differentiation statement conditionally required (if benefitsDifferAcrossEmployees). Whether actual benefits are "equivalent" (655.731(c)(3)) → NEEDS-COUNSEL.

check: On a change in corporate structure, PAF contains a sworn statement by a responsible official of the new entity accepting all predecessor-LCA obligations, plus a list of each affected LCA + certification date, and the new entity's actual-wage system + FEIN.
requirement: Verbatim 20 CFR 655.760(a)(7). CONDITIONAL — applies only on a corporate-structure change (merger/acquisition/reorganization) where the successor relies on predecessor LCAs.
trigger: Corporate-structure change while H-1B workers are employed under existing LCAs and the successor relies on them.
threshold: One sworn statement signed by a responsible official of the NEW entity + list of all affected LCAs with certification dates + new actual-wage-system description + new FEIN.
deadline: Placed in the PAF before the new entity employs H-1B workers under predecessor LCAs (655.730(e)(1)) — *(this "before employing" framing is a structural inference, not a verbatim deadline phrase)*; retain per 655.760(c).
severityPenalty: Tier 1, 655.810(b)(1)(vi). Conditional substantive defect; failure can also undermine the successor's ability to rely on predecessor LCAs.
citation: 20 CFR 655.760(a)(7); successor-in-interest mechanics 20 CFR 655.730(e)(1); penalty 20 CFR 655.810(b)(1)(vi). *(Confirmed verbatim incl. the parenthetical cross-reference.)*
dataNeeded: corporateStructureChangeOccurred (bool); successorSwornStatementPresent (bool); statementSignedByResponsibleOfficial (bool); affectedLcaList (array of {lcaId, certificationDate}); newEntityActualWageSystemDescribed (bool); newEntityFEIN; changeEffectiveDate.
implementationNote: Gate on corporateStructureChangeOccurred — false ⇒ N/A (not a violation). When true, validate all four components. Whether a transaction is a "change in corporate structure" (vs a new-employer situation needing fresh LCAs) → NEEDS-COUNSEL; component-presence checks mechanical once triggered.

check: If the employer used the IRC "single employer" definition to determine H-1B-dependency, PAF contains a list of all entities included in that determination.
requirement: Verbatim 20 CFR 655.760(a)(8). CONDITIONAL — applies only when the employer aggregates affiliated entities under the IRC single-employer test (IRC 414(b),(c),(m),(o)) to compute dependency.
trigger: The employer used IRC single-employer aggregation to determine H-1B-dependency.
threshold: A written list of every entity treated as part of the single employer. (Dependency thresholds: ≤25 FTE → >7; 26-50 → >12; 51+ → ≥15% — 655.736(a)(1)(i)-(iii).)
deadline: In PAF within 1 working day of filing; retain per 655.760(c).
severityPenalty: Tier 1, 655.810(b)(1)(vi). Conditional documentation defect.
citation: 20 CFR 655.760(a)(8); single-employer/dependency 20 CFR 655.736(d)(7) & 655.736(a)(1)(i)-(iii); penalty 20 CFR 655.810(b)(1)(vi). *(Confirmed verbatim; note the reg text contains an in-source scrivener typo "§ 766.760" meaning 655.760 — not a defect in this rule. Dependency-threshold pinpoint sharpened to (a)(1)(i)-(iii).)*
dataNeeded: usedIrcSingleEmployerDefinition (bool); singleEmployerEntityListPresent (bool); entitiesInSingleEmployer (array); employerFteCount; h1bWorkerCount; dependencyStatus.
implementationNote: Gate on usedIrcSingleEmployerDefinition. **This item is MISSING from the live 8-key set — add it.** Whether the IRC aggregation was correctly applied → NEEDS-COUNSEL; list-presence mechanical once indicated.

check: If H-1B-dependent and/or a willful violator AND the LCA(s) indicate only "exempt" workers, PAF contains a list of those exempt workers.
requirement: Verbatim 20 CFR 655.760(a)(9). CONDITIONAL — only for dependent employers / willful violators claiming the exempt exception. Exempt = ≥$60,000/yr OR master's-or-higher in a related specialty (INA 212(n)(3); 655.737).
trigger: Dependent/willful-violator employer + LCA attests only exempt workers (to avoid non-displacement/recruitment attestations).
threshold: A list naming each exempt worker. $60,000 is the statutory threshold, NOT inflation-adjusted (655.737(b)/(c)).
deadline: In PAF within 1 working day of filing; retain per 655.760(c).
severityPenalty: Tier 1, 655.810(b)(1)(vi). A false exemption claim can escalate to substantive 655.738/.739 violations (higher tiers).
citation: 20 CFR 655.760(a)(9); exempt-worker list/definition 20 CFR 655.737(e)(1) & 655.737(b)-(c); INA 212(n)(3); penalty 20 CFR 655.810(b)(1)(vi). *(Confirmed verbatim; $60,000 confirmed statutory/fixed — changing it would require new legislation.)*
dataNeeded: h1bDependentOrWillfulViolator (bool); lcaIndicatesExemptOnly (bool); exemptWorkerListPresent (bool); exemptWorkers (array of {workerId, basis, wageAmount, degreeLevel, degreeField}).
implementationNote: Gate on (h1bDependentOrWillfulViolator AND lcaIndicatesExemptOnly). **This item is MISSING from the live 8-key set — add it.** Validate each listed worker meets an exemption basis (wage ≥ $60k or qualifying advanced degree). $60,000 is fixed (do not inflation-adjust). Degree "in a related specialty" → NEEDS-COUNSEL; wage-based ≥$60k is mechanical.

check: If H-1B-dependent or willful violator (and NOT relying solely on exempt workers for the LCA), PAF contains a summary of recruitment methods + time frames of U.S.-worker recruitment.
requirement: Verbatim 20 CFR 655.760(a)(10) (or copies of pertinent documents). CONDITIONAL — for dependent/willful-violator employers employing non-exempt workers. Supports the 212(n)(1)(G) good-faith-recruitment attestation.
trigger: Dependent/willful-violator employer + LCA covering non-exempt workers (655.739 recruitment attestation).
threshold: A summary documenting recruitment methods AND time frames, or copies of pertinent documents.
deadline: In PAF within 1 working day of filing; retain per 655.760(c). (Underlying recruitment precedes/accompanies filing per 655.739.)
severityPenalty: Tier 1 for the PAF-documentation failure; a substantive recruitment/non-displacement failure (655.738/.739) is Tier 2/3 (up to ~$9,624 / ~$67,367) + possible debarment.
citation: 20 CFR 655.760(a)(10); recruitment attestation 20 CFR 655.739(i)(4) & 655.739; non-displacement 20 CFR 655.738; INA 212(n)(1)(G); penalty 20 CFR 655.810(b)(1)(vi),(b)(2),(b)(3). *(Confirmed verbatim — the unbalanced trailing parenthesis after "(4)" is in the actual regulation.)*
dataNeeded: h1bDependentOrWillfulViolator (bool); employsNonExemptH1b (bool); recruitmentSummaryPresent (bool); recruitmentMethods (array); recruitmentTimeFrames (date ranges); lcaId; recruitmentDocsPresent (bool).
implementationNote: Gate on (h1bDependentOrWillfulViolator AND employsNonExemptH1b). Presence/contents (methods + time frames) mechanical; whether recruitment was "good faith" / met industry-wide standards → NEEDS-COUNSEL.

check: The PAF (LCA + supporting docs) assembled and available for public examination no later than 1 working day after the LCA is filed.
requirement: Verbatim 20 CFR 655.760(a) (assembly deadline for the ENTIRE PAF; applies to every LCA and to H-1B1/E-3 per the opening note).
trigger: An LCA (ETA-9035/9035E) is filed with DOL OFLC.
threshold: 1 working day after filing ("working day" excludes weekends and federal holidays).
deadline: filingDate + 1 working day.
severityPenalty: Tier 1, 655.810(b)(1)(vi). Technical-to-substantive depending on duration of unavailability.
citation: 20 CFR 655.760(a); penalty 20 CFR 655.810(b)(1)(vi); DOL WHD Fact Sheet #62F. *(Confirmed.)*
dataNeeded: lcaFilingDate; pafAssembledDate (or pafFirstAvailableDate); businessCalendar (working days, excluding federal holidays + weekends).
implementationNote: Mechanical date-difference: assert (pafAvailableDate − filingDate) ≤ 1 working day. Anchor on the FILING date, not certification. If pafAssembledDate unknown, render "unavailable" rather than assume compliance.

check: PAF records retained 1 year beyond the last date any H-1B worker is employed under the LCA — or, if none employed, 1 year from LCA expiration/withdrawal.
requirement: Verbatim 20 CFR 655.760(c). Applies to every LCA.
trigger: An LCA exists; retention clock starts at last day of H-1B employment under it (or expiry/withdrawal if unused).
threshold: 1 year (365 days) past last-employment-date under the LCA, OR 1 year past expiry/withdrawal if unused.
deadline: retentionEnd; do not destroy before this date.
severityPenalty: Tier 1, 655.810(b)(1)(vi). Premature destruction = recordkeeping violation.
citation: 20 CFR 655.760(c); penalty 20 CFR 655.810(b)(1)(vi); DOL WHD Fact Sheet #62F. *(Confirmed verbatim.)*
dataNeeded: lcaId; lastH1bEmploymentDateUnderLca (nullable); lcaExpiryDate; lcaWithdrawalDate (nullable); anyH1bEmployedUnderLca (bool); pafRecordsRetainedThroughDate; pafStorageLocation.
implementationNote: retentionEnd = if anyH1bEmployedUnderLca then lastH1bEmploymentDateUnderLca + 1yr else min(lcaExpiryDate, lcaWithdrawalDate) + 1yr. Flag a violation only if records destroyed/missing before retentionEnd. Distinguish from the 3-year payroll rule. "Last date employed under the LCA" for a worker on multiple LCAs → NEEDS-COUNSEL.

check: Payroll records for H-1B employees AND comparator employees in the same occupational classification retained 3 years from creation (indefinitely if enforcement commenced).
requirement: Verbatim 20 CFR 655.760(c). Payroll records are NOT part of the public-examination file but ARE part of required retention. Applies to every LCA.
trigger: Payroll records created for H-1B workers and comparator U.S. workers under an LCA.
threshold: 3 years (1,095 days) from each record's creation; extended indefinitely if a WHD enforcement action is commenced.
deadline: recordCreationDate + 3 years per record; hold until enforcement complete if commenced.
severityPenalty: Tier 1, 655.810(b)(1)(vi). Impedes back-wage/enforcement determinations.
citation: 20 CFR 655.760(c); content of payroll records 20 CFR 655.731(b)(1); penalty 20 CFR 655.810(b)(1)(vi). *(Confirmed verbatim.)*
dataNeeded: payrollRecordCreationDates (per record); payrollRecordsRetainedThroughDate; occupationalClassification; comparatorEmployeesCovered (bool); enforcementActionCommenced (bool); enforcementActionCloseDate (nullable).
implementationNote: Per-record retentionEnd = creationDate + 3yr, overridden by open enforcement. IMPORTANT: payroll records are NOT a public-access-file item but ARE a 655.760(c) retention obligation — keep separate from PAF-completeness. The 3-year clock is per-record (rolling), not a single file-level date.

check: The PAF is located at the principal place of business in the U.S. OR at the place of employment, and a member of the public may examine it (transcription/scanning/photograph; copies need not be provided).
requirement: Location per 20 CFR 655.760(a). Access method per DOL WHD Fact Sheet #62F: must permit capture by transcription, scanning, or photographs; no requirement to provide copies. Applies to every LCA.
trigger: An LCA is filed; the public-examination obligation attaches through the retention period.
threshold: Location ∈ {principal place of business in U.S., place of employment}. Access: must permit transcription/scanning/photography on request; no mailing/handing-over of copies.
deadline: Available within 1 working day of filing; maintained through the 655.760(c) retention period.
severityPenalty: Tier 1, 655.810(b)(1)(vi). Refusing public examination / storing where the public cannot reach it directly triggers (b)(1)(vi).
citation: 20 CFR 655.760(a) (location); DOL WHD Fact Sheet #62F (access method); penalty 20 CFR 655.810(b)(1)(vi). *(Confirmed.)*
dataNeeded: pafStorageLocationType (principalPlaceOfBusiness|placeOfEmployment|other); pafAddress; publicExaminationProcessDocumented (bool); allowsTranscriptionScanPhoto (bool); worksiteAddresses (for multi-site).
implementationNote: Largely a policy/config attestation: verify location is one of the two permitted categories and the process permits public capture. Remote/distributed worksites ("where is the place of employment for a remote worker?") → NEEDS-COUNSEL. Surface the "no copies required, but must allow capture" nuance explicitly.

check: For H-1B1 (Chile/Singapore) and E-3 (Australia) workers, the PAF applies but only items (a)(1)-(a)(6) + paragraphs (b) and (c) — the dependent/willful items (a)(7)-(a)(10) do NOT apply.
requirement: Verbatim opening note of 20 CFR 655.760: "Paragraphs (a)(1) thru (a)(6) and paragraphs (b) and (c) of this section also apply to the H-1B1 and E-3 visa categories." Dependency/recruitment/non-displacement attestations do not apply to those categories.
trigger: The worker is in H-1B1 or E-3 status rather than H-1B.
threshold: Required PAF items for H-1B1/E-3 = {(a)(1)..(a)(6)} + retention (c). Items (a)(7)-(a)(10) = N/A.
deadline: Same 1-working-day assembly + 1-year/3-year retention as H-1B.
severityPenalty: Same penalty regime via INA 212(t). Misapplying dependent items to H-1B1/E-3 would produce false positives — this rule prevents that.
citation: 20 CFR 655.760 (opening applicability note); INA 212(t) / 8 USC 1182(t). *(Confirmed verbatim.)*
dataNeeded: visaCategory (H-1B|H-1B1|E-3); workerId; lcaId.
implementationNote: SCOPING/selector rule, not a document check: when visaCategory ∈ {H-1B1, E-3}, evaluate only paf.item1-6 + retention and suppress paf.item7-10 (and the dependency/recruitment rule families) as N/A. Confirm the actual classification from the petition/LCA, not from assumption.

check: Paid wage ≥ greater of (actual wage, prevailing wage) for the entire period of authorized employment.
requirement: Attest on the LCA to pay the "required wage rate" = greater of (1) actual wage to others with similar experience/qualifications for the specific employment, or (2) prevailing wage for the occupation in the area. Runs for the full authorized-employment period.
trigger: Any certified LCA with one or more H-1B/H-1B1/E-3 workers in pay status.
threshold: paid_wage ≥ MAX(actual_wage, prevailing_wage). No de minimis — any underpayment is a violation.
deadline: Continuous, entire authorized-employment period.
severityPenalty: Substantive wage violation. Back wages (655.810(a)). CMP up to $2,364 (substantial) / $9,624 (willful); debarment ≥1 yr.
dataNeeded: Per worker: actual gross wage paid; pay frequency; actual_wage benchmark; prevailing_wage; LCA validity start/end; FT/PT; hours.
implementationNote: Deterministic compare: required = max(actual, prevailing); flag if paid < required. Normalize to a common period before comparing. PT → compare prorated hourly (see parttime.proration). Piece-rate/commission → convert to an effective period rate.

check: Documented, consistently-applied actual-wage system; H-1B paid ≥ similarly-employed in-house workers (after legitimate factors).
requirement: "Actual wage" = the rate paid to all individuals with experience/qualifications SIMILAR to the H-1B worker, for the SPECIFIC EMPLOYMENT at the place of employment. Pay differences only on legitimate business factors (experience, qualifications, education, job responsibility, specialized knowledge, performance/productivity, geographic location). If no other employees hold the position, actual wage = the H-1B worker's wage.
trigger: Any H-1B worker whose classification is also held by other employees at the same worksite.
threshold: H-1B paid ≥ the actual wage from the documented system for a worker of that experience/qualifications. Differences must trace to enumerated legitimate factors.
deadline: System exists at filing; documentation retained per 655.760.
severityPenalty: Substantive if H-1B below in-house comparators without a legitimate basis (disguised underpayment). Back wages + CMP per 655.810.
citation: 20 CFR 655.731(a)(1); documentation 20 CFR 655.731(b).
dataNeeded: Roster of all employees in the same title/classification with wage, experience years, education, documented differential factor(s); the H-1B worker's experience/education; written actual-wage methodology.
implementationNote: Partly mechanical (compare H-1B wage to the min paid to an equal-or-lesser-experience comparator). Whether a differential is justified by a "legitimate business factor" → NEEDS-COUNSEL (esp. subjective factors like "performance"). Build as: detect H-1B-below-comparator → raise review flag; do not auto-conclude.

check: Retains a memo/documentation describing the actual-wage system and how the H-1B wage relates to others.
requirement: Establish the actual wage and RETAIN documentation specifying the basis — a written explanation of the system/factors, showing how the H-1B wage relates to others with similar experience/qualifications.
trigger: Every LCA (public-access/payroll documentation must support the actual-wage attestation).
threshold: Existence + adequacy of the actual-wage memo.
deadline: Retained per 655.760(c) (generally 1 year beyond the employment/validity period).
severityPenalty: Recordkeeping failure (technical) if missing but wages correct; becomes substantive if it masks underpayment. Supports CMP; frequent WHD finding.
citation: 20 CFR 655.731(b); retention 20 CFR 655.760(c). *(Re-verify the exact (b)(1)/(b)(2) sub-letter against current eCFR when wiring the citation string.)*
dataNeeded: Boolean: actual-wage memo present; date; whether it identifies the wage-setting factors and ties to payroll.
implementationNote: Mechanical presence/absence against a document store. Cannot judge adequacy → NEEDS-COUNSEL for adequacy; auto-flag only on absence.

check: The prevailing wage was obtained from one of the four permitted sources.
requirement: Set PW using ONE of: (i) an arm's-length CBA rate (controls if covered); (ii) an OFLC NPWC PWD (arithmetic mean of similarly-employed workers, OES/OEWS unless an acceptable employer survey); (iii) an independent authoritative survey; or (iv) the DBA/SCA wage for covered contracts. For H-1B: (a) NPWC PWD, (b) independent authoritative survey, or (c) another legitimate source.
trigger: Every LCA — a PW value + source selected and documented before filing.
threshold: Source ∈ the four enumerated types; CBA controls where applicable; DBA/SCA controls on covered contracts.
deadline: Source/PWD valid as of filing; documentation retained per 655.760.
severityPenalty: Substantive if an invalid source understated the PW (→ underpayment, back wages, CMP). Using an unqualified survey is itself an attestation violation.
dataNeeded: PW source type enum (NPWC_PWD | CBA | independent_survey | DBA | SCA); source document/ID; PW value; SOC + area.
implementationNote: Mechanical: validate the source enum is allowed and the supporting document exists. Survey qualification governed by the survey-criteria rule; whether a CBA covers the occupation → NEEDS-COUNSEL.

check: On a wage challenge, confirm whether the employer obtained and properly applied an NPWC PWD (safe harbor).
requirement: If the employer obtains an NPWC PWD, files the LCA, and pays per the PWD, WHD will not challenge the PW validity in an enforcement action — provided the PWD was applied properly (correct occupation, area, and skill/wage level). Does not immunize misclassification of level/occupation/area.
trigger: Wage-compliance investigation where the employer relied on an NPWC PWD.
threshold: Safe harbor only if occupation, area, AND wage level were all correctly applied.
deadline: n/a (defensive posture).
severityPenalty: n/a (a shield). Loss of safe harbor (wrong level/SOC/area) reopens PW back-wage liability.
citation: 20 CFR 655.731(a)(2)(ii)(A); 20 CFR 655.731(d) (PWD reliance).
dataNeeded: PWD present?; PWD SOC, area, level vs the actual job's SOC/area/level; wage paid vs PWD wage.
implementationNote: Mechanical cross-check: does the PWD's SOC/area/level match the position as staffed? Divergence (esp. level) → surface safe-harbor-at-risk. Mechanical anchor for the Level-1-on-senior-role red flag below.

check: Any employer-provided/independent survey for the PW meets all regulatory validity criteria.
requirement: An independent authoritative survey (or "other legitimate source") must: (1) reflect the arithmetic mean (or weighted average; or median where only a median is provided); (2) be for the SAME occupation; (3) be in the area of intended employment; (4) be based on data collected within 24 months of publication; AND (5) the edition used must have been published within the 24-month period immediately preceding filing. For "other legitimate source," data also latest and across-industry unless the job is in that industry.
trigger: LCA where the PW source is an employer-provided/independent survey.
threshold: Published within 24 months before filing; data collected within 24 months before publication; mean (or median) of similarly-employed workers in the occupation and area.
deadline: Currency measured at the filing date.
severityPenalty: Substantive: an invalid survey understating the PW → underpayment, back wages, CMP.
dataNeeded: Survey publication date; data-collection date; statistic type (mean/median/weighted avg); occupation + geographic + industry scope; LCA filing date.
implementationNote: Largely mechanical date math: (filing − publication) ≤ 24mo AND (publication − data_collection) ≤ 24mo AND statistic ∈ {mean, weighted_avg, median}. Whether the survey's occupation/area "matches" the job → NEEDS-COUNSEL; auto-fail on the date/statistic checks.

check: The wage level (I-IV) on the PWD matches the position's MINIMUM requirements per the OFLC 5-factor worksheet.
requirement: Every OES-based determination STARTS at Level I and adjusts upward via a 5-step worksheet comparing the EMPLOYER'S MINIMUM requirements against O*NET norms: Step 1 Level I baseline; Step 2 +1 if experience exceeds the SVP norm; Step 3 +1 if education exceeds the usual; Step 4 +1 for special skills/licenses beyond the norm; Step 5 +1 for supervisory duties. Levels map to OES percentiles: I=17th, II=34th, III=50th, IV=67th. Set from the position's MINIMUM requirements, not the incumbent's actual credentials.
trigger: Every NPWC OES PWD request (ETA-9141) and every LCA citing an OES-based PW.
threshold: I=17th, II=34th, III=50th, IV=67th percentile; worksheet adds at most ~one level per factor; start at I.
deadline: Determined at PWD issuance; binds the LCA filed within validity.
severityPenalty: Substantive if an understated level produced a below-level PW → underpayment, back wages, CMP; forfeits NPWC safe harbor.
citation: 20 CFR 655.731(a)(2)(ii)(A); DOL OFLC Prevailing Wage Determination Policy Guidance (rev. Nov 2009).
dataNeeded: Position SOC + O*NET Job Zone/SVP; minimum required experience years; minimum education; required special skills/licenses; supervises?; PWD's stated level + percentile; OES wage per level for that SOC/area.
implementationNote: Worksheet partly reproducible deterministically (start at I; +1 per factor exceeding the O*NET norm), but "exceeds the usual" needs O*NET data + judgment → implement as an ADVISORY level-estimator; flag NEEDS-COUNSEL where the estimate diverges from the filed level by ≥1. The percentile-to-level mapping is in active rulemaking (March 2026 proposed rule) — gate the percentile constants behind a wage-year/version flag.

check: AUDIT RED FLAG — a low wage level (esp. Level I) attested for a senior/complex/supervisory title or one whose stated requirements imply seniority.
requirement: A Level I ("entry," routine tasks under close supervision) wage attested for a role that is senior/lead/architect/principal/managerial — or carries elevated experience/education/supervisory requirements — is internally inconsistent and a recognized indicator of PW understatement. Same for Level II on a clearly senior role.
trigger: LCA/PWD where the level is low (I or II) but title/seniority/required experience/supervisory scope indicate higher.
threshold: Heuristic: Level I with (title contains senior/lead/principal/staff/architect/manager/director) OR (min experience ≥ ~3-5 yrs) OR (supervisory=true) OR (advanced degree required for a non-entry role) → flag.
deadline: Detect at filing and on audit.
severityPenalty: Risk indicator, not a per-se violation: signals probable PW underpayment (substantive, back wages + CMP) + loss of safe harbor; primary WHD/audit trigger.
citation: 20 CFR 655.731(a)(2); DOL OFLC PW Determination Policy Guidance (rev. Nov 2009) (level definitions).
dataNeeded: Wage level on LCA; job title text; seniority keywords; min experience years; supervisory flag; required degree level; the SOC's typical level distribution.
implementationNote: Mechanical heuristic scorer producing a RISK FLAG (not a verdict): title-keyword match + experience threshold + supervisory flag. Route hits to human/counsel. Always flag NEEDS-COUNSEL before any adverse conclusion — level adequacy is a legal/factual judgment.

check: The LCA was filed while its supporting NPWC PWD was within the PWD validity window.
requirement: An NPWC PWD specifies a validity period ≥90 days and ≤1 year (365 days) from determination. To rely on the safe harbor, file the LCA (or, for PERM, file/begin recruitment) during that window. Once filed within validity, the LCA remains valid for its certified period.
trigger: Any LCA citing an NPWC PWD.
threshold: 90 ≤ PWD validity ≤ 365 days; filing date ∈ [determination date, expiration date].
deadline: LCA filed on/before the PWD expiration date.
severityPenalty: Loss of safe harbor / invalid PW basis if filed after expiry; exposes to PW challenge + back wages.
citation: 20 CFR 655.731(a)(2)(ii)(A); DOL OFLC NPWC guidance (validity period).
dataNeeded: PWD determination/issue date; PWD expiration date; LCA filing date.
implementationNote: Pure date-window check: LCA_filing_date ≤ PWD_expiration_date AND validity length ∈ [90,365] days. Trivial deterministic evaluator.

check: On the July-1 OES refresh, do not require a new PWD for an already-filed LCA, but recheck new filings against updated data.
requirement: OFLC updates OES/OEWS data once per year, effective July 1 (wage year July 1–June 30). Once an LCA is filed within a PWD's validity, no new PWD is required when data updates; the LCA remains valid. PWD requests and LCAs filed on/after July 1 use the refreshed figures.
trigger: The annual July-1 update; any new PWD/LCA after that date.
threshold: Effective July 1; pre-existing certified LCAs grandfathered; new filings use new data.
deadline: July 1 annually.
severityPenalty: Operational/data-currency. Stale (pre-July-1) data on a NEW filing understates the PW → potential underpayment. Grandfathered LCAs are not violations because the survey later rose.
citation: 20 CFR 655.731(a)(2)(ii) (OES survey); OFLC OEWS wage-year update (effective July 1).
dataNeeded: LCA filing date vs the active wage-year boundary (July 1); cited wage-data vintage; PWD validity dates.
implementationNote: Mechanical: maintain a wage-year calendar (July 1–June 30). Assert the cited OES vintage matches the wage year of the filing date. Suppress "stale data" flags for already-certified LCAs (grandfathered). Refresh embedded OES tables every July 1.

check: H-1B workers offered benefits + eligibility on the same basis/criteria as U.S. workers.
requirement: Offer benefits and ELIGIBILITY (provided as compensation) on the SAME BASIS / SAME CRITERIA as U.S. workers. Covered: cash bonuses; stock options/non-cash comp; paid vacations/holidays; health/life/disability/other insurance; retirement/savings. May not deny on "temporary"-status grounds. Home/host-country election rules apply for temporary assignments.
trigger: Any H-1B worker; compared against similarly-situated U.S. workers.
threshold: Same basis + same criteria (waiting periods, vesting, match, plan access); no "temporary-status" carve-out.
deadline: Throughout the period of employment.
severityPenalty: Substantive benefits violation. WHD may assess back fringe benefits (655.810(a)) + CMP.
dataNeeded: Benefit-plan eligibility rules U.S. workers vs the H-1B worker (waiting periods, plan tiers, bonus eligibility, equity, PTO accrual, 401k match); actual enrollment/offer.
implementationNote: Partly mechanical (compare waiting periods, match %, PTO accrual). "Same basis/criteria" across heterogeneous plans → NEEDS-COUNSEL. Auto-flag clear disparities (e.g., H-1B excluded from a plan U.S. peers get).

check: Required wage paid "cash in hand, free and clear, when due" — net of only authorized deductions.
requirement: Pay CASH IN HAND, FREE AND CLEAR, WHEN DUE — legal tender/negotiable instrument, at period close, no kickback. Only 655.731(c)(9) deductions may reduce below the required wage. Report as earnings with proper IRS/FICA withholding. Pay at least as frequently as the prevailing practice / at least monthly.
trigger: Every pay period for every H-1B worker.
threshold: Net cash (after only authorized deductions) ≥ required wage for the period; paid no later than when due (at least monthly).
deadline: Each regular payday; "when due."
severityPenalty: Substantive wage violation (kickbacks, late pay, unauthorized deductions dropping below required wage) → back wages + CMP.
citation: 20 CFR 655.731(c)(7); cash-wage documentation 20 CFR 655.731(c)(8)/(c)(12). *(Re-verify (c)(7)/(c)(8) sub-letters against current eCFR; WHD Fact Sheet 62G corroborates.)*
dataNeeded: Per period: gross pay; each deduction line + reason code; net cash paid; pay date vs period-end; pay frequency; IRS/FICA withholding evidence.
implementationNote: Mechanical: net_after_authorized_deductions ≥ required_wage_for_period AND pay_date ≤ due_date. Requires the deduction-classification rule to separate authorized from unauthorized.

check: Wage obligation begins no later than 30 days after admission (or 60 days after becoming eligible if already in the U.S.).
requirement: Obligation begins when the worker "enters into employment," but no later than 30 days after first admission pursuant to the petition, or 60 days after becoming eligible to work if already present (COS). Enters into employment = first available for work / under employer control (orientation, etc.).
trigger: New H-1B worker post-admission or post-eligibility; non-payment during the initial window.
threshold: Pay starts by min(actual entry, admission+30) or by eligibility+60 (if already in U.S.).
deadline: 30 days (consular) / 60 days (in-US COS).
severityPenalty: Substantive wage violation / benching if unpaid past the trigger → back wages from the start date + CMP.
citation: 20 CFR 655.731(c)(6); DOL WHD Fact Sheet #62G. *(Re-verify (c)(6) sub-letter against current eCFR; Fact Sheet 62G confirms the 30/60-day rule substantively.)*
dataNeeded: US admission date (I-94); work-eligibility date (COS); first entered-employment date; first paycheck date.
implementationNote: Mechanical: required_pay_start = consular ? min(entered_employment, admission+30) : min(entered_employment, eligibility+60); flag if first_pay_date > required_pay_start.

check: Full required wage paid during employment-related nonproductive time (no "benching").
requirement: Pay the required wage for ALL nonproductive time caused by conditions RELATED TO EMPLOYMENT (lack of work, lack of permit/license, waiting for a project, studying for a licensing exam). FT → full guaranteed hours; PT → ≥ the LCA/petition hours. NOT required for nonproductive time due to conditions UNRELATED to employment at the worker's voluntary request/convenience or rendering them unable to work — UNLESS otherwise owed under the benefit plan or law (e.g., FMLA). Failing to pay benched time is a per-se violation.
trigger: Any pay period a worker is nonproductive but still employed and not bona-fide-terminated.
threshold: Full required wage for employment-related nonproductive time; PT ≥ LCA hours.
deadline: Each pay period during the nonproductive status.
severityPenalty: Substantive ("benching") → back wages for the unpaid period + CMP; common WHD target.
citation: 20 CFR 655.731(c)(7)(i)-(ii); DOL WHD Fact Sheet #62I.
dataNeeded: Per period: hours/wage paid; employment status (active vs bona-fide-terminated with USCIS notification + return-transportation); nonproductivity reason (employment-related vs voluntary); LCA FT/PT hours range.
implementationNote: Mechanical for the "still employed + zero/low pay" detection; classifying CAUSE (employment-related vs voluntary/personal) and whether a bona fide termination occurred → NEEDS-COUNSEL. A valid bona fide termination (notify USCIS + offer return transport) ends the obligation — check for it before flagging benching.

check: PT H-1B workers paid the required wage for hours worked, and ≥ the LCA-stated minimum hours.
requirement: For PT, pay the required wage for the hours actually worked, and for at least the petition/LCA hours (the LCA states a range or number). The required HOURLY wage governs; may not be paid for fewer hours than the LCA minimum.
trigger: Any H-1B worker designated PT on the LCA/petition.
threshold: hours_paid ≥ LCA_minimum_hours; hourly_rate_paid ≥ required_hourly_wage.
deadline: Each pay period.
severityPenalty: Substantive if below the hourly required wage or LCA minimum hours → back wages + CMP.
citation: 20 CFR 655.731(c)(7)(ii); 20 CFR 655.731(a) (required hourly wage). *(Re-verify the PT sub-letter against current eCFR.)*
dataNeeded: LCA FT/PT flag; LCA stated hours (min/max or specific); hours paid per period; hourly required wage (PW & actual converted to hourly).
implementationNote: Mechanical: hours_paid ≥ lca_min_hours AND effective_hourly ≥ required_hourly. Convert annual PW/actual to hourly using the PWD hours basis (commonly 2,080/yr).

check: Every deduction reducing an H-1B worker below the required wage falls within an authorized category.
requirement: A deduction may reduce below the required wage ONLY if: (i) required by law (taxes, FICA, court-ordered garnishments); OR (ii) CBA-authorized, or reasonable-and-customary (union dues, employee insurance premiums); OR (iii) voluntary meeting ALL of: (A) written + voluntary, (B) NOT a business-expense recoupment, (C) principally for the employee's benefit, (D) ≤ fair market value/actual cost, (E) within FLSA limits / not below the required wage inconsistently. Any deduction failing its category is unauthorized; the shortfall is owed as back wages.
trigger: Any deduction beyond ordinary tax/withholding, esp. recovery of costs/fees/equipment/training/relocation.
threshold: Voluntary deductions ≤ FMV/actual cost; not a business-expense recoupment; within FLSA limits / not below the required wage except as (c)(9) permits.
deadline: Each pay period.
severityPenalty: Substantive for unauthorized deductions → back wages = unauthorized amount + CMP. Certain prohibited charges carry specific CMP exposure.
dataNeeded: Per deduction line: reason code/description; amount; written-authorization (bool); whether it recoups an employer-benefiting cost; FMV/actual-cost reference; net wage vs required wage.
implementationNote: Mechanical for category (i) (tax/garnishment whitelist) and the net-wage floor; "principally for the benefit of the employee" and "business-expense recoupment" → NEEDS-COUNSEL for any non-tax, non-CBA deduction. Build a reason-code taxonomy → authorized/prohibited/needs-review.

check: Employer H-1B business expenses (LCA/petition attorney fees, the ACWIA fee) NOT deducted from or shifted to the worker below the required wage.
requirement: Deductions/required payments recouping the EMPLOYER'S BUSINESS EXPENSES are prohibited where they bring the wage below the required wage. These include: the employer's attorney fees and LCA/petition prep/filing costs; AND the ACWIA training/scholarship fee under INA 214(c)(9) ($1,500 for ≥26 FTE; $750 for ≤25 FTE) — non-recoupable even voluntarily. The $500 fraud-prevention fee is likewise the employer's expense.
trigger: Any deduction/required reimbursement/worker payment tied to immigration-process costs.
threshold: ACWIA fee $1,500 (≥26 FTE) / $750 (≤25 FTE) — never charged to worker. LCA/petition attorney fees & costs — not chargeable if it drops pay below required wage. $500 fraud fee — employer expense.
deadline: At the time of any such deduction/payment.
severityPenalty: Substantive + enumerated: charging the ACWIA fee or LCA/petition costs is specifically actionable; back wages (restore the amount) + CMP up to $2,364 (the worker-paid-fee category is expressly listed among CMP-eligible violations in 655.810(b)(1)).
citation: 20 CFR 655.731(c)(9)(ii)-(iii) & (c)(10)-(c)(11); INA 214(c)(9) (ACWIA fee); penalty 20 CFR 655.810(b)(1). *(Re-verify (c)(10)/(c)(11) sub-letters against current eCFR; Fact Sheet 62H corroborates. ACWIA tiers $1,500/$750 are statutory — confirm current figures.)*
dataNeeded: Any worker charge/deduction for: LCA prep, petition prep, attorney fees, ACWIA training fee, $500 fraud fee; employer FTE count (sets $1,500 vs $750); resulting net wage.
implementationNote: Mechanical: flag any deduction/charge whose reason code maps to {LCA_prep, petition_prep, immigration_attorney_fee, ACWIA_fee, fraud_fee}. ACWIA/fraud-fee prohibition is absolute (flag regardless of net wage); attorney-fee/cost prohibition applies when it reduces below the required wage.

check: No penalty imposed on the worker for ceasing employment before an agreed date (distinguish bona fide liquidated damages).
requirement: May NOT require the worker to pay a PENALTY for ceasing employment before an agreed date. Penalty-vs-liquidated-damages is determined under State contract law: bona fide liquidated damages (a reasonable pre-estimate of actual loss) permitted; a punitive amount is a prohibited penalty. ACWIA fee can never be characterized as liquidated damages.
trigger: Any contractual clawback/repayment/withheld amount triggered by the worker leaving before a stated term.
threshold: Permitted only if it qualifies as bona fide liquidated damages under State law; a punitive penalty is prohibited; ACWIA fee never recoverable.
deadline: At separation / when the charge is imposed.
severityPenalty: Substantive + enumerated: an early-cessation penalty paid by the worker is a CMP-eligible violation, up to $2,364; plus back wages/restoration.
citation: 20 CFR 655.731(c)(10)(i) (penalty vs liquidated damages); penalty 20 CFR 655.810(b)(1). *(Re-verify (c)(10) sub-letter against current eCFR.)*
dataNeeded: Existence/terms of any early-departure repayment clause; amount; whether a reasonable pre-estimate of loss; governing State; whether ACWIA fee is embedded; whether the worker actually paid.
implementationNote: NOT mechanical — penalty-vs-liquidated-damages is fact- and State-law-specific → NEEDS-COUNSEL whenever an early-cessation repayment clause is present. Detect the CLAUSE + the worker payment, route to counsel; do not auto-decide.

check: On any wage/benefit shortfall, back wages (and fringe) = difference between required and paid for the full violation period.
requirement: WHD shall assess and oversee payment of BACK WAGES (or fringe benefits) = (amount that should have been paid) − (amount actually paid), for the entire violation period, to the affected worker(s).
trigger: Any determined underpayment, unpaid benched time, unauthorized deduction, or denied benefit.
threshold: Back wages = Σ over the violation period of (required − actual) per worker; back fringe = (required benefit value − provided).
deadline: Assessed on enforcement finding; for the violation period (within the limitations/retention window).
severityPenalty: Make-whole remedy (in addition to CMP and debarment for the underlying class).
dataNeeded: Per worker per period: required wage; actual paid; hours; deduction amounts; benefit values; violation start/end.
implementationNote: Mechanical accumulator: back_wages = Σ max(0, required_period_wage − paid_period_wage) over all periods in the window. Drives the canonical liability-estimate field. Interest is not specified in 655.810 (do not auto-add interest).

check: Map a found violation to the correct CMP tier + per-violation cap.
requirement: Three tiers (statutory base, annually inflation-adjusted): TIER 1 up to $2,364 for a substantial failure (strike/lockout, U.S.-worker displacement, substantial notification/LCA-specificity/recruitment failures, material misrepresentation, an early-cessation penalty, the worker paying the $500/ACWIA fees, impeding the Administrator). TIER 2 up to $9,624 for a willful failure / willful misrepresentation / whistleblower discrimination. TIER 3 up to $67,367 for a willful violation that resulted in DISPLACEMENT of a U.S. worker in the 90-days-before/90-days-after window.
trigger: A determined LCA wage/condition violation.
threshold: Caps (2026): $2,364 / $9,624 / $67,367. Displacement window = 90 days before to 90 days after petition filing. Per-violation (per worker/occurrence).
deadline: Assessed at enforcement; figures re-indexed each January.
severityPenalty: This rule defines the penalty classes. Amounts are maxima; the Administrator sets the actual amount via 655.810(c) factors.
citation: 20 CFR 655.810(b)(1)-(3); inflation adjustment 20 CFR Part 356 / DOL CMP Adjustment final rule.
dataNeeded: Violation type; willfulness determination; whether a U.S. worker was displaced; petition filing date + 90-day windows; affected-worker count.
implementationNote: Tier SELECTION (willful? displacement?) → NEEDS-COUNSEL; once classified, the cap lookup is mechanical. CRITICAL: hard-code the dollar amounts behind a year/version constant and refresh every January; 2026 = $2,364 / $9,624 / $67,367. Verify the current year's figures against the DOL penalties page at build time.

check: Map a found violation to the minimum debarment (program-disqualification) period.
requirement: On a finding, the employer is disqualified from LCA approval and from filing H-1B / other employment-based petitions for: ≥1 year (substantial/willful per (b)(1)); ≥2 years (willful per (b)(2)); ≥3 years (willful + displacement per (b)(3)). DOL notifies DHS, which may not approve petitions for the period.
trigger: A finalized violation finding in the corresponding tier.
deadline: Runs from the date DHS receives the debarment notice.
severityPenalty: Program disqualification — most severe non-monetary consequence.
dataNeeded: Violation tier (from cmp-tiers rule); willfulness; displacement finding.
implementationNote: Mechanical lookup once tier set: tier1→1yr, tier2→2yr, tier3→3yr (minimums). Tier determination itself → NEEDS-COUNSEL. Surface as a downstream consequence of cmp-tiers, not an independent evaluator.

check: H-1B petition (I-797) initial validity ≤3 years and ≤ the LCA validity period.
requirement: An approved H-1B specialty-occupation petition is valid up to 3 years but not beyond the LCA validity (DOD R&D/coproduction up to 5; fashion modeling up to 3). The I-797 dates are the outer bound of authorized employment.
trigger: Petition approved (I-797C/I-797B) OR a stored petition loaded for monitoring.
threshold: ≤3 years (specialty); validity end ≤ LCA end. 5 years for DOD R&D/coproduction.
deadline: n/a (validity-ceiling check). Petition validity END date anchors downstream expiry/extension rules.
severityPenalty: Data-integrity anchor. A validity window exceeding the LCA window = erroneous/invalid approval → flag for counsel (medium). Working outside the approved window = unauthorized employment.
citation: 8 CFR 214.2(h)(9)(iii)(A)(1); validity tied to LCA per 20 CFR 655.730.
dataNeeded: petition.receiptNumber, validityStart, validityEnd, classification (specialty/DOD/fashion), lca.validityStart, lca.validityEnd.
implementationNote: Deterministic: assert (validityEnd − validityStart) ≤ 3y (or 5y DOD) AND validityEnd ≤ lca.validityEnd. Source of truth for petition.validityEnd that every expiry/extension rule references. Cross-check against I-94 admit-until (can differ).

check: I-94 admit-until date governs authorized stay; flag the gap where I-94 expires before/after petition validity, and the 10-day pre/post admission grace.
requirement: Admitted for the petition validity plus up to 10 days before and 10 days after; may not work except during the validity period. The I-94 "admit until" date — NOT the visa stamp, NOT always the petition end — is the operative end of authorized STAY. Where I-94 admit-until is earlier than petition validity end, the earlier I-94 date controls.
trigger: An I-94 admit-until date exists and differs from petition.validityEnd, OR is approaching/passed.
threshold: Authorized stay = min(I-94 admit-until, petition validityEnd + 10 days). Work window = petition validityStart..validityEnd only. Unlawful presence begins the day AFTER I-94 expiry absent a timely-filed extension.
deadline: On the I-94 admit-until date. Escalate at 90/30/0 days remaining.
severityPenalty: Substantive. Overstay → unlawful-presence accrual (3/10-yr bars). Working past the validity window without 240-day coverage = unauthorized employment (employer I-9 / 1324a exposure).
citation: 8 CFR 214.2(h)(13)(i)(A) (validity + 10-day pre/post); 8 CFR 214.1(l)(1) (10-day grace); admit-until controlling per 8 CFR 214.1(a)(3); unlawful-presence bars INA 212(a)(9)(B) / 8 USC 1182(a)(9)(B).
dataNeeded: i94.admitUntilDate, i94.mostRecentEntryDate, petition.validityStart/End, visaStamp.expiry (informational), any pending extension receipt + filing date.
implementationNote: Deterministic gap detector: authorizedStayEnd = min(i94.admitUntilDate, petition.validityEnd). If i94.admitUntilDate < petition.validityEnd → raise a "truncated I-94" finding. Always require the I-94 from i94.cbp.dhs.gov, not the visa foil. The +10-day grace is STAY only — do not let it authorize work. Maps to existing key `i94_expiration`.

check: Extension/amendment of stay (I-129) filed up to 6 months before the start/current expiry, and MUST be filed before the current authorized stay expires to preserve status.
requirement: Extension may be filed only if the original petition's validity has not expired; the beneficiary must be physically present in the U.S. at filing. USCIS will not accept earlier than 6 months before the requested start date. An extension may not be approved for a beneficiary who failed to maintain status or whose status expired before filing.
trigger: petition.validityEnd (or I-94 admit-until) within 180 days AND employment continuing.
threshold: Earliest filing: 6 months (~180 days) before requested start. Latest to preserve status & 240-day coverage: ON or BEFORE the I-94 admit-until / petition validity end.
deadline: File before authorized stay expires. Escalate at 180 (window opens) / 60 / 30 days remaining.
severityPenalty: Technical-but-status-critical. Filing one day late = status lapse: no 240-day work authorization, approval only nunc pro tunc on a discretionary late-filing excuse (8 CFR 214.1(c)(4)), beneficiary out of status.
dataNeeded: petition.validityEnd, i94.admitUntilDate, extension.requestedStartDate, extension.filedDate, beneficiary.presentInUS (bool), employment.continuing (bool).
implementationNote: Deterministic: openWindow = requestedStartDate − 180d; mustFileBy = min(i94.admitUntilDate, petition.validityEnd). today ∈ [openWindow, mustFileBy] + no filedDate → actionable. today > mustFileBy + no filedDate → status-lapse alarm. Late-filing excuse under 214.1(c)(4) → NEEDS-COUNSEL. Maps to existing key `extension_filing`.

check: On a TIMELY-filed extension with the SAME employer, the beneficiary may keep working up to 240 days past I-94 expiry while pending — and MUST stop at 240 days or on denial.
requirement: Where a timely extension (same employer, same classification) was filed before the prior authorized period expired, employment with the same employer is authorized for ≤240 days from the expiration of the authorized stay, or until USCIS denies, whichever first. Employer annotates the I-9 "240-Day Ext." with the I-129 filing date and reverifies by day 240 or upon decision.
trigger: An H-1B extension I-129 filed on/before the I-94 admit-until date, same employer, still pending; I-94 admit-until has passed.
threshold: 240 calendar days from the I-94 admit-until date. Work authorization ENDS at the earlier of day 240 or USCIS decision (approval continues; denial terminates immediately). SAME employer and SAME classification only.
deadline: Day 240 after I-94 expiry. Escalate at 60 / 14 days remaining.
severityPenalty: Substantive for the EMPLOYER: employing past day 240 (or after denial) = knowingly continuing to employ an unauthorized worker → 1324a penalties; for the BENEFICIARY: unauthorized employment + unlawful presence. Hard stop-work trigger.
citation: 8 CFR 274a.12(b)(20); employer I-9 mechanics USCIS M-274 §7.5.
dataNeeded: extension.filedDate, i94.admitUntilDate, extension.sameEmployer (bool), extension.sameClassification (bool), extension.status (pending/approved/denied), extension.decisionDate.
implementationNote: Deterministic: ONLY arm if filedDate ≤ i94.admitUntilDate AND sameEmployer AND sameClassification. autoExtEnd = i94.admitUntilDate + 240d. effectiveStopWork = min(autoExtEnd, decisionDate-if-denied). Approved → superseded by new validity. Does NOT cover a change-of-EMPLOYER petition (that is portability). Common false-positive: applying it to a different employer. Existing key `auto_extension_expiry` carries the corrected 274a.12(b)(20) cite — keep it.

check: After cessation of H-1B employment, the beneficiary has up to 60 consecutive days (or until I-94 expiry, whichever shorter) of authorized stay — once per validity period.
requirement: An H-1B beneficiary (and dependents) is not deemed to have failed to maintain status solely on cessation of the employment, for up to 60 consecutive days or until the end of the authorized validity period (I-94), whichever shorter, once during each validity period. May file a COS, a portability petition, or depart.
trigger: H-1B employment terminates (voluntary or involuntary) before the I-94 admit-until date.
threshold: min(60 consecutive days from last day of employment, I-94 admit-until). ONCE per validity period — a second cessation gets no fresh 60 days. Does not extend the I-94.
deadline: Day 60 after termination, or I-94 admit-until, whichever earlier. Escalate at 45 / 14 / 0 days remaining.
severityPenalty: Substantive for the BENEFICIARY: past the window with no new petition/COS → out of status, accruing unlawful presence. Trigger for the employer's termination duties.
dataNeeded: employment.terminatedDate, i94.admitUntilDate, priorCessationThisValidityPeriod (bool), newPetition.filedDate or cos.filedDate, validityPeriodId.
implementationNote: Deterministic: graceEnd = min(terminatedDate + 60d, i94.admitUntilDate). Dedupe per validityPeriodId — a second cessation flags "no fresh 60 days" (discretionary edge → NEEDS-COUNSEL). "Cessation" vs "between assignments / benched but still employed" → NEEDS-COUNSEL where ambiguous (benching may be an LCA wage violation, not a cessation). Maps to existing key `grace_period`.

check: An eligible H-1B beneficiary may begin new/concurrent employment upon the FILING of a nonfrivolous H-1B petition by the new employer — before approval — under AC21 §105 / INA §214(n).
requirement: Authorized to start concurrent/new employment under §214(n) upon the filing of a nonfrivolous H-1B petition, or the requested start date, whichever later. Eligible = (i) lawfully admitted/provided H-1B status; (ii) a nonfrivolous new-employment petition (with amend/extend-stay request) filed BEFORE the authorized stay expired; (iii) no unauthorized employment from last admission through filing. Authorization continues until adjudication; if denied, it ceases.
trigger: A new-employer H-1B I-129 (portability petition) filed for a beneficiary holding/provided H-1B status.
threshold: Work may begin on max(petitionFiledDate, requestedStartDate). Petition MUST be filed before I-94 admit-until expiry (an expired I-94 from a prior portability petition still counts as "period of stay authorized" for a successive port — bridge porting). Requires NO unauthorized employment since last admission.
deadline: n/a (enabling rule). Authorization runs until adjudication; denial ceases work authorization immediately.
severityPenalty: Substantive. If conditions unmet (I-94 expired with no qualifying prior petition, or prior unauthorized employment), working for the new employer is unauthorized → employer 1324a exposure + beneficiary status violation. Bridge chains high-risk: an upstream denial can collapse later ports (214.2(h)(2)(i)(H)(3)(ii)).
citation: 8 CFR 214.2(h)(2)(i)(H); INA §214(n) / 8 USC 1184(n); AC21 §105. *(Note: 8 CFR 274a.12(b)(21) governs H-2, NOT H-1B — H-1B work auth flows from §214(n)+(h)(2)(i)(H).)*
dataNeeded: newPetition.filedDate, requestedStartDate, nonfrivolous (bool/attested), beneficiary.currentStatus, i94.admitUntilDate, beneficiary.unauthorizedEmploymentSinceAdmission (bool), priorPortabilityChain[].
implementationNote: Partially deterministic: assert filedDate ≤ i94.admitUntilDate (or covered by an unexpired/qualifying prior petition for successive ports) AND no flagged unauthorized employment. workStartEligible = max(filedDate, requestedStartDate). "Nonfrivolous" and "valid H-1B classification" → NEEDS-COUNSEL. Bridge-petition risk → NEEDS-COUNSEL. Do NOT conflate with the 240-day rule (same-employer only). Existing key `ac21_portability` is about INA §204(j) green-card portability (different doctrine) — this is a NEW, distinct rule.

check: Total H-1B (+L) time ≤6 years; beyond 6 requires either a 1-year-abroad reset or an AC21 7th-year exemption.
requirement: An H-1B alien who has spent six years under (H) and/or (L) may not extend, change status, or be readmitted under (H)/(L) unless physically present outside the U.S. (except brief business/pleasure trips) for the immediate prior year. The 6-year cap is the statutory "period of authorized admission" under INA §214(g)(4).
trigger: Cumulative H-1B+L time approaches/exceeds 6 years (net of recapture) and an extension beyond 6 is contemplated.
threshold: 6 years (2,190 days) aggregate H-1B + L physical presence. Time >24h physically outside the U.S. during validity is NOT counted and is recapturable. Reset to a fresh 6 years requires 1 continuous year abroad.
deadline: On reaching the 6-year mark (net of recapture).
severityPenalty: Substantive. An extension beyond 6 years without valid recapture or an AC21 exemption is improvidently granted and revocable; working past the true ceiling = out of status. Mis-counting recapture is the most common error.
dataNeeded: all prior H-1B and L petition validity periods + entry/exit history (I-94 travel), daysPhysicallyOutsideUS per validity, anyContinuousYearAbroad (dates), proposedExtension.endDate.
implementationNote: Deterministic counting IF travel data complete: cumulativeDays = sum(daysInStatus) − recapturableDays. Alarm when cumulative + proposedExtension would exceed 2190 unless an AC21 exemption (104c/106) applies or a 1-year-abroad reset is recorded. "Brief trips for business or pleasure" during the year abroad are non-interruptive but don't count toward the year → NEEDS-COUNSEL where the year-abroad is borderline. Burden on petitioner.

check: Days spent physically outside the U.S. (>24h) during H-1B validity can be recaptured and added back to the 6-year max — petitioner must request and document them.
requirement: Time >24h physically outside the U.S. during the validity of an approved H-1B petition is not counted toward §214(g)(4), regardless of whether the absence interrupted the stay. Remaining time may be recaptured in a later petition at any time before the full period is used. Petitioner's burden to request and demonstrate with evidence (passport stamps, I-94, tickets, a chart of dates abroad).
trigger: Preparing an extension for a beneficiary near the 6-year cap with documented time abroad during prior H-1B validity.
threshold: Recapturable = full days (>24h absences) physically outside the U.S. during validity periods. No temporal limit on claiming. Recapture of a cap-counted beneficiary does NOT re-subject them to the cap.
deadline: n/a (a credit). Claimed in/with the extension that needs the time.
severityPenalty: Remediation/credit calculation, not a violation. Risk: under-claiming wastes time; over-claiming (counting <24h trips, or trips outside validity) → improvident grant. Documentation failure → RFE/denial.
dataNeeded: I-94 arrival/departure travel history (every entry/exit), per-trip duration, petition validity windows, evidence-inventory flags (passport stamps/tickets).
implementationNote: Deterministic given complete travel data: recapDays = sum of full days where (exit..entry) > 24h AND within an approved H-1B validity window. Only whole days >24h. Surface the computed number AND the evidence-completeness gap as a documentation checklist. USCIS may grant all/part/none → legal sufficiency of evidence → NEEDS-COUNSEL. Pairs with `six_year_limit` (net = 6y − recapture).

check: Beyond the 6-year cap, 1-year H-1B extensions available if a PERM labor cert OR I-140 was filed ≥365 days ago (AC21 §106).
requirement: Eligible for H-1B beyond 6 years if ≥365 days have elapsed since (i) the filing of a PERM (if required for §203(b)), or (ii) the filing of an I-140. Approvals in ≤1-year increments until the PERM expires or a final decision on the PERM/I-140/adjustment. May file in advance (within 6 months of start) provided the PERM/I-140 was filed ≥365 days before the exemption period takes effect.
trigger: Beneficiary at/near the 6-year cap AND a PERM or I-140 filed on their behalf.
threshold: ≥365 days since PERM or I-140 filing (to the date the exemption period takes effect, allowing advance filing within 6 months). ≤1-year increments. Cannot aggregate days from two different PERM/I-140 filings to reach 365.
deadline: Each 1-year increment renews; eligibility ends on final PERM/I-140/AOS decision (subject to "no final decision while appeal pending").
severityPenalty: Substantive. An extension on a PERM/I-140 not satisfying the 365-day rule (or finally denied/withdrawn beyond the appeal window) is improvidently granted; working on it is unauthorized.
citation: 8 CFR 214.2(h)(13)(iii)(D)(1)-(10); AC21 §106(a)/(b). *(This is the correct §106 home — the existing catalog references §106 under key `ac21_portability` incorrectly; that key is §204(j).)*
dataNeeded: perm.filedDate and/or i140.filedDate, perm.status, i140.status (incl. appeal), priorH1bMaxedOut (bool), proposedExtension.startDate, visaAvailableDate, aosOrIVApplication.filedDate.
implementationNote: Deterministic core: eligible if (today_or_startDate − max(perm.filedDate, i140.filedDate)) ≥ 365 days (with advance-filing window). 1-year increments. BUT: (a) "final decision" status + whether an appeal is pending (214.2(h)(13)(iii)(D)(3)) → NEEDS-COUNSEL; (b) the (D)(10) bar (failure to file AOS within 1 year of visa availability) requires visa-bulletin cross-referencing → NEEDS-COUNSEL.

check: Beyond the 6-year cap, 3-year H-1B extensions available to a beneficiary with an APPROVED I-140 who cannot get the green card only due to per-country backlog (AC21 §104(c)).
requirement: An alien holding/having held H-1B, beneficiary of an APPROVED I-140 under §203(b)(1)/(2)/(3), eligible to be granted that status but for the per-country limitation, is eligible beyond 6 years. Must demonstrate visa unavailability as of the H-1B filing date. ≤3-year increments for as long as eligible.
trigger: Beneficiary at/near the 6-year cap with an APPROVED I-140 and a backlogged (unavailable) priority date due to country of chargeability.
threshold: APPROVED I-140 (not merely filed) AND visa unavailability (priority date not current) per country of chargeability as of the H-1B filing date. ≤3-year increments (vs 1 under §106). Available until I-140 revoked or IV/AOS approved/denied.
deadline: Each ≤3-year increment renews; ends on I-140 revocation or final IV/AOS decision.
severityPenalty: Substantive. Granting the 3-year extension without an approved I-140, or after the priority date became current, is improvident.
dataNeeded: i140.status (must be approved), i140.preferenceCategory (EB-1/2/3), beneficiary.countryOfChargeability, priorityDate, currentVisaBulletinFinalActionDate, proposedExtension.startDate.
implementationNote: Deterministic gate: i140.status == approved AND priorityDate not current (priorityDate > visaBulletin final-action date for category+country) as of filing. ≤3-year increments. The visa-bulletin comparison needs an authoritative monthly bulletin feed → if absent, render priority-date currency as "unavailable" and flag NEEDS-COUNSEL rather than guess. "Eligible but for per-country limitation" → NEEDS-COUNSEL.

check: A material change in employment terms (or eligibility) requires an AMENDED or new I-129 (with a new LCA) before the change takes effect.
requirement: File an amended/new petition (+ fee) to reflect any material changes in employment/training terms or eligibility as specified in the original petition; an amended H-1B petition must include a new LCA. Separately, immediately notify USCIS of changes affecting eligibility and file an amended petition while continuing to employ the beneficiary.
trigger: A material change: job duties (SOC/specialty), worksite location (see worksite_simeio), material hours reduction (FT↔PT), employer-entity change (merger/acquisition unless successor-in-interest assumes the LCA), or a wage change below the LCA wage.
threshold: Material change → amended petition required. Immaterial (same-MSA move, successor-in-interest assuming the LCA, a promotion not affecting eligibility) → no amendment. File BEFORE the change takes effect.
deadline: Before the material change takes effect (no fixed numeric grace; the catalog's 30-day window is a prep guideline, not a regulatory deadline).
severityPenalty: Substantive. Employing under materially changed terms without an amended petition = working not as authorized → revocable petition (214.2(h)(11)(iii)(A)(1)/(3)), status violation, employer LCA/wage + 1324a exposure.
citation: 8 CFR 214.2(h)(2)(i)(E) (amended/new petition + new LCA); 8 CFR 214.2(h)(11)(i)(A) (immediate notification).
dataNeeded: current job: SOC, title, duties, worksite(s), wage, hours, employer entity; approvedPetition baseline of the same; changeEffectiveDate; corporateEvent (merger/acquisition + successor-in-interest flag); amendedPetition.filedDate.
implementationNote: Detector compares current fields vs baseline; flags deltas. Some deltas mechanically material (wage below LCA, FT→PT, new SOC). Whether a duties change is "material," and whether a restructuring qualifies as successor-in-interest (no amendment) → NEEDS-COUNSEL. Maps to existing key `amendment_filing` (existing cite is the Simeio memo PM-602-0114; add the cleaner 214.2(h)(2)(i)(E) + (h)(11)(i)(A)).
