check: Moving the worker to a worksite outside the existing MSA/area of intended employment (requiring a new LCA) is a MATERIAL CHANGE requiring an amended petition (Matter of Simeio Solutions).
requirement: A change to a worksite requiring a new LCA (outside the MSA/area of intended employment of the approved petition+LCA) is a material change; file an amended H-1B petition with a new certified LCA. A same-MSA move requires LCA posting but no amendment. Short-term placements (655.735) and non-worksite locations may be excepted.
trigger: Change of primary worksite to a location not covered by the LCA(s) underlying the approved petition.
threshold: New worksite OUTSIDE the existing MSA/area of intended employment AND requiring a new LCA → amended petition, filed BEFORE the worker begins at the new location. Within-MSA: posting only.
deadline: Amended petition filed before the worker starts at the new worksite. (Post-Simeio, no retroactive safe-harbor filing window for new moves.)
severityPenalty: Substantive. Placing the worker at the out-of-area worksite before filing = unauthorized worksite / deviation → revocable petition, status violation, LCA violation, employer 1324a/LCA exposure. One of the most heavily enforced H-1B triggers.
citation: Matter of Simeio Solutions, LLC, 26 I&N Dec. 542 (AAO 2015); 8 CFR 214.2(h)(2)(i)(E); 8 CFR 214.2(h)(11)(i)(A); LCA worksite/posting 20 CFR 655.734; short-term placement 20 CFR 655.735.
dataNeeded: approvedPetition.worksites[] (with MSA), newWorksite.address + derived MSA, newLCA.certified (bool) + certifiedDate, moveEffectiveDate, amendedPetition.filedDate, shortTermPlacement (bool, days).
implementationNote: Deterministic IF MSA derivable: newWorksite.MSA != any approved worksite.MSA → amended petition required, assert amendedPetition.filedDate ≤ moveEffectiveDate. Geocoding + the short-term-placement exception (655.735 day-counts) → NEEDS-COUNSEL where short-term or the MSA boundary is ambiguous. Sub-rule of `amendment.material_change`; ties to the repo's materialWorksiteSlice / worksiteCompare reconciliation.

check: To end H-1B wage liability and effect a "bona fide termination": (1) notify the beneficiary, (2) notify USCIS to withdraw the petition, and (3) offer return-transportation costs for an involuntary termination.
requirement: The required (LCA) wage obligation continues until a BONA FIDE termination. DOL/case law (Amtel) requires: (1) express notice to the employee; (2) notice to USCIS so the petition is canceled/withdrawn (withdrawal → immediate automatic revocation); (3) for an involuntary dismissal before the end of authorized admission, liability for the reasonable costs of return transportation to the last foreign residence. Until USCIS is notified, back-pay/wage liability can accrue.
trigger: H-1B employment is terminated by the employer.
threshold: All THREE prongs for a complete bona fide termination. Wage liability runs until at least the USCIS-notification prong. Return-transportation applies only to involuntary dismissals (not voluntary resignations). Separate 60-day grace (or until I-94 end) under 8 CFR 214.1(l)(2).
deadline: Promptly upon termination. Wage liability accrues until USCIS notification. Escalate at 1 / 0 days.
severityPenalty: Substantive (DOL WHD + USCIS). Failure → continued back-wage liability through the I-94 end (20 CFR 655.731 / Subpart I CMP + back wages); failure to offer return transport → §214(c)(5) liability; failure to withdraw → an active petition the employer is still liable for. Cannot shift petition costs to the worker.
dataNeeded: employment.terminatedDate, termination.type (voluntary/involuntary), employeeNotice.given (bool)+date, uscisWithdrawal.sentDate, returnTransport.offered (bool)+date (involuntary), lca.requiredWage, wagesPaidThrough, beneficiary.lastForeignResidence.
implementationNote: Deterministic checklist: involuntary → require all three prongs; voluntary → return-transport prong N/A. continued-wage-liability exposure = required LCA wage from terminatedDate until uscisWithdrawal.sentDate. Whether actions legally constitute a "bona fide termination" (constructive discharge, benching disputes, notice effectiveness) → NEEDS-COUNSEL. Maps to existing key `termination_obligations`.

check: On termination, withdraw the I-129 with USCIS and withdraw/cancel the LCA with DOL to stop ongoing obligations.
requirement: Approval is immediately and automatically revoked on a written withdrawal (or going out of business, or DOL LCA revocation). A petitioner no longer employing the beneficiary shall send a letter explaining the change to the approving director. Separately withdraw the LCA from DOL — though LCA withdrawal alone does NOT end wage liability; only a bona fide termination does.
trigger: H-1B employment ends and the employer intends to cease sponsorship.
threshold: Written withdrawal letter to the approving USCIS service center (→ immediate automatic revocation). LCA withdrawal request to DOL. No fixed day-count; promptly.
deadline: Promptly upon (bona fide) termination. The USCIS-withdrawal date caps continued wage-liability accrual.
severityPenalty: Substantive/administrative. An un-withdrawn petition leaves the employer as petitioner of record (FDNS site-visit / fraud exposure for a "ghost" beneficiary); an un-withdrawn LCA leaves a live attestation.
dataNeeded: petition.receiptNumber, approvingServiceCenter, uscisWithdrawal.sentDate, lca.caseNumber, lcaWithdrawal.sentDate, employment.terminatedDate.
implementationNote: Deterministic: on terminatedDate, require uscisWithdrawal.sentDate and lcaWithdrawal.sentDate set (not after a long lag). Surface the un-withdrawn-petition state as an open finding. Mostly mechanical; timing/strategy (e.g., delaying withdrawal during a grace-period port) → low-grade NEEDS-COUNSEL. Complements the bona-fide-termination rule.

check: Continuous maintenance of status: work only within the authorized petition window, keep a valid unexpired I-94, no unauthorized employment; an extension cannot be approved if status lapsed.
requirement: Every nonimmigrant must maintain status. An extension/amendment may NOT be approved for a beneficiary who failed to maintain status or whose status expired before filing (absent the discretionary late-filing excuse). May not work except during the validity period (plus §214(n)/240-day windows).
trigger: Ongoing — evaluated continuously while holding H-1B status.
threshold: Maintained iff: (a) all employment within an authorized window (approved validity, OR 240-day coverage, OR §214(n) portability, OR a documented grace period); (b) I-94 not expired without a timely extension; (c) no unauthorized employment. A lapse breaks the chain and blocks future extensions/AOS.
deadline: Continuous (no single date).
severityPenalty: Substantive. A status lapse disqualifies extensions (214.1(c)(4)), can bar AOS (INA §245(c)), and starts unlawful-presence accrual. Employing during a lapse = 1324a exposure.
dataNeeded: timeline of: petition validity windows, I-94 admit-until, all employment start/stop + employer/worksite, extension/port filing dates + decisions, grace-period invocations — the union of inputs from the other h1b.* rules.
implementationNote: COMPOSITE/derived rule: a status-continuity reconciler walking the beneficiary timeline, asserting every employment day is covered by some authorized window and no I-94 expiry passed without a timely extension. Output: continuous-status (bool) + first gap date. Discretionary late-filing excuse under 214.1(c)(4) → NEEDS-COUNSEL. Aggregates extension_filing, auto_extension_expiry, grace_period, i94_expiration, portability.

check: An F-1 student who is the beneficiary of a timely-filed, cap-subject H-1B change-of-status petition gets automatic extension of F-1 D/S and OPT work authorization until April 1 of the relevant fiscal year (or H-1B start, whichever earlier).
requirement: Under cap-gap (8 CFR 214.2(f)(5)(vi), as amended by the H-1B Modernization final rule, 89 FR 103054 (Dec 18, 2024)), an F-1 who is the beneficiary of a cap-subject petition requesting COS to H-1B, timely filed, automatically has F-1 D/S and any OPT employment authorization extended until April 1 of the relevant fiscal year, or until the H-1B validity start, whichever earlier. Terminates immediately if the petition is rejected, denied, revoked, or withdrawn.
trigger: An F-1 (OPT) beneficiary is cap-selected and a cap-subject I-129 requesting COS is timely filed before the F-1/OPT authorization expires.
threshold: Petition must be (a) cap-subject, (b) request COS (not consular), (c) filed while F-1 status or OPT is valid (timely). Cap-gap end = min(April 1 of the relevant FY, H-1B validity start). Ends immediately on rejection/denial/revocation/withdrawal.
deadline: Cap-gap ends April 1 of the relevant FY, or the H-1B start if earlier. Escalate at 30 / 0 days remaining.
severityPenalty: Substantive. Employing after the cap-gap endpoint (without the H-1B having taken effect) = unauthorized employment → 1324a exposure + beneficiary status violation. A petition denial/withdrawal collapses cap-gap immediately.
citation: 8 CFR 214.2(f)(5)(vi); H-1B Modernization final rule, 89 FR 103054 (Dec 18, 2024) (cap-gap end → April 1).
dataNeeded: f1Opt.authorizationEndDate, h1bPetition.capSubject (bool), requestsCOS (bool), filedDate, status (pending/approved/denied/withdrawn), validityStart, capSelectionYear.
implementationNote: Deterministic: arm only if capSubject AND requestsCOS AND filedDate ≤ f1Opt.authorizationEndDate (timely). capGapEnd = min(April 1 of (capSelectionYear+1), validityStart). Reuse the repo's calculateCapGapEnd(selectionYear) returning `${year+1}-04-01`. If status flips to denied/withdrawn, terminate immediately regardless of date. Maps to existing key `cap_gap`.

check: H-1B petition filed on/after 2026-04-01 uses Form I-129 edition 02/27/26 (not 01/17/25).
requirement: USCIS requires the 02/27/26 edition for all H-1B/H-1B1 petitions filed on/after April 1, 2026; prior-edition petitions received on/after that date are rejected. Before 04/01/2026 the 01/17/25 edition remains acceptable.
trigger: An I-129 petition assembled/filed with a filing/postmark date on/after 2026-04-01.
threshold: Edition date (lower-right corner) must read 02/27/26 for filings on/after 2026-04-01; cutover = 2026-04-01.
deadline: Hard cutover 2026-04-01.
severityPenalty: Procedural / fatal-to-filing: wrong-edition petitions rejected (not adjudicated) → loss of filing date — critical for cap-subject cases with a registration-selection window. No statutory CMP.
citation: USCIS Form I-129 edition 02/27/26; form-edition acceptance policy on the I-129 forms page; PRA docket USCIS-2025-0040.
dataNeeded: petition.formEditionDate; petition.filingDate (or intended postmark); petition.classification (H-1B/H-1B1).
implementationNote: Deterministic: compare formEditionDate against filingDate vs the 2026-04-01 boundary. Maintain a small editions table (USCIS may grace-period an edition); verify exact cutover wording on uscis.gov/i-129 at config time. Edge: a petition prepared before but mailed after cutover still gets rejected — key off the receipt/postmark date, not prepare date.

check: All five new position-requirement fields (Q7–Q11) on the H-1B Data Collection / H Classification Supplement are completed (non-blank).
requirement: On the 02/27/26 edition, answer Q7 education required; Q8 field(s) of study; Q9 years of experience required; Q10 special skills required; Q11 number supervised + their titles. Petitioners must answer every applicable Data Collection Supplement question.
trigger: An H-1B/H-1B1 petition on the 02/27/26 edition validated for completeness.
threshold: 5 required fields, all non-empty (Q11 may be "0"/"None" but must be explicitly answered).
deadline: At filing (Section 2(a) of the Data Collection Supplement).
severityPenalty: Procedural: omission → RFE or rejection for an incomplete form; not a CMP item.
citation: Form I-129 (02/27/26), H-1B and H-1B1 Data Collection and Filing Fee Exemption Supplement, Questions 7–11 (form page 21); Instructions for Form I-129, H Classification / Data Collection Supplement section.
dataNeeded: hSupp.q7_educationLevelRequired; q8_fieldsOfStudy; q9_yearsExperienceRequired; q10_specialSkills; q11_numberSupervised + supervisedTitles.
implementationNote: Deterministic null/blank check per field. BYTE-VERIFY the exact on-form question numbers, labels, and answer formats against the official 02/27/26 PDF before production (corroborated across five analyses; not captured byte-exact).

check: Stated minimum education (I-129 Q7) consistent with the LCA prevailing-wage LEVEL and the SOC/OEWS occupation.
requirement: Required education on the I-129 must be reconcilable with the certified LCA wage level. Under DOL methodology, an education requirement above the O*NET-SOC usual education adds wage-level step(s); a graduate-degree minimum is generally inconsistent with a Level I wage unless otherwise justified.
trigger: I-129 Q7 education exceeds the occupation's usual education AND the certified LCA wage level is Level I (or lower than the education factor implies).
threshold: Education above the O*NET-SOC E&T/Appendix-D usual category = +1 step per category above (DOL Step 3). Flag when education-implied level > LCA wage level.
deadline: Evaluated at petition assembly / pre-filing audit; LCA must be certified before the I-129 is filed.
severityPenalty: Substantive adjudication risk: supports an RFE/denial on specialty-occupation or LCA-correspondence grounds; willful LCA misstatement → civil penalties + debarment (INA 212(n); 20 CFR 655 Subpart I).
citation: DOL ETA Prevailing Wage Determination Policy Guidance (Nov-2009), Appendix A Step 3 (Education); 20 CFR 655.731; cross-ref 8 CFR 214.2(h)(4)(iii)(A).
dataNeeded: hSupp.q7_educationLevelRequired; lca.wageLevel (I–IV); lca.socCode; soc.usualEducationCategory; lca.prevailingWageSource.
implementationNote: Partly deterministic: map SOC → usual education category, compute education-implied step, compare to certified level. DOL guidance says the determination "should not be implemented in an automated fashion" — emit a FLAG for analyst review, not an auto-fail. NEEDS-COUNSEL where the employer asserts a documented business justification for a higher requirement at a lower level.

check: Stated minimum experience (I-129 Q9) consistent with the LCA wage level.
requirement: Required years of experience above the occupation's SVP/usual range push the level up (II/III). A multi-year experience minimum is generally inconsistent with a Level I wage.
trigger: I-129 Q9 experience exceeds the O*NET SVP/usual range AND the LCA level is below the experience-implied level (e.g., experience required but Level I).
threshold: Experience above the SVP range = +1 step (DOL Step 2). Heuristic: any required experience > 0 yrs paired with Level I; or experience materially above the typical entry range.
deadline: Pre-filing (LCA certified before I-129).
severityPenalty: Substantive: a documented USCIS RFE theme + LCA actual/prevailing-wage exposure (20 CFR 655.731; Subpart I penalties).
citation: DOL ETA PW Guidance (Nov-2009), Appendix A Step 2 (Experience); 20 CFR 655.731.
dataNeeded: hSupp.q9_yearsExperienceRequired; lca.wageLevel; lca.socCode; soc.svpRange.
implementationNote: Deterministic threshold compare (experience vs SVP-implied step vs certified level) → flag; final call → analyst/counsel because DOL allows experience in lieu of education (Step 2 vs Step 3 mutual-exclusion) and forbids double-counting. NEEDS-COUNSEL when experience substitutes for a degree.

check: Stated special skills (I-129 Q10) consistent with the LCA wage level.
requirement: Special skills/knowledge/licensure beyond entry-level add a step. Substantive special-skill requirements are generally inconsistent with a Level I wage.
trigger: I-129 Q10 lists special skills/licensure beyond entry-level for the SOC AND the LCA level is Level I.
threshold: Special skill/knowledge beyond normal entry = +1 step (DOL Step 4). Flag: non-empty special-skills requirement paired with Level I.
deadline: Pre-filing.
severityPenalty: Substantive adjudication / LCA-correspondence risk (RFE; potential Subpart I exposure if it signals a knowingly understated level).
citation: DOL ETA PW Guidance (Nov-2009), Appendix A Step 4 (Special Skills, Knowledge, Licensure); 20 CFR 655.731.
dataNeeded: hSupp.q10_specialSkills; lca.wageLevel; lca.socCode; soc.entryLevelSkillBaseline.
implementationNote: Deterministic presence-vs-level flag; skill severity (entry-normal vs specialized) → judgment. A license that is a normal entry requirement (RN, attorney) adds NO step per DOL guidance — encode a per-SOC "license-is-entry-normal" exception list; NEEDS-COUNSEL for ambiguous skills.

check: Supervisory duties (I-129 Q11 > 0) reconciled with the LCA wage level WITHOUT auto-inflating to Level IV.
requirement: Supervision of >0 people adds one step — UNLESS supervision is a customary duty of the SOC (e.g., a First-Line Supervisor/Manager occupation), where no step is added. Supervisory duties do NOT automatically warrant Level IV.
trigger: I-129 Q11 number-supervised > 0. Cross-check: (a) SOC is supervisory but no supervision stated, or (b) supervision stated but level not stepped up for a non-supervisory SOC.
threshold: Supervised count > 0 AND SOC not a First-Line-Supervisor/Manager occupation → +1 step (DOL Step 5). If SOC IS supervisory → +0.
deadline: Pre-filing.
severityPenalty: Substantive both directions: understated level (supervision present, level not raised) = LCA/wage exposure; an inflated Level IV justified solely by supervision = over-statement risk + specialty-occupation credibility issue.
citation: DOL ETA PW Guidance (Nov-2009), Appendix A Step 5 (Supervisory Duties); 20 CFR 655.731.
dataNeeded: hSupp.q11_numberSupervised; q11_supervisedTitles; lca.wageLevel; lca.socCode; soc.isSupervisoryOccupation (flag).
implementationNote: Mostly deterministic: maintain a set of First-Line-Supervisor/Manager SOC codes (BLS "XX-1xxx" family) for the exception. Two-sided flag. NEEDS-COUNSEL only for borderline "lead" roles where titles imply supervision but count = 0.

check: Field(s) of study required (I-129 Q8) directly related to the duties and to a specific specialty (not a general degree).
requirement: Under 8 CFR 214.2(h)(4)(ii) (as amended eff. 01/17/2025), a specialty occupation requires a bachelor's-or-higher in a DIRECTLY RELATED specific specialty; not a specialty occupation if a general degree suffices. "Directly related" = a logical connection between degree and duties. Where multiple fields are listed, each must be directly related.
trigger: Q8 names a general field ("Business Administration," "Liberal Arts") with no specialization, OR a wide disparate set, OR a field with no logical connection to the duties.
threshold: Required field must be a "specific specialty" directly related to duties; general-degree-sufficient = disqualifying. n/a numeric.
deadline: Adjudication (eligibility at filing; bona fide position as of requested start date).
severityPenalty: Substantive / dispositive: failure means not a specialty occupation → denial. (Eligibility, not a CMP item.)
citation: 8 CFR 214.2(h)(4)(ii); INA 214(i)(1) (8 USC 1184(i)(1)); "Modernizing H-1B Requirements" final rule, 89 FR 103054 (Dec 18, 2024), RIN 1615-AC70, eff. 01/17/2025.
dataNeeded: hSupp.q8_fieldsOfStudy[]; position.dutiesText; position.socCode; petition.degreeRequirement.
implementationNote: NEEDS-COUNSEL for the core "directly related" judgment (a legal/adjudicative determination). Deterministic pre-screens: (1) flag if Q8 contains a known general-degree string ("business administration","liberal arts","general studies") with no specialization; (2) flag if the field list is unusually broad/disparate. Surface to counsel; do not auto-deny.

check: The position satisfies ≥1 of the four 8 CFR 214.2(h)(4)(iii)(A) specialty-occupation criteria, and the petition records which.
requirement: Must meet ≥1 of: (A)(1) a U.S. bachelor's-or-higher in a directly related specific specialty (or equivalent) is normally the minimum for entry; (A)(2) such a degree is normally required for parallel positions among similar organizations in the industry; (A)(3) the employer (or third party) normally requires such a degree for the duties; or (A)(4) the duties are so specialized, complex, or unique that the required knowledge is normally associated with such a degree.
trigger: Any H-1B specialty-occupation petition; evaluate whether ≥1 criterion is established and whether the stated minimums (Q7–Q10) coherently support it.
threshold: ≥1 of 4 criteria. ((A)(1)/(A)(2) hinge on "normally"; (A)(3) on the employer's normal practice; (A)(4) on specialized/complex/unique duties.)
deadline: Adjudication (eligibility at filing; bona fide position as of requested start date).
severityPenalty: Substantive / dispositive: failing all four = denial. Eligibility (no CMP).
dataNeeded: petition.assertedCriterion (1/2/3/4); position.dutiesText; position.socCode; evidence.industryDegreeNorm; evidence.employerNormalPractice; hSupp.q7_educationLevelRequired; q8_fieldsOfStudy.
implementationNote: NEEDS-COUNSEL: which criterion is met and whether the evidence suffices is the central H-1B legal judgment. Deterministic support: require the file to (a) declare which criterion is asserted, (b) attach the matching evidence type (parallel-position postings for (A)(2); employer hiring history for (A)(3)), and (c) flag internal contradictions (asserting (A)(1) while Q7 states only a generic/no-degree minimum; claiming (A)(4) complex duties against a Level I entry wage). Flag, route to counsel.

check: If specialty status is asserted, the I-129 stated minimum education (Q7) is at least a bachelor's in the directly-related specialty.
requirement: An occupation qualifies only if it requires a bachelor's-or-higher in a directly related specific specialty as a minimum for entry. If the petitioner's own stated minimum (Q7/Q8) is less than a relevant bachelor's (or accepts a general/unrelated degree), the position is internally inconsistent with specialty-occupation status.
trigger: Petition asserts specialty occupation BUT Q7 < bachelor's, OR Q8 accepts a non-specialty/general field, OR Q7/Q8 allow a degree-or-experience-equivalent that undercuts "degree normally required."
threshold: Q7 minimum ≥ U.S. bachelor's (or foreign equivalent) in a Q8 specialty field; less-than-bachelor's or "any field" = inconsistency.
deadline: Adjudication / pre-filing audit.
severityPenalty: Substantive: a stated sub-baccalaureate or any-field minimum is strong evidence against specialty occupation → RFE/denial.
dataNeeded: hSupp.q7_educationLevelRequired; q8_fieldsOfStudy; petition.assertedSpecialty (bool); petition.degreeRequirement.
implementationNote: Deterministic: normalize Q7 to a degree-level ordinal (none/associate/bachelor/master/doctorate) and assert ≥ bachelor AND Q8 != general/any-field when specialty claimed. High-value mechanical contradiction check from the new fields. Borderline equivalency (experience-in-lieu-of-degree) → NEEDS-COUNSEL.

check: The beneficiary actually holds the qualification the position requires (degree/field/license/equivalency), matching Q7/Q8.
requirement: Per 8 CFR 214.2(h)(4)(iii)(C), the beneficiary must (1) hold the required U.S. bachelor's-or-higher from an accredited institution; or (2) an equivalent foreign degree; or (3) an unrestricted state license/registration/certification for full practice; or (4) education + specialized training and/or progressively responsible experience equivalent to the required U.S. degree, with recognized expertise. The degree field must match the directly-related field (Q8).
trigger: Beneficiary's degree/field/license/equivalency does not satisfy Q7/Q8, or the file relies on the 3-for-1 experience equivalency without adequate documentation.
threshold: Beneficiary credential ≥ required degree level AND field within Q8 acceptable fields (or a documented (C)(2)/(C)(3)/(C)(4) equivalency). Experience equivalency: 3 yrs specialized experience per 1 year of missing college; for a Master's-equivalent, bachelor's + ≥5 yrs.
deadline: Eligibility as of filing.
severityPenalty: Substantive / dispositive: a beneficiary not meeting (C) = denial. Eligibility.
citation: 8 CFR 214.2(h)(4)(iii)(C)(1)-(4) and (D) (equivalency, incl. the 3:1 ratio); INA 214(i)(2).
dataNeeded: beneficiary.degreeLevel; degreeField; institutionAccredited (bool); licenses[]; yearsRelevantExperience; hSupp.q7_educationLevelRequired; q8_fieldsOfStudy; evidence.credentialEvaluation.
implementationNote: Partly deterministic: compare beneficiary degree level/field to Q7/Q8 (ordinal compare on level; ontology match on field); for (C)(2) foreign-equivalency and (C)(4)/(D) experience-equivalency apply the 3:1 and bachelor's+5yrs arithmetic as a mechanical pre-check. "Recognized expertise" and credential-evaluation sufficiency → NEEDS-COUNSEL. Flag field-mismatch (beneficiary degree not in Q8 list) as high-priority — the classic "degree not related to duties" RFE.

check: The petitioner has a bona fide specialty-occupation position available for the beneficiary as of the requested start date.
requirement: Per 8 CFR 214.2(h)(4)(iii)(F) (added eff. 01/17/2025), at filing the petitioner must establish a bona fide specialty position available as of the requested validity start. Need not establish day-to-day assignments for the entire period, but must show non-speculative actual specialty work (esp. for third-party placement / staffing).
trigger: Petition lacks evidence of actual available specialty work as of the requested start (e.g., no work order/SOW/itinerary for a staffed beneficiary; speculative/benching arrangement).
threshold: Bona fide position must exist as of the requested validity start. n/a numeric.
deadline: As of the requested validity-period start date; established at filing.
severityPenalty: Substantive: failure → RFE/denial. For third-party placements, also implicates employer-employee-relationship and LCA worksite-coverage.
citation: 8 CFR 214.2(h)(4)(iii)(F); "Modernizing H-1B Requirements" final rule, 89 FR 103054 (Dec 18, 2024), eff. 01/17/2025.
dataNeeded: petition.requestedStartDate; evidence.workAvailability (SOW/work order/itinerary/project); placement.isThirdParty (bool); lca.worksites[].
implementationNote: NEEDS-COUNSEL for the bona-fide / non-speculative judgment. Deterministic supports: require a work-availability artifact when placement.isThirdParty == true; check the LCA worksite(s) cover the actual place(s) of employment and the requested start ≥ LCA validity start. Flag missing artifacts.

check: SOC code and wage level consistent across the H-1B registration, the certified LCA, and the I-129 (incl. Q7–Q11) — no level-shopping or post-hoc downgrade.
requirement: Occupation (SOC), wage level, and position requirements must be coherent across registration, LCA (ETA-9035), and I-129. The LCA wage level cannot be "fixed" at the petition stage (no post-certification correction), so registration/LCA level must already match the I-129 position. A level inflated only to improve lottery odds, or a Level I selected to cut cost against a high-requirement role, is an inconsistency USCIS can now see directly.
trigger: SOC differs across registration/LCA/I-129; OR the I-129 Q7–Q11 minimums imply a level different from the certified LCA level; OR the level changed between registration and LCA/petition without a documented basis.
threshold: SOC identical (or defensibly mapped) across all three; the I-129-requirements-implied level (DOL 4-factor mapping) must equal the certified LCA level. n/a single numeric.
deadline: Pre-filing (registration → LCA → I-129; reconcile before filing).
severityPenalty: Substantive + integrity: cross-document mismatch is a leading RFE/denial driver and, if knowingly understated, an LCA misrepresentation exposure (INA 212(n)/214(c); 20 CFR 655 Subpart I + debarment). Registration-stage misrepresentation can trigger 8 CFR 214.2(h)(10)(iii) revocation.
citation: 20 CFR 655.731 (required wage = greater of actual or prevailing); 8 CFR 214.2(h)(4)(iii)(A)/(E); DOL ETA PW Guidance (Nov-2009) level methodology.
dataNeeded: registration.socCode; registration.wageLevelProxy (if captured); lca.socCode; lca.wageLevel; lca.prevailingWage; lca.actualWage; hSupp.q7..q11; i129.socCode.
implementationNote: Deterministic cross-field equality + the 4-factor-implied-level recomputation (reuse the education/experience/skills/supervisory rules to derive an expected level from Q7–Q11, then compare to lca.wageLevel). Emit a graded flag (minor SOC mapping vs hard level mismatch). The "is this level-shopping" intent question → NEEDS-COUNSEL; the structural mismatch is mechanical.

check: Wage offered/paid is at least the greater of the prevailing wage (at the certified level) and the actual wage.
requirement: Per 20 CFR 655.731, pay the required wage = greater of (a) the prevailing wage at the certified level, or (b) the actual wage to similarly employed workers with similar experience/qualifications. A higher offered wage can be justified by superior qualifications but must still meet the actual-wage test.
trigger: Offered/paid wage < prevailing wage at the certified level, OR < the employer's actual wage for similarly situated workers.
threshold: offeredWage ≥ max(prevailingWage_at_level, actualWage). Strict numeric.
deadline: For the entire period of authorized employment (attested at LCA filing; ongoing).
severityPenalty: Substantive civil-penalty: wage violations under INA 212(n) / 20 CFR 655 Subpart I → back-wage liability + tiered CMP (substantial/willful escalate + debarment).
citation: 20 CFR 655.731(a) (first LCA requirement — required wage rate); INA 212(n)(1) (8 USC 1182(n)(1)).
dataNeeded: offer.wage; lca.prevailingWage; lca.wageLevel; lca.actualWage (employer pay data for similar workers); lca.areaOfEmployment; lca.socCode.
implementationNote: Deterministic numeric compare once the three wage values are available. Caveat: the "actual wage" requires the employer's internal pay data (often not in the petition) — when actualWage is unavailable, render "unavailable" rather than passing on prevailing-wage alone. Wage-level correctness feeding the prevailing wage is governed by the wage-level consistency rules above.

verify: OK — NC (<50% / de facto control / affiliate proportion)
check: A qualifying corporate relationship (parent/branch/subsidiary/affiliate) exists between the U.S. petitioner and the foreign entity.
requirement: Petitioner and the employing organization must be a "qualifying organization" meeting EXACTLY ONE of parent/branch/subsidiary/affiliate. Parent = "a firm, corporation, or other legal entity which has subsidiaries"; Branch = "an operating division or office of the same organization housed in a different location"; Subsidiary = parent owns, directly or indirectly, (a) >half + controls, (b) half + controls, (c) 50% of a 50-50 JV with equal control/veto, or (d) <half but in fact controls; Affiliate = two subsidiaries of the same parent/individual, two entities owned/controlled by the same group in approximately the same share, or the accounting-firm international-name arrangement.
trigger: Any L-1 petition (individual I-129 or blanket I-129S) filed or in force.
threshold: Subsidiary: >50%+control; or 50%+control; or 50% of a 50-50 JV with equal control/veto; or <50% with de facto control. Affiliate: common ownership/control by the same parent/individual/proportionate group. Exactly ONE qualifying relationship.
deadline: n/a (structural; must exist at filing and be maintained).
severityPenalty: Substantive eligibility defect — not approvable / deniable; revocable under 8 CFR 214.2(l)(9)(iii)(A)(1) if approved on a false statement; INA 212(a)(6)(C)(i) if misrepresented. No statutory fine — denial/revocation/loss of status.
citation: 8 CFR 214.2(l)(1)(ii)(G) (qualifying organization); (I) Parent; (J) Branch; (K) Subsidiary; (L) Affiliate; INA 101(a)(15)(L) (8 USC 1101(a)(15)(L)).
dataNeeded: petitioner_entity_id; foreign_entity_id; relationship_type; ownership_percent; control_evidence_flag (stock ledger / operating agreement / board minutes / audited financials / tax returns); joint_venture_flag; veto_power_flag; common_parent_or_individual_owner_id.
implementationNote: Deterministic for the numeric ownership prongs (>50/50/JV). The "<half but in fact controls" subsidiary prong and the affiliate "approximately the same share" prong → NEEDS-COUNSEL when ownership is <50% or control is asserted via agreement. Evidence types per USCIS PM Vol 2 Part L Ch 5 (Ownership and Control). Edge: sole proprietorships and the international accounting-firm name arrangement have special treatment.

check: The qualifying relationship is MAINTAINED, and the petitioner continues doing business in the U.S. AND at least one other country, throughout the entire L stay.
requirement: The qualifying organization must be "doing business as an employer in the United States and in at least one other country directly or through a parent, branch, affiliate, or subsidiary for the duration of the alien's stay." DOS: "The qualifying relationship must be maintained, and the employer must be doing business in both countries throughout the period of the L visa status." Ceasing to be a qualifying organization → revocation on notice.
trigger: L-1 status in effect; re-test at extension, amendment, audit, M&A event, or site visit.
threshold: "Doing business" = regular, systematic, and continuous provision of goods/services (NOT mere presence of an agent/office) in ≥2 countries, continuously.
deadline: Continuous — for the entire duration of stay.
severityPenalty: Substantive — automatic/notice revocation ground under 8 CFR 214.2(l)(9)(iii)(A)(1); beneficiary falls out of status.
citation: 8 CFR 214.2(l)(1)(ii)(G)(2) (doing business in 2 countries for duration); (l)(1)(ii)(H) (doing business definition); (l)(9)(iii)(A)(1) (revocation); DOS 9 FAM 402.12.
dataNeeded: us_doing_business_flag; foreign_doing_business_flag; foreign_entity_active_status; relationship_still_valid_flag; last_verified_date; corporate_change_events (merger|acquisition|dissolution|sale) with dates; revenue_or_activity_evidence_per_entity.
implementationNote: Deterministic as a state check IF the system ingests corporate-status + doing-business signals (foreign entity dissolved? US entity stopped operating? ownership change broke the chain?). M&A fact patterns (does the new structure still satisfy a qualifying relationship?) → NEEDS-COUNSEL on any restructuring event. "Doing business" excludes a shell/agent-only presence; a dormant foreign parent breaks eligibility.

check: Beneficiary has ≥1 continuous year of full-time employment abroad with a qualifying organization within the 3 years immediately preceding the petition (or admission).
requirement: An intracompany transferee is one who, "within three years preceding the time of his or her application for admission … has been employed abroad continuously for one year" by a qualifying organization. Individual-petition evidence must show ≥1 continuous year of full-time employment abroad within the 3 years preceding filing, in a managerial/executive/specialized-knowledge position.
trigger: Any initial L-1 petition (the qualifying year is an initial-classification requirement, not re-tested at extension).
threshold: 1 continuous year (12 months) of FULL-TIME employment, accrued WITHIN the 3-year window immediately preceding filing/admission. Reference = petition filing date (USCIS PM).
deadline: 3-year lookback measured backward from filing/admission. Time in the U.S. for the same employer and brief U.S. business/pleasure trips do NOT interrupt the year but are NOT counted toward it (they toll/extend the lookback).
severityPenalty: Substantive eligibility — not approvable if unmet; revocable if approved on misstated dates; INA 212(a)(6)(C)(i) if fabricated.
citation: 8 CFR 214.2(l)(1)(ii)(A) (intracompany transferee / continuous year / tolling); (l)(3)(iii); (l)(3)(iv); USCIS PM Vol 2 Part L Ch 2.
dataNeeded: foreign_employment_start_date; end_date; employment_full_time_flag; petition_filing_date; beneficiary_us_presence_periods (same employer); us_business_pleasure_trip_days; foreign_role_capacity (managerial|executive|specialized_knowledge).
implementationNote: Deterministic: continuous_months = full-time months with a qualifying org; verify ≥12 continuous AND those 12 fall within (filing − 3 years, filing). CRITICAL edge (USCIS PM Ch 2): days the beneficiary spent in the U.S. (e.g., prior H/B status) are SUBTRACTED and extend the 3-year lookback day-for-day; B-1/B-2 trips toll the foreign year. Part-time foreign employment does NOT count. Flag for review if foreign employment overlaps U.S. presence.

check: (L-1A) The U.S. position is in a bona fide MANAGERIAL capacity per all four elements.
requirement: Managerial capacity (8 CFR 214.2(l)(1)(ii)(B)) = an assignment in which the employee primarily: (1) manages the org/department/subdivision/function/component; (2) supervises and controls the work of other supervisory/professional/managerial employees, OR manages an essential function; (3) has authority to hire/fire or recommend personnel actions if another employee is directly supervised, or functions at a senior level (function/personnel manager); and (4) exercises discretion over day-to-day operations. A first-line supervisor is NOT managerial merely by supervising unless the supervised employees are professional.
trigger: Petition (or extension) requests L-1A on a managerial theory.
threshold: "Primarily" on all four prongs. First-line supervisor of non-professionals = NOT managerial. Function manager allowed only if managing an essential function at a senior level.
deadline: n/a (tested at each adjudication; re-tested at extension and for new-office second-year).
severityPenalty: Substantive — deniable/revocable if the role is really line/operational; common RFE/denial. Misclassification to obtain the benefit → INA 212(a)(6)(C)(i).
citation: 8 CFR 214.2(l)(1)(ii)(B); INA 101(a)(44)(A) (8 USC 1101(a)(44)(A)); USCIS PM Vol 2 Part L Ch 3.
dataNeeded: requested_classification (L-1A); job_title; job_duties_text; org_chart; direct_reports_count; direct_reports_are_professional_flag; hire_fire_authority_flag; essential_function_managed; seniority_level; percent_time_on_managerial_duties.
implementationNote: NEEDS-COUNSEL for the ultimate sufficiency determination (totality-of-the-circumstances). Deterministic risk signals: zero direct reports + no "essential function" claim; non-professional reports + first-line; small org with no subordinate managerial layer; duties dominated by hands-on/operational tasks. Capture whether the function-manager or personnel-manager theory is claimed. INA 101(a)(44)(C): take org size into account but staffing alone is not dispositive.

check: (L-1A) The U.S. position is in a bona fide EXECUTIVE capacity per all four elements.
requirement: Executive capacity (8 CFR 214.2(l)(1)(ii)(C)) = an assignment in which the employee primarily: (1) directs the management of the org or a major component/function; (2) establishes goals and policies; (3) exercises wide latitude in discretionary decision-making; and (4) receives only general supervision/direction from higher-level executives, the board, or stockholders.
trigger: Petition (or extension) requests L-1A on an executive theory.
threshold: "Primarily" on all four prongs (direct management at a major-component level; set goals/policies; wide discretion; only general supervision from board/top execs).
deadline: n/a (tested at each adjudication).
severityPenalty: Substantive — deniable/revocable if operational rather than executive. Same misrepresentation exposure.
citation: 8 CFR 214.2(l)(1)(ii)(C); INA 101(a)(44)(B) (8 USC 1101(a)(44)(B)); USCIS PM Vol 2 Part L Ch 3.
dataNeeded: requested_classification (L-1A); job_title; job_duties_text; org_chart; reports_to (board|stockholders|higher_exec); major_component_or_function_directed; policy_setting_authority_flag; discretionary_authority_scope.
implementationNote: NEEDS-COUNSEL for the final determination. Deterministic risk flags: reports to a mid-level manager (not board/top exec); no major component/function identified; duties show day-to-day execution rather than policy/goal-setting; very small entity with no subordinate management to "direct." Executive and managerial are alternative L-1A theories — record which is asserted; do not require both.

check: (L-1B) The beneficiary possesses, and the role requires, specialized knowledge per regulation and statute.
requirement: Specialized knowledge (8 CFR 214.2(l)(1)(ii)(D)) = "special knowledge possessed by an individual of the petitioning organization's product, service, research, equipment, techniques, management, or other interests and its application in international markets, OR an advanced level of knowledge or expertise in the organization's processes and procedures." Statute (INA 214(c)(2)(B)): "special knowledge of the company product and its application in international markets" OR "an advanced level of knowledge of processes and procedures." A "specialized knowledge professional" ((l)(1)(ii)(E)) must also be a professional per INA 101(a)(32).
trigger: Petition (or extension) requests L-1B.
threshold: Either "special" (product/service + international-market application) OR "advanced" (org processes/procedures) knowledge. Sufficiency by preponderance of the evidence on the totality of factors (USCIS PM Vol 2 Part L Ch 4).
deadline: n/a (tested at each adjudication; max stay 5 years).
severityPenalty: Substantive — historically high RFE/denial; deniable/revocable if knowledge is ordinary/commonly held. INA 212(a)(6)(C)(i) if misrepresented.
citation: 8 CFR 214.2(l)(1)(ii)(D); (l)(1)(ii)(E); INA 214(c)(2)(B) (8 USC 1184(c)(2)(B)); USCIS PM Vol 2 Part L Ch 4.
dataNeeded: requested_classification (L-1B); knowledge_type (special_product_knowledge|advanced_process_knowledge); description_of_knowledge; how_acquired; time_to_train_replacement; uniqueness_within_company; is_professional_flag; international_market_application_flag.
implementationNote: NEEDS-COUNSEL for sufficiency (explicitly a preponderance/totality judgment per USCIS PM Vol 2 Part L Ch 4: knowledge not generally found in the industry; gained through significant prior experience/training; difficult/time-consuming to impart). Capture the asserted theory; flag weak signals (knowledge readily available; short ramp-up; generic skills). Do NOT auto-approve/deny.

check: (L-1B only) If the beneficiary will be stationed PRIMARILY at an unaffiliated employer's worksite, the statutory third-party-placement ineligibility bar does NOT apply.
requirement: INA 214(c)(2)(F): an L-1B beneficiary stationed primarily at the worksite of an employer other than the petitioner (or its affiliate/subsidiary/parent) is INELIGIBLE if either (i) "controlled and supervised principally by such unaffiliated employer"; OR (ii) the placement is "essentially an arrangement to provide labor for hire … rather than a placement in connection with the provision of a product or service for which specialized knowledge specific to the petitioning employer is necessary." To avoid the bar, show BOTH: (1) control/supervision stays principally with the petitioner, AND (2) placement is for a product/service requiring the petitioner's specialized knowledge (not labor-for-hire).
trigger: L-1B beneficiary's primary worksite is at an unaffiliated (third-party/client) location.
threshold: "Primarily" stationed at the third-party site triggers the test. "Principally" controlled/supervised by the unaffiliated employer = bar applies. Both safe-harbor prongs must be satisfied.
deadline: n/a (eligibility condition; applies for any period at a third-party site).
severityPenalty: Substantive — statutory ineligibility; not approvable / revocable. Primary L-1B "staffing/labor-for-hire" red line; an enforcement priority.
citation: INA 214(c)(2)(F)(i)-(ii) (8 USC 1184(c)(2)(F)); USCIS PM Vol 2 Part L Ch 4 (off-site placement); DOS 9 FAM 402.12.
dataNeeded: primary_worksite_is_third_party_flag; unaffiliated_client_entity; who_controls_supervises (petitioner|client|both); product_or_service_provided; specialized_knowledge_specific_to_petitioner_flag; labor_for_hire_indicator; itinerary_of_worksites.
implementationNote: Deterministic GATE: if primary_worksite_is_third_party_flag, the rule FIRES and both prongs must be affirmatively evidenced. The two prongs themselves → NEEDS-COUNSEL. Per USCIS PM Ch 4, a petitioner primarily providing a specialized service that sends SK personnel to client sites can avoid the bar IF control/supervision remains principally with the petitioner. **L-1B ONLY** (not L-1A).

check: New-office L-1 petitions (U.S. entity doing business <1 year) meet the heightened evidentiary requirements and are approved for ≤1 year.
requirement: "New office" = doing business in the U.S. through a qualifying org for <1 year (8 CFR 214.2(l)(1)(ii)(F)). For a manager/exec opening a new office ((l)(3)(v)): (A) sufficient physical premises secured; (B) the beneficiary had 1 continuous year (in the preceding 3) in an exec/managerial capacity AND the proposed employment involves exec/managerial authority over the new operation; and (C) within one year the U.S. operation will support an exec/managerial position. For SK new office ((l)(3)(vi)): (A) secured premises; (B) is/will be a qualifying organization; (C) financial ability to remunerate and commence doing business. Per (l)(7)(i)(A)(3), a new-office petition "may be approved for a period not to exceed one year."
trigger: Petition indicates the beneficiary is opening/employed in a new office (U.S. entity in existence/doing business <1 year).
threshold: U.S. doing-business < 1 year = new office. Initial validity ≤1 year (vs ≤3 for established offices).
deadline: Initial approval ≤1 year; within the first year the office must begin doing business to qualify for extension.
severityPenalty: Substantive — deniable if heightened evidence absent; extension fails if not operational. Scrutinized for shell/non-viable operations.
citation: 8 CFR 214.2(l)(1)(ii)(F); (l)(3)(v); (l)(3)(vi); (l)(7)(i)(A)(3); USCIS PM Vol 2 Part L Ch 2.
dataNeeded: new_office_flag; us_entity_doing_business_start_date; physical_premises_secured_flag + lease_evidence; business_plan_flag (scope/org/financial_goals); us_investment_amount; foreign_entity_financial_ability_evidence; requested_validity_period; beneficiary_capacity.
implementationNote: Deterministic: new_office_flag derivable (us_entity_doing_business_duration < 12 months). Hard checks: requested/approved validity ≤1 year; premises-secured evidence present; (mgr/exec) a credible plan that the role becomes managerial/executive within 1 year. Adequacy of the business plan / "will support" → NEEDS-COUNSEL. New-office L-1A first-year role need not yet be fully managerial but must have managerial authority over the new operation.

check: An L-1 new-office extension is supported by evidence the office is actually doing business and (L-1A) now supports a managerial/executive position.
requirement: Per (l)(7)(i)(A)(3) + (l)(14)(ii): demonstrate it is doing business; evidence (A) entities still qualifying; (B) U.S. entity has been doing business for the previous year; (C) statement of the beneficiary's prior-year and extended duties; (D) staffing of the new operation (number of employees, position types, wages paid) where employed in a managerial/executive capacity; (E) financial status of the U.S. operation.
trigger: Extension filed for a beneficiary originally approved under a new-office petition.
threshold: U.S. entity must have been "doing business" for the previous year; staffing/financials support the claimed capacity.
deadline: Filed before the 1-year new-office validity expires (extension only if the original validity has not expired, (l)(14)(i)).
severityPenalty: Substantive — deniable if the office never became a going concern; beneficiary loses status on denial/expiry.
dataNeeded: original_new_office_flag; current_doing_business_evidence (12 months); employee_count; positions_held; payroll_evidence; financial_statements; prior_year_duties; extended_duties; relationship_still_qualifying_flag; original_validity_expiry_date; extension_filing_date.
implementationNote: Deterministic checks: extension_filing_date < original_validity_expiry_date; doing-business evidence for the trailing 12 months; for L-1A, staffing exists to support a managerial/executive role (an office with no subordinate staff after year one = strong adverse signal). Whether the staffing genuinely supports the capacity → NEEDS-COUNSEL.

check: (L-1A) Total stay in managerial/executive capacity ≤7 years.
requirement: Statute (INA 214(c)(2)(D)(i)): total authorized admission "shall not exceed 7 years." Reg (8 CFR 214.2(l)(12)(i)): one who has spent 7 years in a managerial/executive capacity may not be readmitted under (L) unless resided and physically present outside the U.S. for the immediate prior year. (l)(15)(ii): extensions in ≤2-year increments; total ≤7 years; no further extensions.
trigger: L-1A extension requested or cumulative L-1A time approaching 7 years.
threshold: 7 years cumulative L-1A. ≤2-year increments. Recapture: time physically outside the U.S. does not count; a full year abroad resets eligibility.
deadline: Hard cap at 7 years; after the cap, readmission requires 1 continuous year abroad (subject to the exceptions rule).
severityPenalty: Substantive — extension beyond 7 years not approvable; further stay is unlawful presence.
citation: INA 214(c)(2)(D)(i) (8 USC 1184(c)(2)(D)); 8 CFR 214.2(l)(12)(i); (l)(15)(ii); USCIS PM Vol 2 Part L Ch 9 / Part M Ch 9.
dataNeeded: classification (L-1A); cumulative_us_l_days_or_years; admission_history; periods_physically_outside_us; days_in_other_status_H_or_L; current_validity_end; requested_extension_period; recapture_claim_days.
implementationNote: Deterministic: sum authorized L (and H) time; flag if cumulative ≥7 years or a requested extension would cross 7. L and H time are aggregated for the cap under (l)(12); recapture days require physical-presence-abroad evidence. Per (l)(15)(ii), an L-1B promoted to L-1A must have been in the managerial/executive role ≥6 months to be eligible for the full 7-year period. Reset requires 1 continuous year abroad.

check: (L-1B) Total stay in specialized-knowledge capacity ≤5 years.
requirement: Statute (INA 214(c)(2)(D)(ii)): total "shall not exceed 5 years." Reg (8 CFR 214.2(l)(12)(i)): one who has spent 5 years in a SK capacity may not be readmitted under (L) unless physically present outside the U.S. for the immediate prior year. (l)(15)(ii): ≤2-year increments; total ≤5 years.
trigger: L-1B extension requested or cumulative L-1B time approaching 5 years.
threshold: 5 years cumulative L-1B. ≤2-year increments. Time physically outside the U.S. is recapturable; 1 full year abroad resets eligibility.
deadline: Hard cap at 5 years; readmission thereafter requires 1 continuous year abroad (subject to the exceptions rule).
severityPenalty: Substantive — extension beyond 5 years not approvable; further stay is unlawful presence.
citation: INA 214(c)(2)(D)(ii) (8 USC 1184(c)(2)(D)); 8 CFR 214.2(l)(12)(i); (l)(15)(ii); USCIS PM Vol 2 Part L Ch 9.
dataNeeded: classification (L-1B); cumulative_us_l_days_or_years; admission_history; periods_physically_outside_us; days_in_other_status_H_or_L; current_validity_end; requested_extension_period; recapture_claim_days.
implementationNote: Deterministic: sum authorized L/H time; flag if cumulative ≥5 years or a requested extension would cross 5. Same L+H aggregation and recapture mechanics as L-1A. A beneficiary reaching 5 years as L-1B can move to L-1A only with a new/amended petition AND ≥6 months in the managerial/executive role to reach the 7-year ceiling. Reset requires 1 continuous year abroad.

check: Recapture / commuter / intermittent exceptions to the 5- and 7-year caps are correctly applied.
requirement: 8 CFR 214.2(l)(12)(ii): the max-stay limitations do NOT apply to aliens who do not reside continually in the U.S. and whose U.S. employment is "seasonal, intermittent, or consists of an aggregate of six months or less per year," nor to those who reside abroad and regularly commute to the U.S. for part-time employment. Must provide CLEAR AND CONVINCING proof (arrival/departure records, tax returns, foreign-employment records).
trigger: A beneficiary whose cumulative time would otherwise exceed the cap claims a seasonal/intermittent/≤6-months or commuter exception.
threshold: U.S. employment seasonal OR intermittent OR ≤6 months aggregate/year, no continual U.S. residence; OR resident-abroad regular commuter in part-time employment. Standard = clear and convincing.
deadline: n/a (status condition supporting continued eligibility past the nominal cap).
severityPenalty: Substantive — a wrongly claimed exception masking full-time continuous employment = misrepresentation/overstay risk; a correctly proven exception lawfully avoids the cap.
dataNeeded: exception_claimed_flag; us_employment_pattern (seasonal|intermittent|aggregate_days_per_year|commuter); us_residence_continual_flag; days_in_us_per_year; tax_returns; arrival_departure_records; foreign_residence_evidence.
implementationNote: Deterministic threshold: aggregate U.S. days/year ≤ ~183 AND not continually resident → may qualify under the 6-months-or-less prong. Whether a pattern is genuinely seasonal/intermittent or meets clear-and-convincing → NEEDS-COUNSEL. Require documentary proof (I-94 travel, tax returns) before honoring the exception.

check: Individual (non-new-office) L-1 petition validity ≤3 years and matches the period of established need.
requirement: 8 CFR 214.2(l)(7)(i)(A)(2): "An individual petition … shall be valid for the period of established need …, not to exceed three years, except where the beneficiary is coming to … open or to be employed in a new office." (New-office initial ≤1 year per (l)(7)(i)(A)(3).)
trigger: Approval/extension of an individual L-1 petition for an established office.
threshold: ≤3 years per increment (established); ≤1 year for new office. Extensions ((l)(15)(ii)) ≤2-year increments, within the 5/7-year ceilings.
deadline: Validity on the I-797; admission may not exceed validity.
severityPenalty: Technical/operational if merely a validity computation; substantive if used beyond validity (status violation).
dataNeeded: petition_type (individual|blanket); new_office_flag; established_need_period; approved_validity_start; approved_validity_end; extension_increment.
implementationNote: Deterministic: assert approved_validity_duration ≤3 years (established) or ≤1 year (new office), each extension increment ≤2 years, cumulative ≤5/7. Flag any petition whose validity exceeds these. The "need" period is set by the petitioner but capped by the reg.

check: A blanket L petition meets all four blanket-eligibility thresholds.
requirement: 8 CFR 214.2(l)(4)(i): file a blanket only if (A) petitioner and each listed entity are engaged in commercial trade or services; (B) the petitioner has a U.S. office doing business for ≥1 year; (C) ≥3 domestic and foreign branches/subsidiaries/affiliates; AND (D) either ≥10 "L" managers/execs/SK-professionals approved in the previous 12 months, OR U.S. subsidiaries/affiliates with combined annual sales ≥$25 million, OR a U.S. workforce ≥1,000 employees.
trigger: An employer files/maintains a blanket L petition.
threshold: U.S. office ≥1 year; ≥3 entities; AND (≥10 L approvals in prior 12 months OR ≥$25,000,000 combined U.S. annual sales OR ≥1,000 U.S. employees).
deadline: Blanket initial validity 3 years ((l)(7)(i)(B)(2)), extendible indefinitely if compliant.
severityPenalty: Substantive — failure = blanket not approvable; if it lapses/denied, the org must use individual petitions for three years before re-seeking a blanket ((l)(14)(iii)(B)).
dataNeeded: blanket_flag; commercial_trade_or_services_flag_all_entities; us_office_doing_business_years; count_branches_subs_affiliates; count_L_approvals_prior_12mo; combined_us_annual_sales; us_employee_count.
implementationNote: Fully deterministic gate: (us_office_years ≥ 1) AND (entity_count ≥ 3) AND (L_approvals_12mo ≥ 10 OR sales ≥ 25e6 OR us_employees ≥ 1000). All four prongs (A,B,C,D) must hold; prong D is an OR of three alternatives. The $25M/1,000/10 figures are exact regulatory numbers.

check: Each beneficiary entering under an approved blanket uses a properly completed Form I-129S and the consular/admission documents are valid and within time limits.
requirement: 8 CFR 214.2(l)(5): complete Form I-129S (original + three copies), attach a copy of the approved I-797, retain one copy, send the original + two copies to the alien; the employee "may use these documents to apply for visa issuance … within six months of the date on Form I-129S." The consular/Service officer determines mgr/exec/SK-professional. The I-129S is stamped for ≤3 years. Eligibility under a blanket is limited to managers, executives, and SK PROFESSIONALS (the professional requirement of (l)(1)(ii)(E) applies to blanket SK).
trigger: A beneficiary seeks admission/visa under an approved blanket.
threshold: I-129S used within 6 months of the date on the form; blanket admission/validity ≤3 years; SK beneficiaries under a blanket must be professionals (degree-level).
deadline: 6 months from the I-129S date to apply for the visa; admission ≤ validity.
severityPenalty: Substantive — wrong form/expired I-129S window or a non-professional SK beneficiary = ineligible for blanket entry; individual petition required instead.
dataNeeded: blanket_flag; i129s_present_flag; i129s_date; visa_application_date; i797_blanket_copy_flag; beneficiary_capacity (mgr|exec|SK_professional); is_professional_flag (degree per INA 101(a)(32)); admission_validity_end.
implementationNote: Deterministic: (visa_application_date − i129s_date) ≤ 6 months; admission/validity ≤3 years; for SK under a blanket, is_professional_flag must be true (baccalaureate-or-higher). A non-professional SK worker CANNOT use the blanket — file an individual petition. Reassignment among listed entities for virtually the same duties is allowed without a new filing ((l)(5)(ii)(G)); different duties require a new Certificate of Eligibility.

check: The beneficiary's admission / I-94 period does not exceed the petition (or blanket) validity, and status is maintained within it.
requirement: 8 CFR 214.2(l)(11): apply for admission only while the petition is valid; an individual-petition beneficiary "shall not be admitted for a date past the validity period"; a blanket beneficiary may be admitted for 3 years even if the blanket's initial validity expires sooner. Admission "shall not exceed three years unless an extension … is granted." Under 8 CFR 214.1(l)(1), admitted for validity + up to 10 days before/after, but may not work except during validity.
trigger: Admission, extension, or any maintenance-of-status check against the I-94.
threshold: Admission/I-94 end ≤ petition validity end (individual) or ≤3 years (blanket). +10/−10 day grace bracket (no work in those days). Single admission generally ≤3 years.
deadline: Status ends at I-94 expiry; extensions must be timely filed (before expiry).
severityPenalty: Substantive — working/remaining beyond the I-94/validity is unlawful presence + unauthorized employment; affects future admissibility.
citation: 8 CFR 214.2(l)(11); 8 CFR 214.1(l)(1)-(2) (period of stay / 10-day brackets / 60-day grace on cessation); (l)(7)(i)(A)(2).
dataNeeded: i94_admit_until_date; petition_validity_end; blanket_flag; current_date; work_start_date; work_end_date; grace_period_flag; cessation_of_employment_date.
implementationNote: Deterministic: assert i94_admit_until ≤ petition_validity_end (individual). Flag any beneficiary past i94_admit_until without a timely-filed extension. Track the 10-day pre/post brackets (no work) and the up-to-60-day grace on cessation (8 CFR 214.1(l)(2)). Blanket beneficiaries can get a full 3-year admission even if the blanket expires sooner.

check: An amended L-1 petition is filed on a material change in the approved relationship, employment capacity, or other eligibility fact.
requirement: 8 CFR 214.2(l)(7)(i)(C): file an amended petition (with fee) at the office where the original was filed "to reflect changes in approved relationships, additional qualifying organizations under a blanket petition, change in capacity of employment (i.e., from a specialized knowledge position to a managerial position), or any information which would affect the beneficiary's eligibility under section 101(a)(15)(L)."
trigger: A change in: corporate/qualifying relationships; the set of qualifying orgs under a blanket; the beneficiary's capacity (L-1B SK → L-1A managerial); or any eligibility fact.
threshold: Materiality = any change affecting the approved relationship, capacity, or eligibility under INA 101(a)(15)(L). (A work-location change performing the same duties for the same employer is generally NOT, by itself, material — but fact-dependent.)
deadline: When the material change occurs / before the changed employment begins (no fixed numeric clock; unlike H-1B Simeio).
severityPenalty: Substantive — failure on a material change can render the beneficiary out of status + the petition revocable (l)(9). Operational/technical for non-material changes.
citation: 8 CFR 214.2(l)(7)(i)(C); (l)(9)(iii)(A) (revocation grounds); USCIS PM Vol 2 Part L.
dataNeeded: change_event_type (relationship|blanket_entity|capacity|worksite|duties|salary|other); change_date; amended_petition_filed_flag; amended_petition_filed_date; new_capacity; new_worksite; duties_changed_flag.
implementationNote: Deterministic for the enumerated triggers: change_event_type ∈ (relationship, blanket_entity_added, capacity_change) → amended_petition_filed_flag MUST be true. The "any information affecting eligibility" catch-all and WORKSITE changes → NEEDS-COUNSEL (AAO has held an amendment is not required in every worksite move for the same employer/same duties). Unlike H-1B (Simeio), no bright-line worksite-amendment rule for L — assess materiality case-by-case.

check: No automatic- or notice-revocation ground under 8 CFR 214.2(l)(9) is present; petitioner met its notify-of-changes duty.
requirement: 8 CFR 214.2(l)(9): immediately notify USCIS of changes affecting eligibility. (ii) Automatic revocation on withdrawal or (blanket) failure to request indefinite validity. (iii) Revocation on notice if: (1) entities no longer qualifying; (2) alien no longer eligible under 101(a)(15)(L); (3) a qualifying organization violated requirements; (4) statement of facts not true and correct; (5) approval involved gross error; or (6) no qualifying org used the blanket for three consecutive years.
trigger: Any change in employment terms, corporate structure, or eligibility; petition withdrawal; blanket non-use.
threshold: Any (l)(9)(iii) ground = revocable on notice; withdrawal / failure to request indefinite blanket validity = automatic; blanket unused 3 consecutive years = revocable.
deadline: Notification "immediate"; blanket 3-consecutive-years-non-use is the bright-line for that ground.
severityPenalty: Substantive — revocation terminates status; a false statement-of-facts (ground 4) overlaps INA 212(a)(6)(C)(i) + 18 USC 1001.
dataNeeded: entity_still_qualifying_flag; beneficiary_still_eligible_flag; petition_facts_true_flag; petition_withdrawn_flag; blanket_indefinite_validity_requested_flag; blanket_years_since_last_use; employment_terms_change_flag; change_notified_flag.
implementationNote: Deterministic state-machine: raise revocation-risk if entity_still_qualifying_flag false (ground 1), beneficiary_still_eligible_flag false (ground 2), petition_withdrawn (auto), or blanket_years_since_last_use ≥ 3 (ground 6). Grounds 3-5 ("violated requirements," "not true and correct," "gross error") → NEEDS-COUNSEL. The "immediately notify" duty is auditable: pair any detected change with change_notified_flag.

check: Extension of stay (and concurrent petition extension) filed before the current authorized stay expires, increments within caps.
requirement: 8 CFR 214.2(l)(15)(i): for individual petitions, apply for the petition extension and the alien's EOS concurrently on Form I-129. For a blanket beneficiary, file a new Certificate of Eligibility + a copy of the prior approved certificate; the dates must be the same for petition and EOS. The beneficiary must be physically present in the U.S. at filing. (l)(14)(i): an individual extension may be filed only if the original validity has not expired. (l)(15)(ii): EOS in ≤2-year increments, ≤5/7 years.
trigger: Continued L employment beyond the current petition/I-94 validity.
threshold: File before original validity expires; beneficiary physically present at filing; increments ≤2 years; cumulative ≤5/7 years.
deadline: Before the original petition's validity expires (a late extension cannot be filed on an expired petition).
severityPenalty: Substantive — untimely filing leaves a status gap (unauthorized stay/work); may also lose the ability to extend in the U.S.
dataNeeded: original_petition_validity_end; extension_filing_date; beneficiary_physically_present_us_flag; requested_increment; cumulative_l_time; classification (L-1A|L-1B).
implementationNote: Deterministic: assert extension_filing_date ≤ original_petition_validity_end AND beneficiary_physically_present_us_flag AND requested_increment ≤2 years AND projected_cumulative ≤5/7 (per classification). Flag any extension filed after the underlying petition expired or breaching the cap. USCIS makes a SEPARATE determination on the petition and the EOS even when combined on one I-129.

check: L-1 dual intent is respected (pending PERM/I-140/I-485 is not a denial basis); L-2 dependents properly classified and (spouse) work-authorized.
requirement: 8 CFR 214.2(l)(16): an alien may legitimately come as L-1 and simultaneously lawfully seek permanent residence; the filing of a PERM, immigrant visa preference petition, or AOS "shall not be the basis for denying" an L-1 petition/extension/admission or related COS. (l)(7)(ii): the spouse and unmarried minor children get L-2 for the same period/limits; per INA 214(c)(2)(E) the L-2 spouse is authorized to work (incident to status).
trigger: L-1 beneficiary has a pending/approved immigrant process; or L-2 dependents accompany/follow.
threshold: Dual intent permitted (no denial solely on immigrant intent). L-2 spouse work-authorized; L-2 children may NOT work. Dependents' stay tied to the principal's period/limits.
deadline: n/a (status condition).
severityPenalty: Operational/technical — an L-1 wrongly denied for immigrant intent = adjudication error; an L-2 child or non-spouse working without authorization = unauthorized employment.
citation: 8 CFR 214.2(l)(16) (dual intent); (l)(7)(ii) (spouse/dependents); INA 214(c)(2)(E) (8 USC 1184(c)(2)(E)) (L-2 spouse employment); 8 CFR 274a.12(a) (L-2 spouse employment incident to status).
dataNeeded: pending_perm_or_i140_or_i485_flag; dependent_records (relationship: spouse|child); dependent_status (L-2); l2_spouse_employment_flag; child_age; child_marital_status; dependent_admit_until_date.
implementationNote: Deterministic: L-2 child working = violation flag (children not work-authorized); L-2 spouse employment authorized incident to status (no separate EAD required since the 2021/2022 USCIS update, though many carry an I-94 annotation). Assert dependent_admit_until aligns with the principal's. Surface any L-1 RFE/denial premised on a pending green-card process as an error to escalate.

check: No fraud or willful material misrepresentation in the L petition / supporting evidence (statement of facts true and correct).
requirement: 8 CFR 214.2(l)(9)(iii)(A)(4) makes a petition revocable where the statement of facts "was not true and correct." INA 212(a)(6)(C)(i): an alien who by fraud or willfully misrepresenting a material fact seeks/procures a visa/admission/benefit is inadmissible. Material if, had the truth been known, the alien would not have been eligible. Submitting false-information evidence is a covered affirmative act.
trigger: Any L petition/extension/admission supported by inaccurate, fabricated, or misleading facts/documents.
threshold: Willful (knowing) misrepresentation of a MATERIAL (outcome-determinative) fact = inadmissibility; any untrue statement of facts = revocation ground.
deadline: n/a (applies whenever the benefit is sought).
severityPenalty: HIGHEST — INA 212(a)(6)(C)(i) is a PERMANENT inadmissibility bar (waiver-limited); revocation under (l)(9); potential 18 USC 1001 / 1546 criminal liability.
dataNeeded: petition_facts_verified_flag; supporting_doc_authenticity_flags; discrepancy_log (claimed vs actual: dates, duties, org structure, premises, payroll); site_visit_findings; prior_petition_disclosure_flag.
implementationNote: NEEDS-COUNSEL for any "fraud/willful misrepresentation" finding — willfulness and materiality are legal determinations for adjudicators/counsel, NOT an automated label. The evaluator surfaces DISCREPANCIES deterministically (claimed managerial role vs payroll showing no subordinates; claimed secured premises vs virtual office; inconsistent foreign-employment dates; undisclosed prior petitions, which (l)(2)(i) warns may itself cause denial) and routes to counsel. Do not auto-adjudicate intent.

check: F-1 student performs OPT/STEM-OPT work only within the validity dates of an approved EAD (Form I-766) of the correct class.
requirement: May not work before the approved start date or after the end date on the I-766. Pre-completion OPT under (c)(3)(i)(A); post-completion under (c)(3)(i)(B); STEM extension under (c)(3)(i)(C). Work outside the EAD window (or before approval) is unauthorized.
trigger: Student in OPT or STEM OPT and is (or claims to be) working.
threshold: Work only between "Card Valid From" and "Card Expires" (inclusive). Start no earlier than the approved start; OPT start may not be >60 days after the program end date (8 CFR 214.2(f)(11)(i)(D)).
deadline: Per-EAD validity window; 60-day cap on requested OPT start after program end.
severityPenalty: Substantive status violation — unauthorized employment; SEVIS termination, loss of status, unlawful-presence accrual. No monetary penalty.
dataNeeded: EAD class (c3A/c3B/c3C), EAD valid-from, valid-to, actual employment start, program end date, employment periods with dates.
implementationNote: Deterministic: assert every employment interval ⊆ [eadValidFrom, eadValidTo] and employmentStart ≥ eadStart. Flag if requested OPT start > programEndDate + 60 days. Model cap-gap and the 8 CFR 274a.13(d)/274a.12(b)(6)(iv) automatic EAD extension (pending timely STEM/H-1B filings) as additional permitted windows — don't false-positive on an expired card while a timely extension is pending. The 180-day auto-extension on a timely-filed STEM I-765 is judgment-adjacent (timely filing + DSO recommendation) → flag edge cases.

check: All OPT employment is directly related to the student's major area of study (post-completion) / qualifying STEM degree (STEM extension).
requirement: Employment must be directly related to the major area of study; for STEM, directly related to the qualifying STEM degree. The student/DSO/employer documentation must support the relationship.
trigger: Student engaged in any OPT or STEM OPT employment.
threshold: Qualitative "directly related" — no numeric threshold. STEM training must relate to the specific qualifying STEM degree, not any prior degree.
deadline: Continuous throughout the OPT/STEM-OPT period.
severityPenalty: Substantive status violation if not in the field — treated as not maintaining OPT terms; SEVIS termination risk. No fine.
citation: 8 CFR 214.2(f)(10) (intro, "directly related to their major area of study"); 8 CFR 214.2(f)(10)(ii)(C)(4) (STEM "directly related to the degree").
dataNeeded: Student major/CIP, qualifying degree (STEM), job title, duties/description, employer SOC/industry. For STEM: the I-983 Section-5 "how training relates to the STEM degree" narrative.
implementationNote: NEEDS-COUNSEL — "directly related" is interpretive; heuristically score (CIP-to-SOC plausibility, keyword overlap) and surface low-confidence matches for human/DSO review, but do NOT auto-adjudicate. For STEM, deterministically check that a non-empty Section-5 narrative exists; substantive sufficiency is counsel/DSO territory.

check: Student on post-completion OPT (without STEM extension) has not accrued >90 days of unemployment.
requirement: During post-completion OPT, F-1 status depends on employment; may not accrue >90 days aggregate unemployment during a post-completion OPT period under (c)(3)(i)(B). The counter starts the day after the EAD start.
trigger: Student in a post-completion OPT period (c3B) not engaged in qualifying employment.
threshold: 90 days aggregate unemployment (hard cap).
deadline: Counted cumulatively across the entire initial post-completion OPT period; counter begins the day after the EAD start.
severityPenalty: Substantive status violation on exceeding 90 days — SEVIS auto-flags; F-1 termination. No monetary penalty.
dataNeeded: OPT EAD start, end, employment start/end dates + hours/week per employer, qualifying unpaid/volunteer periods, approved travel.
implementationNote: Deterministic counter: sum of calendar days within the post-completion window with NO qualifying employment, starting the day after EAD start. Qualifying employment ≥20 hrs/wk; <20 hrs counts toward unemployment per SEVP — flag <20-hr cases. Volunteer-as-employment / not-in-field interact with `opt.employment.related_to_field` — chain. Days outside the US on approved travel still count as unemployment unless employed remotely. Surface at 60/75/90-day thresholds.

check: STEM extension based on a qualifying STEM-designated degree (bachelor's/master's/doctoral) from an accredited SEVP-certified U.S. institution, in a category on the current STEM Designated Degree Program List.
requirement: The basis degree must be a bachelor's/master's/doctoral from an accredited, SEVP-certified U.S. institution, in a field on the current STEM Designated Degree Program List (DHS-determined). May use a previously obtained STEM degree only if conferred within the 10 years preceding the DSO recommendation and the employer is E-Verify-enrolled. ≤2 lifetime STEM extensions.
trigger: Student applies for / is in a 24-month STEM extension.
threshold: Degree CIP on the current list; previously-obtained STEM degree ≤10 years old; lifetime max = 2; first extension = 24 months for the first qualifying degree.
deadline: Eligibility at DSO recommendation / I-765 filing; previously-obtained 10-year lookback from the DSO recommendation date.
severityPenalty: Eligibility gate — an extension on a non-qualifying degree is voidable; working on an improperly granted STEM EAD = unauthorized employment (substantive). No fine.
citation: 8 CFR 214.2(f)(10)(ii)(C)(1) (accreditation), (C)(2) (DHS-approved degree / list / 24-month / 2-lifetime), (C)(3) (previously obtained STEM degree, 10-year).
dataNeeded: Degree level, CIP, conferral date, institution SEVP-certification + accreditation, current STEM Designated Degree Program List (versioned), count of prior STEM extensions, basis (current or previously-obtained).
implementationNote: Deterministic against a version-pinned, regularly refreshed STEM Designated Degree Program List (treat as canonical reference data): CIP ∈ list; level ∈ {bachelor, master, doctoral}; if previously-obtained, conferralDate ≥ (dsoRecommendationDate − 10 years); priorStemExtensions < 2. DOEd CIP taxonomy + "related field" determinations have judgment edges → flag novel/ambiguous CIPs NEEDS-COUNSEL.

check: The STEM OPT employer is enrolled in and in good standing with E-Verify, with a valid E-Verify company ID (or client company ID via designated agent) and an EIN.
requirement: May not authorize STEM OPT unless the employer is enrolled in E-Verify (valid E-Verify Company ID or, if using an employer agent, a valid E-Verify Client Company ID) AND remains a participant in good standing, AND has an EIN.
trigger: Student on (or applying for) the 24-month STEM extension with a given employer.
threshold: Binary: valid E-Verify Company ID (or client company ID) AND good standing AND EIN. Enrollment active for the duration of the STEM OPT employment.
deadline: Required at I-983/DSO recommendation and continuously.
severityPenalty: Substantive — STEM OPT with a non-E-Verify employer is unauthorized; status violation / SEVIS termination. Misrepresenting E-Verify status on the I-983 = false-statement liability.
dataNeeded: Employer E-Verify Company ID (or client company ID), enrollment status/good-standing flag, EIN, designated-agent use, STEM OPT employment start/end.
implementationNote: Deterministic field-presence + format check (valid E-Verify ID present, EIN present). "Good standing as determined by USCIS" is not machine-verifiable from student-side data — treat a valid ID as the proxy and flag good standing as an attestation to re-verify on complaint/site visit. Optionally cross-check the employer name against public E-Verify participant data.

check: An individualized, fully completed and signed Form I-983 is on file before the DSO recommends the extension, customized to the student.
requirement: Before the DSO recommends, the student fully completes an individualized I-983 with signatures from an employer official with signatory authority. Section 5 must (i) identify training goals (knowledge/skills/techniques + how achieved through work-based learning); (ii) describe a performance-evaluation process; (iii) describe oversight/supervision; and explain how training is directly related to the qualifying STEM degree. Must be customized for the individual student.
trigger: Student applies for the 24-month extension / is employed under STEM OPT.
threshold: I-983 present, signed by student AND an employer Official with Signatory Authority; Sections 1-6 completed; non-empty narrative for goals, evaluation process, oversight/supervision, and STEM-relationship.
deadline: Completed and signed BEFORE the DSO recommends the extension in SEVIS.
severityPenalty: Substantive — STEM OPT cannot be validly authorized without a complete I-983; material false statements = federal false-statement exposure for the signatory.
dataNeeded: I-983 on-file flag; student signature + date; employer Official-with-Signatory-Authority signature + date; Sections 1-6 completeness; non-empty training-plan fields; employer EIN + E-Verify ID on the form.
implementationNote: Deterministic completeness/signature check on structured I-983 fields. SUBSTANTIVE adequacy of the training plan (bona fide objectives vs ordinary labor) → NEEDS-COUNSEL for generic/boilerplate plans or where duties read as staffing. Cross-check that the I-983 employer matches the E-Verify-enrolled employer (links to everify_enrolled and bona_fide_employer).

check: STEM OPT duties, hours, and compensation commensurate with similarly situated U.S. workers; ≥20 hours/week.
requirement: Terms (duties, hours, compensation) must be commensurate with the employer's similarly situated U.S. workers in the area. If the employer has not recently employed >2 similarly situated U.S. workers, it must still attest the terms are commensurate.
