May not work <20 hours/week (excluding leave consistent with the employer's policies). Disclose compensation (incl. adjustments) on the I-983.
trigger: Student employed under the 24-month STEM extension.
threshold: ≥20 hours/week (hard minimum). Compensation/duties/hours "commensurate" with similarly situated U.S. workers (comparative, no fixed wage floor).
deadline: Continuous; compensation changes reflected via amended I-983 (see material_change.report_10day).
severityPenalty: Substantive — dropping below 20 hrs/wk or non-commensurate terms = material deviation / defective attestation; SEVIS termination risk + employer-attestation liability. No CMP schedule.
dataNeeded: Hours/week, compensation amount/structure, employer's comparable U.S.-worker wage data (or attestation), area wage benchmark, count of similarly situated U.S. workers, compensation reductions over time.
implementationNote: Deterministic on the 20-hours/week floor (hoursPerWeek ≥ 20). "Commensurate with similarly situated U.S. workers" → NEEDS-COUNSEL; compare disclosed compensation against an external benchmark (BLS OEWS by SOC + area) only as a heuristic flag. A compensation reduction not tied to an hours reduction is an explicit material-change trigger — wire to material_change.report_10day.

check: The employer's I-983 attestations are present and truthful: sufficient resources/personnel to train; will not replace a U.S. worker; the opportunity assists training goals.
requirement: The student may participate only where the employer attests (by signing the I-983) that: (i) it has sufficient resources/personnel and is prepared to provide appropriate training at the identified location(s); (ii) the student will not replace a full/part-time, temporary/permanent U.S. worker; and (iii) the opportunity assists the student in reaching their training goals.
trigger: Student employed under the 24-month STEM extension.
threshold: All three attestations (i)-(iii) made and signed; each must be true.
deadline: At I-983 signing and continuously (a later change rendering an attestation inaccurate triggers an amended I-983).
severityPenalty: Substantive + employer fraud exposure — a false attestation (displacing a U.S. worker, no real training capacity) → DHS site visit, SEVP referral, federal false-statement liability; for the student, voids the opportunity. No fixed fine.
dataNeeded: I-983 attestation checkboxes/signature; employer headcount + training personnel at the worksite; recent layoff/RIF/furlough records; training-resources description; worksite location(s).
implementationNote: Deterministic on attestation PRESENCE (all three signed). TRUTHFULNESS → NEEDS-COUNSEL. Stress-test the non-replacement attestation against recent layoff/furlough data for the same SOC/area (red flag if the employer laid off U.S. workers in the same SOC shortly before/after placing the student) — surface as a risk flag, not an auto-violation.

check: Bona fide employer-employee relationship: the I-983 signer is the same entity that employs the student and provides the training; no prohibited third-party/staffing placement where the signer is not the trainer.
requirement: The I-983 signer must be the same entity that employs the student and provides the training; the student must be a bona fide employee (may not provide the attestation on their own behalf). A staffing/temp agency may assist in placement, but only the E-Verify-enrolled employer that actually provides the qualifying training may sign the I-983 — an agency that merely places the student at third-party client sites and does not itself train cannot be the signer. Required training/oversight personnel must be where the training occurs.
trigger: STEM OPT arrangement involving a staffing/temp agency, third-party client worksite, consulting/placement model, sole-proprietor self-employment, or any case where the signer may not be the trainer/employer.
threshold: Qualitative bona-fide standard; key structural test: I-983 signer == employer of record == provider of training, with supervisory personnel at the training site.
deadline: At extension recommendation and continuously.
severityPenalty: Substantive — a non-bona-fide arrangement (agency signs but client trains; student self-attests) = not a valid STEM opportunity; unauthorized employment / SEVIS termination; agency/employer attestation liability. No fine.
citation: 8 CFR 214.2(f)(10)(ii)(C)(7) (I-983 signer must be the employer providing training) with USCIS Policy Manual Vol. 2 Pt. F Ch. 5 (bona fide employer-employee relationship).
dataNeeded: I-983 employer name + EIN vs employer-of-record name + EIN; worksite address vs employer address; staffing/temp agency involved; training/supervision personnel at the worksite; self-employment flag; client-site arrangement flag.
implementationNote: Partially deterministic: assert I-983 signer EIN == employer-of-record EIN; flag if a staffing/temp agency is the signer but training occurs at an unrelated client; flag self-employment (student == attesting employer). Ultimate bona-fides → NEEDS-COUNSEL for consulting/staffing/third-party-client models. High-risk audit area; surface all third-party-placement and self-employment cases for human review.

check: Student submits the 12-month self-evaluation and the concluding (final) evaluation, each signed by student and employer, to the DSO on time.
requirement: The student submits a self-evaluation of progress toward I-983 training goals. All STEM opportunities require an initial evaluation within 12 months of the approved STEM EAD start, and a concluding evaluation. Student and an appropriate employer individual must sign each. The student ensures the DSO receives each within 10 days of the end of the relevant reporting period.
trigger: Student in a 24-month STEM OPT period.
threshold: Two evaluations minimum: (1) initial within 12 months of EAD start; (2) concluding. Each carries both student and employer signatures.
deadline: 12-month eval to DSO within 10 days after the first 12-month reporting period; final eval within 10 days after the conclusion of the STEM opportunity.
severityPenalty: Substantive — failure (esp. the final) violates the I-983 terms and may jeopardize F-1 status; SEVIS termination risk. No monetary penalty.
dataNeeded: STEM EAD start, opportunity end, 12-month-eval submission date, final-eval submission date, student + employer signatures on each, DSO-received timestamps.
implementationNote: Deterministic deadline math: 12-month eval due ≤ eadStart + 12 months + 10 days; final eval due ≤ opportunityEndDate + 10 days. Assert each has BOTH signatures. Model the 12-month reporting period as [eadStart, eadStart+12mo]; due = period end + 10 days. Surface upcoming-due reminders (e.g., 30 days before each deadline).

check: Material changes to the I-983 / training plan reported to the DSO via an amended I-983 at the earliest available opportunity; new employer triggers a new I-983 within 10 days.
requirement: On any material change/deviation from the I-983 plan, student and employer sign a modified I-983 and submit it to the DSO at the earliest available opportunity. Material changes include: any EIN change from corporate restructuring; any compensation reduction not tied to an hours reduction; any significant decrease in hours/week; any decrease below the 20-hour minimum; and anything rendering an employer attestation inaccurate or changing the nature/purpose/oversight/assessment of the training. A NEW employer / NEW opportunity requires a new I-983 to the DSO within 10 days of beginning it + a new DSO recommendation.
trigger: A material change (employer change, EIN change, compensation cut not tied to hours, significant hours change, change to learning objectives/oversight, anything making an attestation inaccurate).
threshold: New employer / new opportunity: new I-983 within 10 days of starting. Other material changes: amended I-983 "at the earliest available opportunity" (no fixed day-count).
deadline: New employer: 10 days from start. Other material changes: earliest available opportunity (pair with the 10-day general change-reporting under (f)(12)(ii)(A)).
severityPenalty: Substantive — operating under a stale/false I-983 = status + attestation violation; SEVIS termination risk. No monetary penalty.
citation: 8 CFR 214.2(f)(10)(ii)(C)(7)(iv) (new employer, 10 days) and (f)(10)(ii)(C)(9)(ii) (material change / modified I-983).
dataNeeded: Change events with dates/types (employer change, EIN change, comp change + whether tied to hours, hours change magnitude, learning-objective/oversight change), new-opportunity start date, amended-I-983 submission date, DSO-received date.
implementationNote: Deterministic for the new-employer case: newI983SubmittedDate ≤ newOpportunityStart + 10 days. For other material changes ("earliest available opportunity," not a fixed deadline): detect a material-change event, require an amended I-983 with submission ≥ event date within a configurable promptness window (flag if none). Whether a given change is "material" (e.g., "significant" hours decrease) → NEEDS-COUNSEL for borderline cases. A comp reduction NOT tied to hours is explicitly material — deterministically flag.

check: Student reports to the DSO any change of legal name, residential/mailing address, employer name/address, and/or loss of employment within 10 days (STEM OPT); general F-1 name/address within 10 days.
requirement: STEM students: within 10 days of the change, report a change of legal name, residential/mailing address, employer name, employer address, and/or loss of employment. General F-1: inform the DSO of any legal name/address change within 10 days; the DSO enters it in SEVIS within 21 days.
trigger: A change in legal name, residential/mailing address, employer name, employer address, or employment status.
threshold: Report within 10 days.
deadline: 10 days from the change (student → DSO). DSO then has 21 days to update SEVIS for name/address ((f)(17)).
severityPenalty: Substantive status-maintenance violation — failure to report within 10 days = failure to maintain F-1 status; SEVIS termination risk. No monetary penalty.
citation: 8 CFR 214.2(f)(12)(ii)(A) (STEM 10-day); 8 CFR 214.2(f)(17) (general name/address, 10 days student / 21 days DSO).
dataNeeded: Change event type (name/address/employer-name/employer-address/loss-of-employment), change date, student-report-to-DSO date, DSO SEVIS-update date.
implementationNote: Deterministic: per change event, assert reportToDsoDate ≤ changeDate + 10 days. Separately (DSO-side) assert sevisUpdateDate ≤ reportDate + 21 days for name/address. (f)(12)(ii)(A) applies specifically to STEM and explicitly includes employer name/address and loss of employment (which general (f)(17) does not) — apply the STEM rule for STEM students.

check: Student on STEM OPT completes the recurring validation report every 6 months, confirming the (f)(12)(ii)(A) information has not changed, within 10 business days of each reporting date.
requirement: Complete a validation report confirming the (f)(12)(ii)(A) info (legal name, residential/mailing address, employer name/address, loss of employment) has not changed, every six months. Starts on the date the 24-month extension begins and ends at the earlier of F-1 status expiration or the extension conclusion. Due to the DSO within 10 business days of each reporting date.
trigger: Student in an active 24-month STEM OPT period; a 6-month milestone arrives.
threshold: Every 6 months (reporting dates at +6, +12, +18, +24 months from start); each due within 10 business days of the reporting date.
deadline: Within 10 business days of each 6-month reporting date.
severityPenalty: Substantive status-maintenance violation — a missed validation report jeopardizes F-1 status; SEVIS termination risk. No monetary penalty.
dataNeeded: STEM OPT start, end, F-1 status expiration, validation-report submission dates, business-day calendar.
implementationNote: Deterministic: generate reporting dates at stemStart + {6,12,18,24} months (bounded by min(statusExpiration, extensionEnd)); each due = reportingDate + 10 business days; assert a report exists on/before each due date. Requires a business-day calendar (exclude weekends + federal holidays). SEPARATE from and additional to the 12-month/final self-evaluations — both run concurrently. Surface upcoming validation windows.

check: The employer reports the student's termination/departure to the DSO within 5 business days when it occurs before the end of the authorized OPT period.
requirement: By signing the I-983, the employer agrees to report a STEM OPT student's termination or departure to the DSO if it is prior to the end of the authorized OPT period, within 5 business days. The employer considers a student departed at the earlier of (a) knowing the student left, or (b) 5 consecutive business days of unexcused non-attendance without consent.
trigger: A STEM OPT student is terminated/resigns/departs before the authorized OPT end (incl. a no-show of 5 consecutive business days without consent).
threshold: Report within 5 business days of the (deemed) termination/departure. "Departure" deemed at the earlier of employer knowledge or 5 consecutive unexcused-absence business days.
deadline: 5 business days from the (deemed) termination/departure date.
severityPenalty: Employer compliance obligation in the I-983 attestation — non-reporting = breach of the signed I-983; contributes to a defective attestation + DHS site-visit/SEVP-referral exposure. For the student, drives unemployment-clock and status consequences. No fixed CMP schedule.
dataNeeded: Termination/resignation/departure date, last-day-worked / last-attendance date, employer-knowledge date, consecutive unexcused-absence business days, employer-report-to-DSO date, business-day calendar, authorized OPT end date.
implementationNote: Deterministic: deemedDepartureDate = min(employerKnowledgeDate, firstDayOf 5-consecutive-unexcused-business-day-absence + 4 business days); assert employerReportDate ≤ deemedDepartureDate + 5 business days, but only if deemedDepartureDate < authorizedOptEndDate. Requires a business-day calendar. The "without consent" qualifier on the 5-day no-show → NEEDS-COUNSEL for ambiguous absence cases. Employer-side data the platform may only have via the employer portal; if absent, surface as an open obligation.

verify: OK — NC (whether a finding is noncompliance)
check: Employer on notice of and prepared for DHS site-visit authority (ability/resources to provide structured training consistent with the I-983), with awareness that visits get 48 hours' notice except when complaint-triggered.
requirement: DHS may conduct a site visit of any STEM OPT employer to ensure it possesses and maintains the ability/resources to provide structured, guided work-based learning consistent with the signed I-983. DHS provides 48 hours' advance notice, except where the visit is triggered by a complaint or other evidence of noncompliance.
trigger: Employer participates in STEM OPT (standing authority).
threshold: 48 hours' advance notice for routine visits; NO advance notice when complaint/noncompliance-triggered.
deadline: n/a (DHS-initiated; not a periodic obligation). The 48-hour notice is DHS's obligation, not the employer's deadline.
severityPenalty: Enforcement mechanism, not a violation per se — a visit finding the employer lacks training ability/resources, or that the I-983 doesn't reflect reality, can lead to SEVP referral, revocation of the opportunity, and false-attestation exposure. No monetary penalty.
dataNeeded: Employer participation flag; current I-983 on file; evidence of training resources/personnel at worksite; worksite address(es); site-visit history/outcomes.
implementationNote: Not a deterministic deadline check — model as a readiness/exposure indicator: assert the employer maintains a current, accurate I-983 + documented training resources at each worksite (links to i983.required_and_complete and employer.attestations). Drives an audit-readiness score, not a date computation. Whether a site-visit finding constitutes noncompliance → NEEDS-COUNSEL.

check: Beneficiary's ACTUAL physical work location matches the worksite on the certified LCA and the approved petition.
requirement: The beneficiary must be working at the worksite stated on the petition and the certified LCA. FDNS verifies work location and physical workspace against the petition; a mismatch is a primary fraud/noncompliance indicator. An out-of-MSA move also independently triggers the amended-petition rule.
trigger: Any active H-1B beneficiary whose recorded actual worksite (or remote/home location) differs from the most recent certified LCA / approved petition; or an empty/unverified worksite field.
threshold: Binary match to the LCA's area of intended employment (same MSA / 20 CFR 655.715). Exact-address for the site the officer will visit; MSA-level for the Simeio amended-petition boundary.
deadline: Continuous (readiness). FDNS visits are UNANNOUNCED — no notice window to cure.
severityPenalty: Substantive. Worksite misrepresentation supports revocation (8 CFR 214.2(h)(11)) + a fraud finding; per 8 CFR 214.2(h)(4)(i)(B)(2), inability to verify may result in denial/revocation for workers at the inspected location(s). No FDNS fine; downstream = revocation, future-petition denial, ICE/USCIS referral.
citation: 8 CFR 214.2(h)(4)(i)(B)(1); USCIS ASVVP program description; LCA worksite basis 20 CFR 655.715 / 655.730(c)(5).
dataNeeded: Per beneficiary: actual current worksite (+ remote-work flag/home address); certified LCA worksite(s) + MSA; approved petition worksite; LCA validity dates; petition receipt/approval; effective date of any worksite change.
implementationNote: Deterministic: normalize both addresses to MSA via a geocode/crosswalk and compare; flag (a) exact-address mismatch for the named site and (b) out-of-MSA moves separately. Edge cases: multi-site/roving roles (compare against the itinerary set), remote/telework (the home address is itself a place of employment requiring an LCA), short-term placement (655.735). NEEDS-COUNSEL: whether a telework/client-site arrangement falls within the LCA's area of intended employment vs requires a new LCA.

check: Beneficiary's ACTUAL paid wage ≥ the wage on the petition/LCA (which must itself be the greater of actual or prevailing wage).
requirement: Actually pay at least the required wage — the greater of the actual wage or the prevailing wage (20 CFR 655.731(a)). FDNS verifies the petition salary against actual pay; underpayment is a core noncompliance finding and independently a DOL WHD violation.
trigger: Any active beneficiary whose actual annualized pay rate < the LCA-attested wage; or missing pay data.
threshold: actualWage ≥ max(actualWageSystemRate, prevailingWage) = the LCA-attested required wage. Compare on the same basis; account for FT/PT and benching.
deadline: Continuous; no announce window.
severityPenalty: Substantive (FDNS) AND DOL-enforceable (20 CFR 655.810: back wages + CMP, tiered; willful → higher + debarment). For FDNS, a wage mismatch supports revocation (h)(11) + fraud referral.
dataNeeded: Per beneficiary: actual pay rate + basis + FT/PT; LCA-attested wage + basis; prevailing-wage determination value/source/level; actual-wage-system rate; payroll evidence; benching/non-productive periods.
implementationNote: Deterministic comparison once normalized to a common basis. Edge cases: benching (must still pay required wage per 655.731(c)(7)), authorized deductions, partial-period proration, bonus/commission inclusion (generally only guaranteed cash counts). NEEDS-COUNSEL: whether a particular deduction/non-cash benefit counts toward the required wage, and whether a benching period is bona fide.

check: Beneficiary's ACTUAL job title, duties, and SOC match the petition and LCA SOC.
requirement: Work actually performed must match the specialty occupation, duties, and SOC described in the approved petition and certified LCA. Materially different duties / a different occupation / a non-specialty role is a substantive noncompliance/fraud indicator and can mean the worker is not maintaining status.
trigger: Any active beneficiary whose actual title/SOC or documented duties differ materially from the petition; or absent actual-duties evidence.
threshold: SOC code match; material consistency of duties (qualitative). A change in SOC, or duties no longer constituting the specialty occupation, is the trip-wire. Distinguish a mere title relabel with identical duties.
deadline: Continuous; no pre-visit cure window.
severityPenalty: Substantive. Materially different duties support revocation ((h)(11)) + a finding the beneficiary failed to maintain status; may require an amended petition. FDNS referral possible. No standalone FDNS penalty.
citation: 8 CFR 214.2(h)(4)(i)(B)(1); specialty-occupation/SOC basis 8 CFR 214.2(h)(4)(ii) and LCA SOC 20 CFR 655.730(c)(4); material-change amended-petition 8 CFR 214.2(h)(2)(i)(E).
dataNeeded: Per beneficiary: actual title + current SOC; actual duties (manager/HR); petition title, SOC, duties; LCA SOC; date/nature of any role change.
implementationNote: SOC-code comparison deterministic; duties comparison semantic — implement as (a) hard SOC-code mismatch flag + (b) a flag when an HR-attested duties summary diverges from petition duties beyond a threshold, for human review. NEEDS-COUNSEL: whether a duties change is "material" (requiring an amended petition / breaking eligibility).

check: Beneficiary's ACTUAL hours / FT-vs-PT status match the petition and LCA.
requirement: Actual hours and FT/PT status must match the petition and LCA. FDNS verifies hours. A worker petitioned FT but working PT (or not working / benched without pay) is a noncompliance indicator and affects the required-wage computation.
trigger: Any active beneficiary whose actual FT/PT or weekly hours differ from the petition/LCA; or recorded as not currently working (benched) while in H-1B status.
threshold: FT/PT match; for PT, the LCA hours range (20 CFR 655.730(c)(5)) must bracket actual hours. Any "not working / benched" state is a flag regardless of pay.
deadline: Continuous.
severityPenalty: Substantive (status maintenance) + interacts with DOL wage liability (benching without required-wage pay violates 655.731(c)(7)). Supports revocation/fraud via FDNS. No standalone FDNS penalty.
citation: 8 CFR 214.2(h)(4)(i)(B)(1); LCA hours basis 20 CFR 655.730(c)(5); benching/required-wage 20 CFR 655.731(c)(7).
dataNeeded: Per beneficiary: actual FT/PT + weekly hours; petition FT/PT; LCA FT/PT + (if PT) hours range; benching/non-productive-time flag + dates.
implementationNote: Deterministic FT/PT and hours-range comparison. Edge: an FT-petitioned worker temporarily on reduced hours may still be compliant if paid the full required wage — pair the hours flag with the wage check before escalating. NEEDS-COUNSEL: whether a reduced-hours period breaks status.

check: A bona fide employer-employee relationship with right-to-control exists between petitioner and beneficiary (critical for third-party/client-site placements).
requirement: The petitioner must be a "United States employer" with a bona fide job offer and the requisite control. Under 8 CFR 214.2(h)(4)(ii), a U.S. employer has a bona fide offer, a legal presence (amenable to service of process), and an IRS tax ID. For third-party placements, FDNS probes who supervises/assigns/controls the day-to-day work; absence of right-to-control (the end-client controls, petitioner is a pass-through) is a core revocation/fraud basis.
trigger: Any beneficiary at a third-party/client worksite, OR any petitioner whose relationship indicators point to the end-client; also any petitioner missing legal-presence/tax-ID attributes.
threshold: Qualitative right-to-control (supervision, assignment, hire/fire/discipline, tools, work-setting indicia). A valid contract/SOW chain from petitioner through intermediaries to the end-client, plus petitioner-retained supervisory control, is the readiness bar.
deadline: Continuous; especially load-bearing at third-party sites (8 CFR 214.2(h)(4)(i)(B)(1) names third-party worksites).
severityPenalty: Substantive and high-risk. Loss of the relationship = independent revocation ground ((h)(11)). A third party's refusal to cooperate can itself cause denial/revocation under (h)(4)(i)(B)(2). No standalone FDNS penalty.
citation: 8 CFR 214.2(h)(4)(ii) (United States employer); 8 CFR 214.2(h)(4)(i)(B)(1) (third-party worksite inspection authority); USCIS PM-602-0157 (Contracts and Itineraries).
dataNeeded: Per beneficiary/placement: placement type (direct vs third-party); end-client + worksite; contract/SOW chain (petitioner→vendor(s)→client) + validity dates; who supervises/assigns; petitioner's legal-presence proof, service-of-process agent, IRS tax ID; itinerary of services.
implementationNote: Deterministic prechecks: (a) petitioner has tax ID + legal presence on file; (b) for third-party placements, an unbroken, in-date contract/SOW chain; (c) a right-to-control attestation (supervisor employed by petitioner). Then surface the qualitative right-to-control determination for review. NEEDS-COUNSEL: the ultimate employer-employee/right-to-control conclusion (post-ITServe/USCIS guidance) — assemble the evidence and flag gaps, don't adjudicate.

check: The petitioning entity physically/operationally exists at the address USCIS has on file.
requirement: FDNS confirms the petitioner's existence — visits HQ/satellites, observes premises, takes photographs, reviews public records, speaks with representatives. A petitioner not actually existing/operating at its stated address (shell/virtual-only) fails verification.
trigger: Every active petitioner: hold current evidence the employer operates at its USCIS-of-record address(es). Flag virtual-office-only addresses, no business records, or no verifiable operations.
threshold: Binary verifiable physical/operational presence at the address(es), corroborated by ≥1 independent existence signal (lease/utility, business license, public-records/VIBE/D&B match, staff on site).
deadline: Continuous.
severityPenalty: Substantive — non-existence/shell findings are among the strongest fraud indicators → revocation + fraud referral; can taint all petitions tied to that location. Inability to verify (no-show/closed premises) triggers (h)(4)(i)(B)(2). No standalone FDNS penalty.
citation: 8 CFR 214.2(h)(4)(i)(B)(1); USCIS ASVVP program description; VIBE program (validation of business existence).
dataNeeded: Petitioner of-record address(es); occupancy evidence (lease/utility/business license); independent business-existence verification (VIBE/D&B/state registry); employee count at site; flag if a registered-agent/virtual office.
implementationNote: Deterministic existence score: (address-type != virtual) AND (≥1 occupancy doc) AND (public-records/VIBE match). Edge cases: remote-first companies, recently relocated HQ (verify the of-record address is current), new offices. NEEDS-COUNSEL only if an apparent non-existence may have an innocent explanation (recent move not yet updated).

check: A complete copy of the approved/filed petition (I-129 + H or L supplement + supporting evidence + I-797) is retrievable on demand at the worksite/HQ.
requirement: Because FDNS verifies "the information and supporting documents submitted with the petition," the employer must produce, during an unannounced visit, the petition package and approval notice the officer's facts will be reconciled against. A readiness/retrievability requirement, not a statutory filing deadline.
trigger: Any active beneficiary for whom the system cannot locate a stored copy of the filed I-129 package + approval notice accessible to the site contact.
threshold: Presence (binary) of: filed I-129 + classification supplement, key supporting evidence, certified LCA (H-1B), and the I-797 — retrievable within minutes at the relevant location.
deadline: On-demand at time of visit (unannounced). Best practice: retained for the full validity period + the LCA/PAF retention horizon.
severityPenalty: Readiness/operational. No direct penalty for not having a copy, but inability to corroborate feeds the (h)(4)(i)(B)(2) "unable to verify" pathway → denial/revocation risk.
citation: 8 CFR 214.2(h)(4)(i)(B)(1); USCIS ASVVP program description.
dataNeeded: Per beneficiary: stored document-set status — filed I-129, H/L supplement, supporting evidence bundle, certified LCA, I-797; document location/owner; last-verified-present date.
implementationNote: Deterministic document-presence checklist per beneficiary; surface missing artifacts. No legal judgment. Tie to a "site packet" the local contact can produce.

check: The DOL H-1B Public Access File is complete and available within one working day at the principal place of business or place of employment (H-1B only).
requirement: Per 20 CFR 655.760, make the certified LCA + supporting documentation available within ONE WORKING DAY of filing. Required PAF: (1) certified LCA + ETA-9035CP; (2) wage-rate documentation; (3) actual-wage-system explanation; (4) prevailing-wage documentation; (5) union/employee notice; (6) benefits summary; plus, for dependent/willful-violator and corporate-change/single-employer situations, items (7)-(10). The document set an FDNS officer (and WHD investigator) will expect even though PAF is a DOL construct.
trigger: Any certified LCA tied to an active beneficiary with an incomplete/unassembled PAF; or any LCA filed >1 working day ago without a complete PAF.
threshold: 1 working day after filing; all required items (4 universal + posting + benefits summary, plus dependent/willful and corporate-change items where applicable).
deadline: Make-available: within 1 working day of filing (655.760(a)). Retention: 1 year beyond the last date any H-1B worker is employed under the LCA (or 1 year from withdrawal/expiry); payroll records 3 years from creation (655.760(c) / 655.731(b)).
severityPenalty: DOL WHD-enforceable. PAF/recordkeeping failures are typically technical/procedural but carry CMP (inflation-adjusted) and, for substantial/willful failures, back wages + possible debarment. For an FDNS visit, an incomplete PAF undercuts wage/notice corroboration.
citation: 20 CFR 655.760(a) (contents + 1-working-day) and 655.760(c) (retention); DOL WHD Fact Sheet 62F; required-wage docs 20 CFR 655.731(b).
dataNeeded: Per LCA: filing date; PAF-items-present checklist (certified LCA+9035CP, wage-rate doc, actual-wage-system explanation, prevailing-wage doc+source, posting/notice proof+dates, benefits summary); H-1B-dependent/willful flag (drives items 7-9); corporate-change/single-employer flag (item 10); PAF location; retention clock.
implementationNote: Deterministic: per certified LCA, compute days-since-filing vs 1-working-day deadline and run the PAF contents checklist; branch to require the extra dependent/willful items only when dependent or a willful violator. Edge cases: working-day calculation (exclude weekends/federal holidays), multiple LCAs per beneficiary, the longer 3-year payroll horizon vs the 1-year-beyond-employment PAF horizon. NEEDS-COUNSEL: H-1B-dependent/exempt-status determination (changes the required PAF contents).

check: When an H-1B worker's worksite changed to a location outside the LCA's MSA, an amended/new H-1B petition was timely filed (Matter of Simeio).
requirement: Per Matter of Simeio Solutions and USCIS PM-602-0120, a change to a geographic area not covered by the existing LCA (outside the MSA / area of intended employment) is a material change requiring an amended/new H-1B petition with a corresponding certified LCA BEFORE the worker begins at the new location. 8 CFR 214.2(h)(2)(i)(E)(2) codifies this. Same-MSA moves don't require amendment (but do require posting).
trigger: Any active beneficiary with a worksite-change to a location outside the petition's existing LCA MSA, and no amended/new petition recorded as filed on/before the start of work there.
threshold: Boundary = LCA area of intended employment (MSA / normal commuting distance). Filing before the worker starts at the new out-of-area site. Short-term-placement (≤30, or 60, workdays/year under 20 CFR 655.735) and non-worksite (conferences) exceptions may apply.
deadline: Amended/new petition filed on/before the date the beneficiary begins work at the new (out-of-MSA) worksite. (Worker may begin upon filing — portability — not upon approval.)
severityPenalty: Substantive. Failure to file → worker out of status / petition no longer supports the worksite → revocation + status problems; surfaces in an FDNS worksite reconciliation. No standalone FDNS penalty; risk is denial/revocation + status break.
citation: 8 CFR 214.2(h)(2)(i)(E)(2); USCIS PM-602-0120 (Matter of Simeio Solutions); short-term placement 20 CFR 655.735.
dataNeeded: Per beneficiary: worksite-change events + dates; new worksite + MSA; existing LCA's area of intended employment/MSA; whether an amended/new petition + new certified LCA were filed + the filing date; short-term-placement day counts per worksite/year.
implementationNote: Deterministic core: detect out-of-MSA moves (geo/MSA crosswalk) and compare new-site start date vs amended-petition filing date; alert if start precedes filing. Edge cases: same-MSA moves (no amendment, but posting), short-term-placement day-count tracking (655.735), non-worksite locations. NEEDS-COUNSEL: whether a placement qualifies for the short-term-placement or non-worksite exception.

check: For H-1B services in multiple/changing locations, an itinerary of services with dates and locations was filed and matches where the beneficiary actually works.
requirement: 8 CFR 214.2(h)(2)(i)(B) requires an itinerary with the dates and locations of services for a worker performing services in more than one location. FDNS uses the itinerary as the petition-stated baseline for roving/third-party placements; actual worksites/dates must reconcile to it (and each must be LCA-covered).
trigger: Any H-1B beneficiary working at >1 location or rotating among client sites, where no itinerary is on file or actual locations/dates diverge from the filed itinerary.
threshold: Presence of an itinerary covering all locations + reconciliation of actual worksites/dates to it; each itinerary location maps to a certified LCA / area of intended employment.
deadline: Itinerary required at filing; actual placements conform on a continuing basis.
severityPenalty: Substantive/procedural — a missing/contradicted itinerary undermines worksite verification at third-party sites + supports revocation; interacts with the amended-petition rule when actual sites fall outside filed/LCA-covered areas. No standalone FDNS penalty.
citation: 8 CFR 214.2(h)(2)(i)(B); USCIS PM-602-0157 (Contracts and Itineraries Requirements for H-1B Petitions).
dataNeeded: Per beneficiary (multi-site/third-party only): filed itinerary (locations + dates); actual worksite history (locations + dates); mapping of each location to a certified LCA; placement/contract validity dates.
implementationNote: Deterministic set-reconciliation: every actual worksite/date should be covered by an itinerary entry AND an in-date LCA; flag uncovered placements. NEEDS-COUNSEL: adequacy/specificity of the itinerary under PM-602-0157 (post-rescission landscape) — flag thin itineraries rather than auto-failing.

check: (L-1) Both the U.S. entity and the qualifying foreign entity are actually "doing business" for the duration of the beneficiary's stay.
requirement: For L-1, the qualifying organization must be doing business as an employer in the U.S. and in ≥1 other country for the duration of the stay. 8 CFR 214.2(l)(1)(ii)(H) defines "doing business" as "the regular, systematic, and continuous provision of goods and/or services"; the "mere presence of an agent or office" does not qualify. FDNS (expanding ASVVP to L-1) verifies existence + ongoing operations on both sides.
trigger: Any active L-1 beneficiary where evidence of ongoing US-entity operations and continued foreign-entity operations is missing/stale; or a "new office" L-1 past its first year without evidence of a staffed, operating office.
threshold: Evidence of regular/systematic/continuous operations (not a mere office/agent) for BOTH entities, for the full L-1 validity. New-office L-1: by end of year one, the office must support the exec/managerial or SK role.
deadline: Continuous, for the duration of stay; new-office milestone at one year.
severityPenalty: Substantive (L-1). Failure of "doing business"/qualifying-relationship is a revocation ground; FDNS L-1 site visits verify exactly this. Refusal to cooperate carries the same adverse-adjudication exposure. No standalone FDNS penalty.
citation: 8 CFR 214.2(l)(1)(ii)(H) (doing business); 8 CFR 214.2(l)(1)(ii)(G) (qualifying organization); USCIS ASVVP-for-L1 expansion announcement.
dataNeeded: Per L-1 beneficiary: US-entity operations evidence (payroll, revenue, premises, staff); foreign-entity continued-operations evidence; qualifying-relationship docs; new-office flag + first-year operational-milestone evidence; L-1A vs L-1B and the managerial/SK basis.
implementationNote: Deterministic prechecks: both entities have current operations evidence + qualifying-relationship docs on file; new-office cases get a one-year operational-milestone check. NEEDS-COUNSEL: whether activity rises to "regular, systematic, and continuous" (vs mere presence), and whether the relationship is intact after restructuring — assemble evidence and flag, don't adjudicate.

check: A site-visit response protocol exists so the employer can verify the officer, permit/decline cooperation knowingly, reach counsel, and avoid an "unable-to-verify" outcome.
requirement: FDNS makes UNANNOUNCED visits, may photograph, may interview the beneficiary and officials, and may issue administrative subpoenas. FDNS officers are NOT law enforcement and NOT adjudicators; they terminate the visit if someone expresses unwillingness and document that. Because refusal/inability to cooperate can cause denial/revocation under 8 CFR 214.2(h)(4)(i)(B)(2), readiness = site contacts can identify/log the officer, route to a designated responder, and reach counsel — while understanding that non-cooperation has adjudicative consequences. (No regulatory right to delay for counsel, but individuals may decline to be interviewed.)
trigger: Operational readiness per worksite: a named responder, an officer-verification/log procedure, a counsel-contact path? Flag worksites (esp. third-party) with no protocol.
threshold: Presence (binary) of a documented protocol covering: officer ID verification + logging, designated responder, scope of cooperation (records vs interviews), counsel-notification, post-visit documentation.
deadline: Standing/continuous readiness; the visit is unannounced.
severityPenalty: Operational/readiness. Mishandling can convert a routine visit into an "unable to verify" record → denial/revocation under (h)(4)(i)(B)(2). FDNS assesses no civil penalty; obstruction or misrepresentation during the visit can escalate to fraud + ICE referral.
citation: 8 CFR 214.2(h)(4)(i)(B)(2) (consequence of failure/refusal); USCIS ASVVP program description + FDNS brochure.
dataNeeded: Per worksite (incl. third-party): named responder + contact; officer-verification/log procedure flag; counsel contact; whether staff are briefed; record of prior visits + outcomes.
implementationNote: Deterministic readiness checklist per worksite; track third-party sites separately (the petitioner cannot control client-site front desks). NEEDS-COUNSEL: how far to cooperate in any specific visit (which records to produce, whether to permit interviews, responding to a subpoena) — surface the protocol + counsel contact; never script a cooperation/refusal decision.

check: Any post-visit adverse action (RFE / NOIR / NOID) arising from an FDNS report is tracked and answered within its statutory response window.
requirement: After the visit, FDNS writes a report and refers fraud/noncompliance indicators to USCIS adjudicators (FDNS does not decide the petition). The adjudicator may issue an RFE, NOIR, or NOID. The employer must respond by the notice deadline or the petition is decided on the record / revoked. The one genuinely deadline-driven node in this otherwise readiness-based regime.
trigger: Receipt of any RFE/NOIR/NOID referencing or following an FDNS site visit / compliance review for an H-1B or L-1 petition.
threshold: Respond by the date on the notice. Typical: RFE up to ~84 days (max 12 weeks per notice); NOIR/NOID commonly ~30 days (per the notice; 8 CFR 214.2(h)(11)(iii) / 103.2(b)(8)). Always use the date on the specific notice.
deadline: As stated on the RFE/NOIR/NOID. Missing it = decision on the record / revocation.
severityPenalty: Substantive and outcome-determinative — non-response → denial/revocation (+ downstream loss of status). Revocation under 8 CFR 214.2(h)(11). No civil penalty, but loss of the petition.
citation: USCIS ASVVP/FDNS brochure; RFE/NOID procedure 8 CFR 103.2(b)(8); H-1B revocation/NOIR 8 CFR 214.2(h)(11)(iii).
dataNeeded: Per notice: type (RFE/NOIR/NOID); receipt date; printed response-due date; linked petition/beneficiary; whether tied to an FDNS visit; response-filed date + status.
implementationNote: Deterministic deadline timer keyed off the notice's printed due date (do NOT hardcode the window — parse it from the notice; windows vary). Escalate as the deadline approaches. NEEDS-COUNSEL: the substantive content of any response is legal work — the engine tracks the clock and assembles reconciliation evidence; counsel drafts.

check: The system correctly attributes each inbound government action to the right regime (FDNS/USCIS petition-truth vs ICE I-9 employment-eligibility vs DOL WHD wage/LCA) and applies that regime's distinct rules and clocks.
requirement: Three SEPARATE regimes the product must not conflate: (1) FDNS/USCIS ASVVP/TSVVP = unannounced petition-fact verification, no fixed notice, consequence = denial/revocation (8 CFR 214.2(h)(4)(i)(B)); (2) ICE I-9 inspection = served NOI with ≥3 business days to produce I-9s (8 CFR 274a.2(b)(2)(ii)), then ≥10 business days to correct technical failures (INA 274A(b)(6)(B)), consequence = I-9 civil fines/criminal; (3) DOL WHD H-1B investigation = LCA/wage/PAF enforcement, consequence = back wages + CMP + possible debarment (20 CFR 655.805-.810). Route documents, deadlines, and reconciliation logic by regime.
trigger: Any inbound government contact/notice; classify before applying rules. Also a build-time invariant: rules tagged to one regime must not borrow another's deadline.
threshold: Correct 1-of-3 classification. FDNS = unannounced, no production window. I-9/ICE = NOI + 3 business days (+10 business days to cure technical errors). WHD = complaint/directed investigation under 20 CFR 655.805.
deadline: Regime-specific: FDNS none; ICE I-9 = 3 business days from NOI to produce; ICE technical-correction = 10 business days; WHD per its own process.
severityPenalty: Meta/architectural — misclassification is itself a compliance failure (wrong clock/documents/penalty model). Severity inherits from whichever regime is misrouted.
dataNeeded: Per inbound event: issuing agency (USCIS/FDNS vs ICE/HSI vs DOL/WHD); document type (FDNS visit vs NOI vs WHD complaint/subpoena); served-date; any printed production/correction deadline; linked petitions/employees.
implementationNote: Deterministic router keyed on issuing agency + document type → loads that regime's rule set + clock. Encode as an enum guard so a rule tagged FDNS cannot inherit an I-9/WHD deadline. NEEDS-COUNSEL only when an event is genuinely ambiguous (e.g., a coordinated FDNS+ICE action) — flag for legal triage rather than guessing.

check: Form I-9 Section 1 completed by the employee on/before the first day of employment for pay.
requirement: Complete and sign Section 1 no later than the first day of employment ("time of hire" = actual commencement of employment for wages). May be earlier, but only after offer acceptance.
trigger: A new hire begins (or is scheduled to begin) employment for pay; or an existing Section 1 missing/unsigned/undated.
threshold: By end of the first day of employment (day 0); not earlier than offer acceptance.
deadline: First day of employment for pay (hireDate). No grace days.
severityPenalty: Substantive if never completed, unsigned, status box unchecked, or late under the current ICE I-9 Inspection fact sheet. $288–$2,861/individual (2025, through CY2026) under 8 CFR 274a.10(b)(2).
citation: 8 CFR 274a.2(b)(1)(i)(A); penalty 8 CFR 274a.10(b)(2); statutory base 8 USC 1324a(e)(5). *(Field-evaluator view in Regime 1 carries the M-274/274a.1 corrections.)*
dataNeeded: employeeId, hireDate, section1CompletedDate, section1SignedFlag, section1StatusAttestationBox, section1Signature, offerAcceptedDate.
implementationNote: Deterministic: flag if section1CompletedDate IS NULL OR > hireDate OR {signedFlag false, statusBox null}. Rehires within 3 years may reuse a prior I-9 via 274a.2(c) — suppress for rehires electing update-and-reverify. Technical-vs-substantive classification must use the current ICE fact sheet; route genuinely off-table cases to counsel.

check: Section 2 completed within 3 business days of the first day of employment.
requirement: Examine acceptable documentation and complete Section 2 within 3 business days of hire. <3-business-day engagements: at time of hire (day 0).
trigger: A new hire's first day passes; Section 2 not done or done late.
threshold: 3 business days. Day 0 = first day; due by end of the 3rd business day after. Exclude weekends/federal holidays.
deadline: hireDate + 3 business days (or day 0 if <3 business days).
severityPenalty: Substantive if missing/untimely or missing document title/number/expiration or employer attestation/signature. $288–$2,861/individual (2025, through CY2026).
citation: 8 CFR 274a.2(b)(1)(ii); short-engagement exception 8 CFR 274a.2(b)(1)(iii); penalty 8 CFR 274a.10(b)(2).
dataNeeded: employeeId, hireDate, section2CompletedDate, employerBusinessDayCalendar (federal-holiday set), documentTitle, documentNumber, documentExpiration, employerAttestationSignedDate, engagementLengthDays.
implementationNote: Deterministic business-day arithmetic against a federal-holiday calendar (not calendar days). Flag if section2CompletedDate IS NULL OR business-days(hire→s2) > 3, OR engagementLengthDays < 3 AND s2 > hire. Receipt rule: a receipt for a lost/stolen doc is acceptable but the actual document must come within 90 days (no receipts for <3-business-day engagements) — track a separate 90-day clock. Technical-vs-substantive → NEEDS-COUNSEL.

check: Reverification (Supplement B) completed on/before the date the employee's temporary employment authorization (or work-authorizing document) expires.
requirement: When authorization or the document evidencing it has an expiration, reverify no later than that date; the employee presents unexpired evidence. Does NOT apply to LPRs presenting Form I-551 / List B identity docs / U.S. passports.
trigger: A recorded work-auth expiration (or List A/C document expiry evidencing employment auth) approaching/passed with no reverification recorded.
threshold: On/before the work-auth expiration date (day 0). No statutory grace; continued employment past expiry without reverification = knowingly continuing to employ an unauthorized alien.
deadline: workAuthExpirationDate. Recommend a 90-day advance reminder.
severityPenalty: (a) paperwork/substantive ($288–$2,861, 8 CFR 274a.10(b)(2)) and, if the worker is unauthorized, (b) continuing-to-employ: first $716–$5,724, second $5,724–$14,308, third+ $8,586–$28,619 (8 CFR 274a.10(b)(1)(ii), 2025 through CY2026).
citation: 8 CFR 274a.2(b)(1)(vii); continuing-to-employ penalty 8 CFR 274a.10(b)(1)(ii); statutory base 8 USC 1324a(e)(4).
dataNeeded: employeeId, workAuthExpirationDate, documentCategory (List A/B/C; LPR vs EAD vs other), reverificationCompletedDate, newDocumentTitle/Number/Expiration, autoExtensionApplicable.
implementationNote: Deterministic on dates, BUT net out any active auto-extension first: do NOT fire while a 240-day (274a.12(b)(20)) or authority-backed EAD auto-extension (date-gated 274a.13(d), STEM OPT 180-day, TPS/FR notice, etc.) is running — see those rules; otherwise false positive. Suppress for non-reverifiable docs (US passport, LPR I-551, List B). EAD auto-extension category/date eligibility → NEEDS-COUNSEL when ambiguous.

check: Form I-9 retained for the longer of 3 years from hire or 1 year from termination; not destroyed before that date.
requirement: Retain each I-9 for the later of 3 years after hire or 1 year after termination, and produce on request.
trigger: A record reaches/passes its computed purge-eligible date, or an I-9 is destroyed/missing before it, or an audit requests an unproducible I-9.
threshold: Retain until MAX(hireDate + 3y, terminationDate + 1y). Active employees: indefinitely.
deadline: Earliest destruction = MAX(hire+3y, term+1y).
severityPenalty: Failure to retain/produce = substantive (failure to prepare/present): $288–$2,861/individual (2025 through CY2026).
citation: 8 CFR 274a.2(b)(2)(i)(A); statute 8 USC 1324a(b)(3); penalty 8 CFR 274a.10(b)(2).
dataNeeded: employeeId, hireDate, terminationDate (nullable), i9OnFileFlag, i9StorageLocation/format, destructionDate (if purged).
implementationNote: Deterministic: purgeEligibleDate = max(hire+3y, term+1y); flag (a) i9OnFileFlag=false where today < purgeEligibleDate and (b) destructionDate < purgeEligibleDate. Electronic retention must meet 8 CFR 274a.2(e)–(f) integrity/audit-trail standards (separate control). No legal judgment for the date math.

check: Technical/procedural I-9 failures corrected within the ICE-granted period of at least 10 business days after written notice.
requirement: For TECHNICAL/PROCEDURAL failures (not a pattern/practice, acted in good faith), the agency must give written notice and NOT LESS THAN 10 business days to correct; if corrected, deemed compliant. Uncorrected technical failures become substantive after the cure period.
trigger: ICE serves a notice of technical/procedural I-9 deficiencies; a cure clock starts.
threshold: At least 10 business days from the agency's written explanation (may grant more; never less).
deadline: noticeOfTechnicalDeficiencyDate + 10 business days (or longer if specified).
severityPenalty: Within the window: no penalty if cured. After: uncorrected → substantive at $288–$2,861 each. Good-faith compliance is a mitigation factor.
citation: Cure provision = **8 USC 1324a(b)(6)** (INA 274A(b)(6); "not less than 10 business days"); classification table = **ICE I-9 Inspection fact sheet updated 2026-03-16**. *(Original sourced the cure period implicitly to the CFR; it is statutory.)*
dataNeeded: employerId, noticeOfTechnicalDeficiencyDate, listOfFlaggedItems (per-I-9 defects), correctionCompletedDate per item, patternOrPracticeFlag, goodFaithIndicators.
implementationNote: Date arithmetic deterministic (10 business days). Classification — technical/procedural (curable) vs substantive (not curable) — comes from the current ICE fact sheet, with NEEDS-COUNSEL only for genuinely off-table or disputed cases and for whether conduct is "good faith" / not a "pattern or practice." Track the cure clock and surface the classification; do not decide off-table legal questions.

check: I-9s produced to ICE within 3 business days of service of a Notice of Inspection (NOI).
requirement: On service of an NOI, produce Forms I-9 (and requested supporting documents) within 3 business days. ICE then reviews for substantive and technical/procedural violations.
trigger: ICE serves an NOI / administrative subpoena for I-9s.
threshold: 3 business days from service.
deadline: noiServiceDate + 3 business days.
severityPenalty: Failure to produce forecloses the technical-violation cure opportunity + exposes to substantive paperwork penalties ($288–$2,861 each) + adverse inferences; obstruction may aggravate.
citation: 8 CFR 274a.2(b)(2)(ii) (production on request); ICE I-9 Inspection fact sheet.
dataNeeded: employerId, noiServiceDate, productionCompletedDate, i9CountProduced vs activeRosterCount.
implementationNote: Deterministic date check (3 business days). Operational, but the response strategy should involve counsel → NEEDS-COUNSEL for the response strategy, not the clock.

check: Reference rule — current civil-penalty RANGE for I-9 substantive/uncorrected paperwork violations.
requirement: Each substantive paperwork violation or uncorrected technical/procedural failure is penalized within the per-individual range; ICE sets a base then adjusts via five factors (size, good faith, seriousness, unauthorized-alien involvement, prior history).
trigger: ICE assesses penalties after an inspection identifies substantive violations.
threshold: $288 (min) to $2,861 (max) per individual/Form I-9 (statutory base $110–$1,100; un-adjusted statute text $100–$1,000 at 8 USC 1324a(e)(5)).
deadline: n/a (range, not a clock).
severityPenalty: Substantive paperwork tier. $288–$2,861/violation, 2025 amounts effective 2025 AND continuing through CY2026 (FCPIAA deferral to ≤ Jan 14, 2027). Indemnity-bond: $2,861.
citation: 8 CFR 274a.10(b)(2); DHS 2025 inflation adjustment (FR doc 2024-31204, eff. Jan 2, 2025); statutory base 8 USC 1324a(e)(5).
dataNeeded: violationCount, perViolationBaseAmount, fiveFactorInputs (headcount, goodFaithEvidence, seriousnessRating, unauthorizedAlienInvolvedFlag, priorViolationHistory).
implementationNote: RANGE/endpoints are deterministic constants (store $288/$2,861 with effective-year metadata = "2025, continuing through 2026"). The ACTUAL fine within the range = five-factor + ICE/OCAHO discretion → NEEDS-COUNSEL. Re-verify endpoints against eCFR each January (next FCPIAA bump ≤ Jan 14, 2027).

check: Reference rule — current CMP RANGES for knowingly hiring / continuing to employ unauthorized aliens (per individual, by offense tier).
requirement: Knowingly hiring, recruiting/referring for a fee, or continuing to employ an unauthorized alien is penalized per individual, escalating by prior-offense count; five factors adjust. Pattern-or-practice can trigger criminal exposure.
trigger: ICE finds the employer knowingly hired or continued to employ unauthorized aliens.
deadline: n/a (ranges, not a clock).
severityPenalty: Highest I-9 civil tier. 2025 amounts effective 2025 AND continuing through CY2026 (next adjustment ≤ Jan 14, 2027). 8 CFR 274a.10(b)(1)(ii).
citation: 8 CFR 274a.10(b)(1)(ii); DHS 2025 inflation adjustment (FR doc 2024-31204); statutory base 8 USC 1324a(e)(4).
dataNeeded: unauthorizedIndividualCount, employerPriorOffenseTier (0/1/2+ prior final orders), fiveFactorInputs, knowinglyStandardEvidence.
implementationNote: Range endpoints deterministic by offense tier (store with effective-year="2025, continuing through 2026"). Whether the "knowingly" (incl. constructive-knowledge) standard is met, which tier applies, and the in-range amount → NEEDS-COUNSEL. Constructive knowledge (ignoring a no-match or expired EAD) can establish "knowingly" — surface the indicators, don't adjudicate.

check: E-Verify case created no later than the 3rd business day after the employee's first day of employment for pay.
requirement: Create a case by the 3rd business day after start of work for pay. Cannot create before the I-9 is complete; cannot pre-screen before offer acceptance. If E-Verify was unavailable, record the delay reason.
trigger: An E-Verify-enrolled employer hires; case not yet created or created late.
threshold: 3 business days after the first day of work for pay (same counting basis as Section 2).
deadline: firstDayOfWork + 3 business days.
severityPenalty: MOU compliance: late creation requires a documented reason and is a frequent finding; for FAR-clause contractors, a contractual breach. No standalone statutory CMP for E-Verify lateness, but it evidences I-9 non-compliance and can aggravate ICE penalties.
citation: E-Verify MOU (Article II); E-Verify User Manual (M-775) §1.4 / "Create a Case"; statutory basis IIRIRA §403 (Pub. L. 104-208).
dataNeeded: employeeId, firstDayOfWork, everifyCaseCreatedDate, everifyEnrolledFlag, businessDayCalendar, federalContractorFlag, delayReasonCode.
implementationNote: Deterministic business-day arithmetic (3 business days). Only fires for E-Verify-enrolled employers/worksites. A delay because E-Verify itself was down is excused if a reason is logged — capture delayReasonCode and suppress. No legal judgment for the clock.

check: Employer refers a TNC (mismatch) and notifies the employee within 10 federal-government working days of the mismatch result.
requirement: On a TNC, promptly notify the employee, review the Further Action Notice, and — if contested — refer, all within 10 federal-government working days of the mismatch. Must NOT take adverse action (suspend, terminate, delay training/start, reduce pay/hours) while pending.
trigger: E-Verify returns a TNC/mismatch on a created case.
threshold: 10 federal-government working days (Mon–Fri excl. federal holidays) from the mismatch result.
deadline: mismatchResultDate + 10 federal-government working days.
severityPenalty: MOU breach if missed or if adverse action taken while pending; FAR-clause breach for contractors. Adverse action on a pending mismatch → anti-discrimination (IER / 8 USC 1324b) exposure.
citation: E-Verify MOU (Article II); E-Verify User Manual (M-775) §3.3 (TNC), §3.3.3 (Refer to DHS/SSA).
dataNeeded: everifyCaseId, mismatchResultDate, employeeNotifiedDate, furtherActionNoticeAcknowledgedDate, employeeContestDecision, referralDate, adverseActionTakenFlag/Date, federalGovWorkingDayCalendar.
implementationNote: Deterministic on the 10-working-day referral clock. The "no adverse action while pending" rule is a state check (adverseActionDate NULL until final nonconfirmation) — also deterministic. The anti-discrimination overlay (whether conduct is national-origin/citizenship discrimination under 8 USC 1324b) → NEEDS-COUNSEL if adverse action occurred.

check: Employee contacts DHS or visits SSA within 8 federal-government working days of referral (employer-side tracking of the resolution clock).
requirement: After referral, E-Verify issues a Referral Date Confirmation stating the date by which the employee must call DHS or visit an SSA field office — 8 federal-government working days from referral. The employer gives the confirmation to the employee and continues employment without adverse action while pending.
trigger: A contested mismatch case is referred to DHS/SSA.
threshold: 8 federal-government working days from the referral date for the employee to contact DHS/SSA.
deadline: referralDate + 8 federal-government working days (per the Referral Date Confirmation).
severityPenalty: MOU: must provide the confirmation and continue employment without adverse action; failure or premature termination = compliance breach + potential 8 USC 1324b exposure. (The 8-day clock runs against the employee, but the employer is the audited party.)
citation: E-Verify MOU (Article II); E-Verify User Manual (M-775) §3.3.3 (Referral Date Confirmation).
dataNeeded: everifyCaseId, referralDate, referralDateConfirmationProvidedFlag, employeeContactByDate, caseFinalResultDate/Result, adverseActionTakenFlag.
implementationNote: Track as a pending-resolution clock; the employer's deterministic obligations: (a) provided the Referral Date Confirmation, and (b) no adverse action before a Final Nonconfirmation. Do not auto-terminate on day 8 — only a Final Nonconfirmation authorizes (does not require) termination. Whether to terminate on an FNC → NEEDS-COUNSEL.

check: LCA notice posted at each place of employment (or provided to the bargaining rep) and kept up 10 days, within the window on/before filing.
requirement: Before/at filing, give notice to affected workers: notify the bargaining rep, OR post hard-copy in ≥2 conspicuous locations at each place of employment (or electronic notice), on or within 30 days before filing, and keep posted (hard-copy/electronic) for 10 days. Content: H-1B sought; number; occupation; wage; period; location(s); public-inspection availability; DOL-complaint statement.
trigger: An employer files (or is about to file) an LCA for an H-1B/H-1B1/E-3 worksite.
threshold: Posted 10 days; notice on/within 30 days BEFORE filing; two locations per worksite (or electronic), or notice to the bargaining rep.
deadline: Posting begins no earlier than 30 days before filing and runs 10 days; documentation in the PAF.
severityPenalty: Tier-1 CMP up to $2,364 (substantial failure) under 20 CFR 655.810(b)(1); willful up to $9,624 (Tier 2). 2025 through CY2026.
dataNeeded: lcaId, lcaFilingDate, worksiteList, noticeMethod (bargaining-rep vs posting vs electronic), postingStartDate, postingEndDate, postingLocationsCount, postingProofRetainedFlag.
implementationNote: Mostly deterministic: verify postingStartDate within [filing−30d, filing], duration ≥10 days, and (locationsCount ≥2 per worksite OR bargainingRepNotifiedFlag OR electronicNoticeFlag). "10 days" here is calendar days. Third-party/roving worksites and short-term placement (30/60-day rules) → NEEDS-COUNSEL for non-standard placements.

check: Public Access File assembled and available within 1 working day after the LCA is filed.
requirement: Make the PAF (certified LCA, wage rate, actual-wage memo, prevailing-wage source, notice documentation, benefits summary, and other required items) available at the principal place of business or place of employment within one working day of filing.
trigger: An LCA is filed; the PAF must exist within one working day.
threshold: 1 working day after filing.
deadline: lcaFilingDate + 1 working day.
severityPenalty: Tier-1 CMP up to $2,364 (20 CFR 655.810(b)(1)); willful up to $9,624. Retention: 1 year beyond the period of employment (or end of employment). 2025 through CY2026.
citation: 20 CFR 655.760(a) (one working day; contents; location); retention 20 CFR 655.760(c); penalty 20 CFR 655.810(b).
dataNeeded: lcaId, lcaFilingDate, pafCreatedDate, pafContentsChecklist (certified LCA, wage rate, actual-wage system, prevailing-wage source, notice docs, benefits summary), pafLocation, pafRetentionThroughDate.
implementationNote: Deterministic: flag if pafCreatedDate IS NULL OR > lcaFilingDate + 1 working day, OR any required checklist item missing, OR today > pafRetentionThroughDate while still required. Content adequacy (prevailing-wage source / actual-wage memo sufficiency) → NEEDS-COUNSEL, not for existence/timeliness.

check: Certified LCA accompanies the H-1B petition and was filed no earlier than 6 months before the employment start date.
requirement: The LCA must be filed with and certified by DOL, and a copy of the signed certified LCA submitted to USCIS with the I-129 (DOL certification precedes the petition). The LCA may be filed no earlier than 6 months before the start of intended employment.
trigger: An H-1B petition is prepared/filed; check a certified LCA exists and its filing is within 6 months of the start.
threshold: LCA filing date ≥ (employmentStartDate − 6 months); certified LCA exists before/with the I-129.
deadline: LCA filed within [startDate − 6 months, startDate]; certified before the I-129.
severityPenalty: Filing without a certified LCA, or with an LCA filed too early, undermines the petition and can be a misrepresentation/specificity violation. Tier-1 up to $2,364; willful misrepresentation up to $9,624 (20 CFR 655.810(b)(2)). 2025 through CY2026.
citation: 20 CFR 655.730(b) (no earlier than 6 months); 20 CFR 655.730(c)(3) (certified LCA submitted to USCIS with I-129).
dataNeeded: petitionId, lcaId, lcaFilingDate, lcaCertifiedDate, lcaCertificationStatus, employmentStartDate, i129FilingDate.
implementationNote: Deterministic: flag if lcaCertifiedDate IS NULL at i129FilingDate, OR lcaFilingDate < employmentStartDate − 6 months, OR lcaCertifiedDate > i129FilingDate. Cap-subject and amended/extension petitions have their own sequencing, but certified-LCA-before-petition is universal. Material-change scenarios (new worksite outside the LCA's MSA) require a NEW LCA + amended petition before the move (Simeio) → NEEDS-COUNSEL.

check: H-1B worker paid the greater of the actual wage or the prevailing wage (no underpayment below the required wage).
requirement: Pay the required wage — the greater of (1) the actual wage to similarly-qualified workers for the specific employment, or (2) the prevailing wage for the occupation in the area. Cash, free and clear, for the entire authorized-employment period.
trigger: Payroll below the LCA required wage / prevailing wage; or a wage level on the LCA below the OES/prevailing determination.
threshold: actualPay ≥ MAX(actualWageForRole, prevailingWageForArea). Any shortfall per period is a violation; back wages = required − actual.
deadline: Each pay period throughout the authorized employment (continuous).
severityPenalty: Wage violation. Back wages (655.810(a)). CMP up to $2,364 (Tier 1); WILLFUL up to $9,624 (Tier 2); plus debarment (≥1 yr Tier 1, ≥2 yr Tier 2). 2025 through CY2026.
citation: 20 CFR 655.731(a) (greater-of required wage); back wages 20 CFR 655.810(a); penalties 20 CFR 655.810(b); statute 8 USC 1182(n)(1).
dataNeeded: employeeId, lcaRequiredWage, lcaWageLevel, prevailingWageDetermination, actualWageMemoRate, actualGrossPayPerPeriod, hoursPaid, payFrequency, authorizedEmploymentStart/End, deductionsTaken.
implementationNote: Arithmetic (pay ≥ required wage; back-wage delta) deterministic and high-value. Determining the correct "actual wage" (peer comparison) and the correct prevailing wage level (SVP, area, skill level) → NEEDS-COUNSEL for the wage DETERMINATION; the underpayment CHECK against a stated required wage is mechanical. Watch impermissible deductions and the "free and clear" rule.

check: Required-wage obligation begins on time (no late start / illegal benching) — within 30 days of admission or 60 days of work-eligibility, and non-productive time is paid.
requirement: The obligation begins when the worker "enters into employment"; no later than 30 days after first admission, OR 60 days after becoming eligible to work (if already present at approval/COS). Once begun, pay the required wage even for non-productive time ("benching") caused by the employer's decision/lack of work/licensure. Need NOT pay for non-productive time due solely to the worker's voluntary request or inability to work.
trigger: A worker becomes admitted/work-eligible and the employer hasn't begun paying by the 30/60-day mark, or places the worker in unpaid non-productive status for employer-side reasons.
threshold: Wage starts by MIN(entered employment, admission+30) for newly admitted, or by eligibility+60 for those already present. Benching for employer reasons = full-time pay (40 hrs or demonstrated FT) at the required wage.
deadline: admission+30 (newly admitted) OR work-eligibility+60 (already in U.S.).
severityPenalty: Failure-to-pay / benching → back wages (655.810(a)) + Tier-1 up to $2,364, or willful Tier-2 up to $9,624; debarment. 2025 through CY2026.
citation: 20 CFR 655.731(c)(6)(i)-(ii) (30/60-day start); 20 CFR 655.731(c)(7) (non-productive status/benching); statute 8 USC 1182(n)(2)(C)(vii).
dataNeeded: employeeId, admissionDate, workEligibilityDate, firstPaidDate, payStatusByPeriod (productive/non-productive), nonProductiveReason (employer-decision vs employee-request), requiredWage.
implementationNote: Deterministic on the 30/60-day start clock (flag if firstPaidDate exceeds the applicable threshold). Benching: flag any unpaid non-productive period where nonProductiveReason is employer-side. The classification of WHY the worker was non-productive (employer lack-of-work vs bona fide voluntary leave) → NEEDS-COUNSEL.

check: New LCA + amended H-1B petition filed BEFORE an H-1B worker moves to a worksite outside the area(s) of intended employment on the current LCA (material change).
requirement: A material change — most commonly a worksite outside the LCA's MSA(s) — requires a NEW certified LCA for the new worksite and an AMENDED I-129 before the worker begins at the new location (Matter of Simeio Solutions; USCIS policy). Short-term placement and non-worksite exceptions may apply.
trigger: An H-1B worker's worksite changes to a location not covered by the current certified LCA / MSA, or another material change to terms occurs.
threshold: Amended petition + new LCA required before the move when the new worksite is outside the LCA's area of intended employment (subject to short-term-placement and other exceptions).
deadline: Before the worker begins at the new worksite (event-triggered; must precede the change).
severityPenalty: Working at an un-LCA'd worksite = LCA/petition compliance failure + potential status violation; can support misrepresentation findings (Tier-1 up to $2,364; willful up to $9,624) and jeopardize the petition.
citation: Matter of Simeio Solutions, 26 I&N Dec. 542 (AAO 2015); 20 CFR 655.734 / 655.730 (worksite within area of intended employment); USCIS Policy Manual Vol. 2 Pt. H.
dataNeeded: petitionId, currentLcaWorksiteMSAs, currentWorksiteLocation, worksiteChangeDate, newWorksiteMSA, amendedPetitionFiledDate, newLcaId, shortTermPlacementFlag/days.
implementationNote: Partly mechanical (does newWorksiteMSA fall outside currentLcaWorksiteMSAs?), but whether a move is a "material change" requiring an amended petition vs covered by short-term placement (≤30 or ≤60 workdays), non-worksite, or roving-employee exceptions → NEEDS-COUNSEL. Surface MSA mismatches as candidates; do not auto-conclude a violation.

check: Reference rule — current H-1B/LCA CMP tiers + back wages + debarment.
requirement: DOL/WHD enforces LCA obligations with back-wage assessment + tiered CMP + mandatory debarment.
trigger: WHD finds LCA/H-1B violations after investigation.
threshold: Tier 1 (substantial failures, misrepresentation, recruitment/notification/specificity, prohibited employee fees, retaliation): up to $2,364. Tier 2 (willful failures/misrepresentation; discrimination): up to $9,624. Tier 3 (willful + displacement of a U.S. worker within 90 days before/after filing): up to $67,367. Plus back wages = required − actual.
deadline: Debarment: ≥1 year (Tier 1), ≥2 years (Tier 2), ≥3 years (Tier 3).
severityPenalty: Up to $2,364 / $9,624 / $67,367 per violation by tier + back wages + 1/2/3-year debarment. 2025 amounts effective 2025 AND continuing through CY2026 (FCPIAA deferral to ≤ Jan 14, 2027). Confirmed unchanged in the DOL 2026 annual adjustment.
citation: 20 CFR 655.810(b)(1)-(3) (CMP tiers), (a) (back wages), (d) (debarment); statute 8 USC 1182(n)(2)(C). *(§655.810 is in Subpart I — see the corrected URL.)*
dataNeeded: violationTier, violationCount, perViolationAmount, backWageDelta, willfulnessFinding, displacementFinding, debarmentPeriod.
implementationNote: Range endpoints + debarment minimums deterministic constants (store with effective-year="2025, continuing through 2026"; re-verify on eCFR each January). Tier assignment (substantial vs willful vs willful+displacement), willfulness, displacement, and H-1B-dependent/exempt status → NEEDS-COUNSEL. Cross-check $2,364/$9,624/$67,367 against the DOL WHD penalties table and 20 CFR 655.810 at each annual adjustment.

check: Response to a USCIS RFE filed by the deadline on the notice (max 12 weeks / 84 days), +3 days if served by mail.
requirement: Respond by the date on the RFE; the regulatory maximum is 12 weeks (84 days). Non/late response permits summary denial as abandoned, denial on the record, or both.
trigger: USCIS issues an RFE on a pending petition/application (I-129, I-140, I-485).
threshold: By the date on the RFE; regulatory max 12 weeks (84 days) from issuance. +3 days if served by mail (8 CFR 103.8(b)).
deadline: Date on the RFE (≤ issuance + 84 days); +3 days when mailed.
severityPenalty: Procedural — missing the deadline → denial/abandonment (8 CFR 103.2(b)(13)). An abandonment denial cannot be appealed (only a motion to reopen). No CMP; loss of the benefit (+ possible loss of status/work authorization).
citation: 8 CFR 103.2(b)(8)(iv) (12-week max); 8 CFR 103.2(b)(13)(i) (consequences); 8 CFR 103.8(b) (3-day mail rule).
dataNeeded: caseId, rfeIssuanceDate, rfeResponseDueDate (as printed), serviceMethod (mail/electronic), responseFiledDate, responseReceivedConfirmation.
implementationNote: Deterministic: use the printed rfeResponseDueDate as controlling (do NOT compute 84 days — the notice may state less); +3 calendar days if mailed. Flag if responseFiledDate IS NULL approaching the due date, or > due date. Filing must be RECEIVED by USCIS by the deadline (mailbox rule does not apply to benefit filings). Response strategy/substance → NEEDS-COUNSEL.

check: Response to a USCIS NOID filed within 30 days (the regulatory max), +3 days if served by mail.
requirement: Respond by the date on the NOID; the max is 30 days. Non-response permits denial.
trigger: USCIS issues a NOID on a pending case.
threshold: Max 30 days from issuance (date on the notice controls). +3 days if served by mail.
deadline: Date on the NOID (≤ issuance + 30 days); +3 days when mailed.
severityPenalty: Procedural — non/late response → denial. Denial (other than abandonment) may be appealable or subject to a motion. No CMP; loss of benefit + possible status consequences.
citation: 8 CFR 103.2(b)(8)(iv) (30-day max for NOID); 8 CFR 103.8(b) (3-day mail rule).
dataNeeded: caseId, noidIssuanceDate, noidResponseDueDate (as printed), serviceMethod, responseFiledDate.
implementationNote: Deterministic on dates; use printed due date, +3 calendar days if mailed. Flag if response missing/late. NOID rebuttal substance → NEEDS-COUNSEL for strategy; the clock is mechanical.

check: Motion to Reopen or Reconsider (Form I-290B) filed within 30 days of the decision, +3 days if mailed.
requirement: A motion to reopen/reconsider an unfavorable USCIS decision must be filed within 30 days; late filing excused only in USCIS discretion where the delay was reasonable and beyond control. Reopen = new facts + evidence; reconsider = legal/policy error.
trigger: USCIS issues an adverse decision the party wishes to challenge by motion.
threshold: 30 days from the decision; +3 days if mailed (33 days). Discretionary excuse for late filing.
deadline: decisionDate + 30 days (+3 if mailed).
severityPenalty: Procedural — a late motion is generally rejected (subject to the discretionary excuse). No CMP. Missing it can forfeit the challenge.
citation: 8 CFR 103.5(a)(1)(i) (30-day deadline + reasonable-delay excuse); 8 CFR 103.8(b) (3-day mail rule).
dataNeeded: caseId, adverseDecisionDate, serviceMethod, motionFiledDate, motionType (reopen/reconsider), delayJustification (if late).
implementationNote: Deterministic on the 30(+3)-day clock. Whether a late motion qualifies for the "reasonable and beyond control" excuse → NEEDS-COUNSEL. A motion does NOT automatically stay removal/the underlying decision.

check: Appeal to the AAO (Form I-290B) filed within 30 days of service (+3 if mailed); 15 days for certain revocation appeals.
requirement: The complete appeal (incl. any brief per the form instructions) must be filed within 30 days after service. For an appeal of a revocation of petition approval, the period is 15 days. +3 days when served by mail.
trigger: USCIS issues an appealable adverse decision (e.g., I-129/I-140 denial or revocation).
threshold: 30 days from service (general); 15 days for revocation-of-approval appeals; +3 if mailed.
deadline: serviceDate + 30 days (general) or + 15 days (revocation), +3 if mailed.
severityPenalty: Procedural — untimely appeal is rejected (may be treated as a motion if it meets motion requirements). No CMP; forfeits AAO review.
citation: 8 CFR 103.3(a)(2)(i) (30-day appeal); 8 CFR 205.2(d) (15-day revocation-appeal period, where applicable); 8 CFR 103.8(b) (3-day mail rule).
dataNeeded: caseId, decisionType (denial vs revocation), serviceDate, serviceMethod, appealFiledDate.
implementationNote: Deterministic: branch on decisionType for 30 vs 15 days; +3 if mailed. Flag missing/late appeals. Whether a decision is appealable to the AAO vs another body (e.g., BIA for family petitions) → NEEDS-COUNSEL on the correct forum.

check: Premium-processing timeframe met by USCIS (and fee-refund trigger tracked) — generally 15 business days for I-129/I-140 classifications, from receipt of a complete request.
requirement: Where premium processing (Form I-907) is requested for an eligible classification, USCIS must take adjudicative action (approval, denial, RFE/NOID, or open investigation) within the designated timeframe. Most I-129/I-140 = 15 business days; others 30 or 45. The clock starts on receipt of a complete I-907 + fee. If USCIS misses it, it refunds the fee and continues (unless fraud/misrepresentation).
trigger: An I-907 request is filed/received for an eligible petition.
threshold: 15 business days (most I-129/I-140); 30 or 45 for designated others. "Business day" = a day the federal government is open. Clock starts on receipt of the complete I-907 + fee.
deadline: i907ReceiptDate + the per-classification business-day count (15/30/45).
severityPenalty: Not a penalty against the employer — a USCIS service-level clock. Consequence: fee refund + continued processing if missed. Track for refund entitlement + reliance on PP timing.
citation: 8 CFR 106.4(e) (timeframes), 106.4(e)(22) (business-day definition), 106.4(f)(2)(i) (commencement), 106.4(f)(4) (refund if missed); statute 8 USC 1356(u).
dataNeeded: i907RequestId, benefitClassification (drives 15/30/45), i907ReceiptDate, uscisActionDate, actionType (approval/denial/RFE/NOID/investigation), federalBusinessDayCalendar, refundIssuedFlag.
implementationNote: Deterministic business-day arithmetic, but the timeframe DEPENDS on the classification — maintain a lookup mapping each eligible classification to its 15/30/45-business-day timeframe per 8 CFR 106.4(e) (and USCIS PP availability announcements, which expand eligible forms). An RFE/NOID issuance STOPS and RESETS the clock per 106.4(f)(3). "Business days" is NOT calendar days. No legal judgment for the clock; verify the per-form timeframe table against current USCIS notices.

check: Continued employment past I-94 expiry is covered by the 240-day rule only if a timely extension was filed with the same employer (else unauthorized employment).
requirement: If an employer timely files an extension-of-stay petition (same employer, same classification, eligible category: H-1B, L-1, E, O, P, TN, etc.) before the authorized stay expires, the worker is authorized to continue with the same employer for ≤240 days from the expiration, while pending. If denied, work authorization ends immediately on denial. After 240 days with no decision, authorization lapses.
trigger: A worker's I-94 expires while a timely-filed same-employer extension is pending; or 240 days elapse with no decision; or the extension is denied.
threshold: ≤240 days from I-94 expiry, conditioned on a TIMELY-FILED (before expiry) extension with the SAME employer in an eligible class.
deadline: i94ExpiryDate + 240 days (work-auth ceiling while pending), or earlier upon denial.
severityPenalty: If conditions NOT met (untimely, different employer, or 240 days exceeded/denied), continuing to employ = continuing to employ an unauthorized alien: $716–$5,724 (first) per individual (8 CFR 274a.10(b)(1)(ii)) + I-9/status violations. 2025 through CY2026.
